(OP alias) ro-0000053.description: (OP) obo.RO_0000053: Inverse of characteristic_of; former label: bearer_of

(OP alias) aism-0000078.description: (OP) obo.AISM_0000078: x encircles y if both x and y are regions of the 2D structure z, or 2D cross-sections of a 3D object z, and the boundary of y on z is exclusively continuous with x.

(OP alias) aism-0000079.description: (OP) obo.AISM_0000079: y is encircled by x if both x and y are regions of the 2D structure z, or 2D cross-sections of a 3D object z, and the boundary of y on z is exclusively continuous with y.

(C) aism-0000003.description: (C): The region of the insect cuticle that is less flexible than the neighboring conjunctiva(e) (conjunctiva(e) that the sclerite is continuous with.

(C) bfo-0000003.description: (C): An entity that has temporal parts and that happens, unfolds or develops through time.

(C) bfo-0000004.description: (C): A continuant that is a bearer of quality and realizable entity entities, in which other entities inhere and which itself cannot inhere in anything.

(C) bspo-0000010.description: (C): A straight line through space, intersecting an anatomical entity.

(C) bspo-0000054.description: (C): An anatomical region bounded by a plane perpendicular to an axis through the middle.

(C) bspo-0000400.description: (C): A flat 2D plane intersecting an anatomical continuant, dividing it into two adjacent portions.

(C) bspo-0000005.description: (C): A 2D surface of an anatomical continuant.

(C) iao-0000030.description: (C): A generically dependent continuant that is about some thing.

(C) obi-0000011.description: (C): A process that realizes a plan which is the concretization of a plan specification.

(C) bfo-0000020.description: (C): A continuant that inheres in or is borne by other entities. Every instance of A requires some specific instance of B which must always be the same.

(C) bfo-0000002.description: (C): An entity that exists in full at any time in which it exists at all, persists through time while maintaining its identity and has no temporal parts.

(C) bfo-0000040.description: (C): An independent continuant that is spatially extended whose identity is independent of that of other entities and can be maintained through time.

(C) uberon-0000061.description: (C): Material anatomical entity that is a single connected structure with inherent 3D shape generated by coordinated expression of the organism's own genome.

(C) uberon-0000122.description: (C): A fasciculated bundle of neuron projections (GO:0043005), largely or completely lacking synapses.

(C) pato-0002124.description: (C): A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's processing the form of a thin plate sheet or layer.

(C) pato-0001199.description: (C): A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being narrow, with the two opposite margins parallel.

(C) bfo-0000015.description: (C): An occurrent that has temporal proper parts and for some time t, p s-depends_on some material entity at t.

(C) ro-0002577.description: (C): A material entity consisting of multiple components that are causally integrated.

(C) uberon-0001638.description: (C): Any of the tubular branching vessels that carry blood from the capillaries toward the heart.

(C) uberon-0010000.description: (C): An anatomical structure that has more than one cell as a part.

(C) uberon-0001062.description: (C): Biological entity that is either an individual member of a biological species or constitutes the structural organization of an individual member of a biological species.

(C) pato-0000402.description: (C): A branchiness quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having branches.

(C) uberon-0004111.description: (C): Any tube, opening or passage that connects two distinct anatomical spaces.

(C) uberon-0000463.description: (C): Material anatomical entity in a gaseous, liquid, semisolid or solid state; produced by anatomical structures or derived from inhaled and ingested substances that have been modified by anatomical structures as they pass through the body.

(C) aism-0000167.description: (C): The region of cuticle where two sclerites meet.

(C) aism-0000004.description: (C): The region of the insect cuticle that is more flexible than the neighboring sclerite(s) [sclerite(s) that the conjunctiva is continuous with].

(C) aism-0000007.description: (C): The region of cuticle with higher content of resilin.

(C) aism-0000008.description: (C): The region of the cuticle that corresponds to a convex surface.

(C) bspo-0000062.description: (C): Anatomical side that is distally located on an organism or structure.

(C) bspo-0000070.description: (C): A 3D region in space without well-defined compartmental boundaries; for example, the dorsal region of an ectoderm.

(C) uberon-0000955.description: (C): The brain is the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate, and most invertebrate, animals. Some primitive animals such as jellyfish and starfish have a decentralized nervous system without a brain, while sponges lack any nervous system at all. In vertebrates, the brain is located in the head, protected by the skull and close to the primary sensory apparatus of vision, hearing, balance, taste, and smell[WP].

(C) uberon-0001043.description: (C): Tube that connects the pharynx to the stomach. In mammals, the oesophagus connects the buccal cavity with the stomach. The stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium lining the buccal cavity is continued through the pharynx down into the oesophagus. The lowest part of the oesophagus (ca. 2 cm) is lined with gastric mucosa and covered by peritoneum. The main body of the oesophagus is lined with small, simple mucous glands. Each gland opens into the lumen by a long duct which pierces the muscularis mucosae (Wilson and Washington, 1989). A sphincter is situated at the point where the oesophagus enters the stomach to prevent gastro-oesophageal reflux, i.e. to prevent acidic gastric contents from reaching stratified epithelia of the oesophagus, where they can cause inflammation and irritation (Wilson and Washington, 1989; Brown et al., 1993).

(C) uberon-0000059.description: (C): A subdivision of the digestive tract that connects the small intestine to the cloaca or anus. Lacks or has few villi[Kardong].

(C) uberon-0002108.description: (C): Subdivision of digestive tract that connects the stomach to the large intestine and is where much of the digestion and absorption of food takes place (with the exception of ruminants). The mammalian small intestine is long and coiled and can be differentiated histologically into: duodenum, jejunem, ileum[WP,cjm,Kardong].

(C) uberon-0001295.description: (C): The glandular mucous membrane lining of the uterine cavity that is hormonally responsive during the estrous/menstrual cycle and during pregnancy.

(C) uberon-0002337.description: (C): The layer of connective tissue comprised of the endometrial lining of the uterus which fluctuates in thickness throughout the menstrual cycle.

(C) uberon-0003909.description: (C): Small blood vessel similar to a capillary but with a fenestrated endothelium. Sinusoids are found in the liver, lymphoid tissue, endocrine organs, and hematopoietic organs such as the bone marrow and the spleen. Sinusoids found within terminal villi of the placenta are not comparable to these; they possess a continuous endothelium and complete basal lamina[WP].

(C) uberon-0001416.description: (C): A zone of skin that is part of an abdomen [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000087.description: (C): A mass of cells that develop into the body of the embryo and some extraembryonic tissues.

(C) uberon-0002099.description: (C): The thin membranous structure between the two heart atria or the thick muscular structure between the two heart ventricles.

(C) uberon-0000010.description: (C): A major division of the nervous system that contains nerves which connect the central nervous system (CNS) with sensory organs, other organs, muscles, blood vessels and glands.

(C) uberon-0002082.description: (C): Cardiac chamber through which blood leaves the heart.

(C) uberon-0002298.description: (C): Stalk-like part of the brain that includes amongst its parts the medulla oblongata of the hindbrain and the tegmentum of the midbrain[ZFA,MP,generalized].

(C) uberon-0002106.description: (C): The organ that functions to filter blood and to store red corpuscles and platelets.

(C) uberon-0002331.description: (C): The connecting cord from the developing embryo to the placenta.

(C) uberon-0001334.description: (C): A urethra that is part of a female reproductive system.

(C) uberon-0002407.description: (C): The combination of pericardial sac (a double-walled sac containing the heart and the roots of the great vessels) plus fibrous pericardium.

(C) uberon-0000095.description: (C): Portion of neural crest that develops from the dorsal neural tube. It overlaps the vagal neural crest and migrates to populate the pharyngeal arches 3, 4 and 6 (producing structures in the head) and to the heart, forming connective tissue that separates the great vessels of the heart. [Wikipedia].

(C) uberon-0000916.description: (C): The subdivision of the vertebrate body between the thorax and pelvis. The ventral part of the abdomen contains the abdominal cavity and visceral organs. The dorsal part includes the abdominal section of the vertebral column.

(C) uberon-0015172.description: (C): A blood vessel that is part of a endometrium.

(C) uberon-0012168.description: (C): Blood that remains in the placenta and in the attached umbilical cord after childbirth[WP].

(C) uberon-0001976.description: (C): The epithelial layer that lines the luminal space of the esophagus.

(C) uberon-0008998.description: (C): System pertaining to blood vessels in the brain.

(C) uberon-0001891.description: (C): The midbrain is the middle division of the three primary divisions of the developing chordate brain or the corresponding part of the adult brain (in vertebrates, includes a ventral part containing the cerebral peduncles and a dorsal tectum containing the corpora quadrigemina and that surrounds the aqueduct of Sylvius connecting the third and fourth ventricles)[GO].

(C) uberon-0003942.description: (C): The sensory system for the sense of touch and pain.

(C) uberon-0016405.description: (C): A capillary that is part of a lung.

(C) uberon-0004802.description: (C): The pseudostratified ciliated epithelium that lines much of the conducting portion of the airway, including part of the nasal cavity and larynx, the trachea, and bronchi.

(C) uberon-0004811.description: (C): An epithelium that is part of an endometrium [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000084.description: (C): An epithelial swelling on the Wolffian duct that elongates to invade the adjacent metanephric mesenchyme[MP].

(C) uberon-0000114.description: (C): The connective tissue located between the respiratory (airway and alveolar) epithelium, the capillary endothelium and pleural mesothelium; it contains basement membrane composed of collagen, elastin, proteoglycans, and fibronectin.

(C) uberon-0004088.description: (C): The subdivision of the face that includes the eye (eyeball plus adnexa such as eyelids) and the orbit of the skull and associated parts of the face such as the eyebrows, if present.

(C) uberon-0001434.description: (C): Anatomical system that is a multi-element, multi-tissue anatomical cluster that consists of the skeleton and the articular system.

(C) uberon-0004122.description: (C): Anatomical system that has as its parts the organs concerned with the production and excretion of urine and those concerned with reproduction.

(C) uberon-0000081.description: (C): In mammals, the metanephros is the excretory organ of the fetus, which develops into the mature kidney and is formed from the rear portion of the nephrogenic cord. The metanephros is an endocrine and metabolic organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine[GO].

(C) uberon-0000923.description: (C): A layer of cells produced during the process of gastrulation during the early development of the animal embryo, which is distinct from other such layers of cells, as an early step of cell differentiation. The three types of germ layers are the endoderm, ectoderm, and mesoderm.

(C) uberon-0003073.description: (C): A thickened portion of ectoderm which serves as the precursor to the lens. SOX2 and Pou2f1 are involved in its development[WP].

(C) uberon-0002329.description: (C): Somites are spheres of epithelial cells that form sequentially along the anterior-posterior axis of the embryo through mesenchymal to epithelial transition of the presomitic mesoderm.

(C) uberon-0000080.description: (C): The second stage of the kidney. It serves as the main excretory organ of aquatic vertebrates and as a temporary embryonic kidney in higher vertebrates. It is composed of the mesonephric duct (also called the Wolffian duct), mesonephric tubules, and associated capillary tufts. A single tubule and its associated capillary tuft is called a mesonephric excretory unit; these units are similar in structure and function to nephrons of the adult kidney. The mesonephros is derived from intermediate mesoderm in the vertebrate embryo.

(C) uberon-0003075.description: (C): A region of embryonic ectodermal cells that lie directly above the notochord. During neurulation, they change shape and produce an infolding of the neural plate (the neural fold) that then seals to form the neural tube[XAO]. The earliest recognizable dorsal ectodermal primordium of the central nervous system present near the end of gastrulation before infolding to form the neural keel; consists of a thickened pseudostratified epithelium[ZFA].

(C) uberon-0001049.description: (C): In the developing vertebrate, the neural tube is the embryo's precursor to the central nervous system, which comprises the brain and spinal cord. The neural groove gradually deepens as the neural folds become elevated, and ultimately the folds meet and coalesce in the middle line and convert the groove into a closed tube, the neural tube or neural canal (which strictly speaking is the center of the neural tube), the ectodermal wall of which forms the rudiment of the nervous system. [WP,unvetted].

(C) uberon-0005062.description: (C): One of the two elevated edges of the neural groove[GO,MP].

(C) uberon-0007106.description: (C): One of the minute vascular projections of the fetal chorion that combines with maternal uterine tissue to form the placenta.

(C) uberon-0010136.description: (C): An epithelial sheet is a flat surface consisting of closely packed epithelial cells.

(C) uberon-0003072.description: (C): Multi-tissue structure that is comprised of neural and non-neural epithelial layers which will form the retina and retinal pigmented epithelium of the mature eye[ZFA]. double walled structured formed by expansion and invagination of the distal end of the optic vesicle that develops into the pigmented and sensory layers of the retina while the mouth of the optic cup eventually forms the pupil of the eye[MP].

(C) uberon-0009850.description: (C): A multicellular organism that existence_starts_and_ends_during a nematode larval stage.

(C) uberon-0000304.description: (C): A layer of membrane around a tendon. It has 2 layers: synovial sheath + fibrous tendon sheath.

(C) uberon-0001008.description: (C): The renal system in an anatomical system that maintains fluid balance and contributes to electrolyte balance, acid/base balance, and disposal of nitrogenous waste products.

(C) uberon-0004139.description: (C): The first recognizable structure derived from the heart field.

(C) uberon-0004141.description: (C): An epithelial tube that will give rise to the mature heart.

(C) uberon-0004142.description: (C): The outflow tract septum is a partition in the outflow tract.

(C) uberon-0004666.description: (C): The membranous portion of the wall between the two lower chambers of the heart.

(C) uberon-0004667.description: (C): The muscular portion of the wall between the two lower chambers of the heart.

(C) uberon-0004145.description: (C): The outflow tract is the portion of the heart through which blood flows into the arteries.

(C) uberon-0001986.description: (C): A layer of epithelium that lines the heart, blood vessels (endothelium, vascular), lymph vessels (endothelium, lymphatic), and the serous cavities of the body[MESH]. Simple squamous epithelium which lines blood and lymphatic vessels and the heart[FMA].

(C) uberon-0002350.description: (C): The cardiac conduction system consists of specialized cardiomyocytes that regulate the frequency of heart beat[GO].

(C) uberon-0002354.description: (C): The cardiac Purkinje fiber is part of the cardiac conduction system that receives signals from the bundle of His and innervates the ventricular cardiac muscle.

(C) uberon-0004148.description: (C): Vein of heart that drains the myocardium.

(C) uberon-0004292.description: (C): Dense connective tissue that separates the atria from the ventricles and provides physical support for the heart.

(C) uberon-0004151.description: (C): A cardiac chamber surrounds an enclosed cavity within the heart.

(C) uberon-0002079.description: (C): A cardiac atrium that is in the left side of the heart. It receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins, In mammals this is pumped into the left ventricle, via the Mitral valve.

(C) uberon-0002078.description: (C): A cardiac atrium that is in the right side of the heart. It receives deoxygenated blood. In mammals, this comes from the superior and inferior vena cava and the coronary sinus, and pumps it into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.

(C) uberon-0003382.description: (C): A portion of cardiac muscle tissue that is part of a left ventricle [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0003381.description: (C): A portion of cardiac muscle tissue that is part of a right ventricle [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0004126.description: (C): A myocardium trabecular layer that is part of a cardiac ventricle.

(C) uberon-0005064.description: (C): Missing definition for term UBERON:0005064. Please replace it using linked reference.

(C) uberon-0005066.description: (C): Missing definition for term UBERON:0005066. Please replace it using linked reference.

(C) uberon-0004490.description: (C): A portion of cardiac muscle tissue that is part of an atrium [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0002063.description: (C): The sinus venosus is a large cardiac chamber at the inflow tract that receives venous blood from systemic circulation. precedes the atrium on the venous side of the chordate heart.

(C) uberon-0003983.description: (C): A conical pouch formed from the upper and left angle of the right ventricle in the chordate heart, from which the pulmonary artery arises[WP]. the anteriosuperior, smooth-walled portion of the cavity of the right ventricle, beginning at the supraventricular crest and terminates in the pulmonary trunk[MP].

(C) uberon-0006966.description: (C): A capillary that is part of the coronary system.

(C) uberon-0004291.description: (C): A cone-like structure that is formed when myocardial progenitor cells of the heart field fuse at the midline. The heart rudiment is the first structure of the heart tube.

(C) uberon-0004160.description: (C): An embryonic group of progenitor cells that forms from an outpouching of the septum transversum near the venous pole of the heart and gives rise to the epicardium.

(C) uberon-0004161.description: (C): A thick plate of mesodermal tissue that occupies the space between the thoracic cavity and yolk stalk in the early embryo, forming a transverse partition partially separating the coelomic cavity into thoracic and abdominal portions. It gives rise to the central tendon of the diaphragm[VHOG].

(C) uberon-0004128.description: (C): The optic vesicle is the evagination of neurectoderm that precedes formation of the optic cup[GO]. Portion of tissue that is comprised of neuroepitheium which has pinched off from the anterior neural keel and will form the optic cup[ZFA].

(C) uberon-0003902.description: (C): The part of the retina that contains neurons and photoreceptor cells[GO].

(C) uberon-0002513.description: (C): Replacement bone that forms within cartilage.

(C) uberon-0002385.description: (C): Muscle tissue is a contractile tissue made up of actin and myosin fibers[GO].

(C) uberon-0001135.description: (C): Muscle tissue which is unstriated, composed primarily of smooth muscle fibers surrounded by a reticulum of collagen and elastic fibers. Smooth muscle differs from striated muscle in the much higher actin/myosin ratio, the absence of conspicuous sarcomeres and the ability to contract to a much smaller fraction of its resting length[GO].

(C) uberon-0002036.description: (C): Muscle tissue that contains fibers that are divided by transverse bands into striations.

(C) uberon-0000468.description: (C): Anatomical structure that is an individual member of a species and consists of more than one cell.

(C) uberon-0004906.description: (C): A portion of the gut that is derived from ectoderm.

(C) uberon-0001041.description: (C): Anterior subdivision of a digestive tract.

(C) uberon-0001046.description: (C): The caudalmost subdivision of a digestive tract.

(C) uberon-0001045.description: (C): Middle subdivision of a digestive tract[CJM]. In vertebrates: The middle part of the alimentary canal from the stomach, or entrance of the bile duct, to, or including, the large intestine[GO].

(C) uberon-0003855.description: (C): Mesenchyme that is part of a developing gonad [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000991.description: (C): Reproductive organ that produces and releases eggs (ovary) or sperm (testis).

(C) uberon-0000473.description: (C): A gonad of a male animal. A gonad produces and releases sperm.

(C) uberon-0000062.description: (C): Anatomical structure that performs a specific function or group of functions [WP].

(C) uberon-0000479.description: (C): Multicellular anatomical structure that consists of many cells of one or a few types, arranged in an extracellular matrix such that their long-range organisation is at least partly a repetition of their short-range organisation.

(C) uberon-0001781.description: (C): Any of the layers that make up the retina[MP].

(C) uberon-0005068.description: (C): A solid rod of neurectoderm derived from the neural keel. The neural rod is roughly circular in cross section. Neural rod formation occurs during primary neurulation in teleosts[GO]. An intermediate stage in the development of the central nervous system present during the segmentation period; the neural rod is roughly cylindrical in shape, forms from the neural keel, and is not yet hollowed out into the neural tube[ZFIN].

(C) uberon-0007135.description: (C): An intermediate stage (between the neural plate and neural rod) during the early segmentation period in the morphogenesis of the central nervous system primordium; the keel is roughly triangular shaped in cross section.

(C) uberon-0002328.description: (C): A flexible rod-shaped body found in embryos of all chordates. It is composed of cells derived from the mesoderm and defines the primitive axis of the embryo. In some chordates, it persists throughout life as the main axial support of the body, while in most vertebrates it becomes the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc. The notochord is found ventral to the neural tube.

(C) uberon-0003063.description: (C): A horseshoe-shaped thickening of the endoderm at the cranial (rostral) end of the primitive streak formed by the involution of Spemann's organizer cells which, together with the notochord, induces the formation of the neural plate from the overlying ectodermal cells and contributes mesodermal type cells to the surrounding tissue.

(C) uberon-0002028.description: (C): The most posterior of the three principal regions of the brain. In mammals and birds the hindbrain is divided into a rostral metencephalon and a caudal myelencephalon. In zebrafish, with the exception of the cerebellum, the ventral remainder of the metencephalon can be separated only arbitrarily from the more caudal myelencephalic portion of the medulla oblongata (From: Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain)[ZFA]. Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the pons, cerebellum and medulla oblongata[FMA].

(C) uberon-0001785.description: (C): Cranial nerves are nerves that emerge directly from the brain, in contrast to spinal nerves, which emerge from segments of the spinal cord.

(C) uberon-0001892.description: (C): A segment of the developing hindbrain[ZFA]. In the vertebrate embryo, a rhombomere is a transiently divided segment of the developing neural tube, within the hindbrain region (a neuromere) in the area that will eventually become the rhombencephalon. The rhombomeres appear as a series of slightly constricted swellings in the neural tube, caudal to the cephalic flexure.[WP].

(C) uberon-0003052.description: (C): The part of the brain that is the morphological boundary between the midbrain and hindbrain and that is the location of an organizing center which patterns the midbrain and hindbrain primordia of the neural plate.

(C) uberon-0000988.description: (C): The part of the central nervous system lying between the medulla oblongata and the midbrain, ventral to the cerebellum.

(C) uberon-0001896.description: (C): Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the medullary reticular formation, inferior olivary complex and cochlear nuclear complex, among other structures[FMA]. The medulla oblongata lies directly above the spinal cord and controls vital autonomic functions such as digestion, breathing and the control of heart rate[GO].

(C) uberon-0001645.description: (C): Cranial nerve that has three branches - the ophthalmic (supplying the skin of the nose and upper jaw), the maxillary and the mandibular (supplying the lower jaw).

(C) uberon-0001021.description: (C): An enclosed, cable-like bundle of axons in the peripheral nervous system originating in a nerve root in the central nervous system (or a condensed nervous structure) connecting with peripheral structures.

(C) uberon-0002148.description: (C): The locus ceruleus is a dense cluster of neurons within the dorsorostral pons. This nucleus is the major location of neurons that release norepinephrine throughout the brain, and is responsible for physiological responses to stress and panic[GO]. Bluish region in the superior angle of the fourth ventricle floor, corresponding to melanin-like pigmented nerve cells which lie lateral to the ponto-mesencephalic central gray (griseum centrale). It is also known as nucleus pigmentosus pontis[GAID].

(C) uberon-0007247.description: (C): Any of the nuclei that comprise the superior olivary complex (superior olive). This includes both the primary nuclei such as the lateral and medial nuclei, as well as periolivary nuclei.

(C) uberon-0004133.description: (C): Missing definition for term UBERON:0004133. Please replace it using linked reference.

(C) uberon-0002149.description: (C): Nucleus containing parasympathetic neurons giving rise to the parasympathetic division of the facial nerve, innervating the salivary glands (Brodal, Neurological Anatomy, 3rd ed., 1981, pg 703).

(C) uberon-0005076.description: (C): An anatomical boundary that adjacent_to a hindbrain and adjacent_to a spinal cord.

(C) uberon-0001895.description: (C): Rostral segment of the hindbrain that has as its parts the pons (where present) and the cerebellum[WP,modified].

(C) uberon-0000117.description: (C): A tube in the respiratory system. Examples: bronchus, bronchiole, trachea.

(C) uberon-0000079.description: (C): The organs associated with producing offspring in the gender that produces spermatozoa.

(C) uberon-0000016.description: (C): The part of the pancreas that is part of the endocrine system and is made up of islet cells, which produce insulin, glucagon and somatostatin.

(C) uberon-0000026.description: (C): Major subdivision of an organism that protrudes from the body[DOS, CARO].

(C) uberon-0000990.description: (C): Anatomical system that has as its parts the organs concerned with reproduction.

(C) uberon-0000025.description: (C): Any hollow cylindrical anatomical structure containing a lumen through which substances are transported.

(C) uberon-0003143.description: (C): An organism at the pupal stage. A life cycle stage of holometabolous insects in which the organism is a pupa and starts with the larval-pupal apolysis and ends with pupal-adult apolysis.

(C) uberon-0004175.description: (C): The internal genitalia are the internal sex organs such as the uterine tube, the uterus and the vagina in female mammals, and the testis, seminal vesicle, ejaculatory duct and prostate in male mammals.

(C) uberon-0004176.description: (C): The external genitalia are the outer sex organs, such as the penis or vulva in mammals.

(C) uberon-0002330.description: (C): Anatomical system that consists of the glands and parts of glands that produce exocrine secretions and help to integrate and control bodily metabolic activity. Exocrine glands are glands that secrete their products (hormones) into ducts (duct glands). They are the counterparts to endocrine glands, which secrete their products (hormones) directly into the bloodstream (ductless glands) or release hormones (paracrines) that affect only target cells nearby the release site. [Wikipedia].

(C) uberon-0003704.description: (C): Passages within the liver for the conveyance of bile. Includes right and left hepatic ducts even though these may join outside the liver to form the common hepatic duct.

(C) uberon-0001152.description: (C): The tubular structure that conducts gall bladder contents from the gall bladder to the common bile duct.

(C) uberon-0000162.description: (C): Common chamber into which the intestines and excretory system opens. Arises during development in all vertebrates, but in many it becomes subdivided, lost or incorporated into other structures.

(C) uberon-0006955.description: (C): An epithelium that is part of a uterus.

(C) uberon-0000947.description: (C): The main trunk of the systemic arterial system that carries blood from the heart to all the organs and other structures of the body, bringing oxygenated blood to all parts of the body in the systemic circulation.

(C) uberon-0001496.description: (C): The ascending aorta is the portion of the aorta in a two-pass circulatory system that lies between the heart and the arch of aorta[GO]. A portion of the aorta commencing at the upper part of the base of the left ventricle, on a level with the lower border of the third costal cartilage behind the left half of the sternum; it passes obliquely upward, forward, and to the right, in the direction of the heart's axis, as high as the upper border of the second right costal cartilage, describing a slight curve in its course, and being situated, about 6 cm behind the posterior surface of the sternum. The total length is about 5 cm in length [Wikipedia].

(C) uberon-0001514.description: (C): The descending aorta is the portion of the aorta in a two-pass circulatory system from the arch of aorta to the point where it divides into the common iliac arteries[GO]. The descending aorta is part of the aorta, the largest artery in the body. The descending aorta is the part of the aorta beginning at the aortic arch that runs down through the chest and abdomen. The descending aorta is divided into two portions, the thoracic and abdominal, in correspondence with the two great cavities of the trunk in which it is situated. Within the abdomen, the descending aorta branches into the two common iliac arteries which serve the legs. [WP,unvetted].

(C) uberon-0005805.description: (C): The dorsal aorta is a blood vessel in a single-pass circulatory system that carries oxygenated blood from the gills to the rest of the body. In a single-pass circulatory system blood passes once through the heart to supply the body once.

(C) uberon-0000043.description: (C): Dense regular connective tissue that connects muscle to bone[VSAO].

(C) uberon-0007812.description: (C): A tail that extends from the posterior tip of the organism to the anus, contains muscle and skeleton.

(C) uberon-0005309.description: (C): A pronephric nephron is the functional unit of the pronephros[GO].

(C) uberon-0003060.description: (C): In mammals, the pronephric duct is the predecessor of the Wolffian duct[WP].

(C) uberon-0000459.description: (C): An anatomical wall that is part of a uterus [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0003068.description: (C): The axial mesoderm includes the prechordal mesoderm and the chordamesoderm. It gives rise to the prechordal plate and to the notochord.

(C) uberon-0003077.description: (C): The paraxial mesoderm is the mesoderm located bilaterally adjacent to the notochord and neural tube[GO].

(C) uberon-0003081.description: (C): Portion of the middle of the three primary germ layers of the embryo that resides on the periphery of the embryo, is continuous with the extra-embryonic mesoderm, splits into two layers enclosing the intra-embryonic coelom, and gives rise to body wall structures[MP].

(C) uberon-0003064.description: (C): The intermediate mesoderm is located between the lateral mesoderm and the paraxial mesoderm. It develops into the kidney and gonads.

(C) uberon-0000013.description: (C): The sympathetic nervous system is one of the two divisions of the vertebrate autonomic nervous system (the other being the parasympathetic nervous system). The sympathetic preganglionic neurons have their cell bodies in the thoracic and lumbar regions of the spinal cord and connect to the paravertebral chain of sympathetic ganglia. Innervate heart and blood vessels, sweat glands, viscera and the adrenal medulla. Most sympathetic neurons, but not all, use noradrenaline as a post-ganglionic neurotransmitter [GO].

(C) uberon-0003103.description: (C): Anatomical structure that has as its parts two or more multi-tissue structures of at least two different types and which through specific morphogenetic processes forms a single distinct structural unit demarcated by bona fide boundaries from other distinct anatomical structures of different types.

(C) uberon-0000467.description: (C): Multicellular, connected anatomical structure that has multiple organs as parts and whose parts work together to achieve some shared function.

(C) uberon-0002120.description: (C): In mammals, the pronephros is the first of the three embryonic kidneys to be established and exists only transiently. In lower vertebrates such as fish and amphibia, the pronephros is the fully functional embryonic kidney and is indispensible for larval life[GO].

(C) uberon-0000125.description: (C): A spatially aggregated collection of nerve cell bodies in the CNS, consisting of one or more subpopulations that share cell type, chemical phenotype, and connections, and including nearby cells that share the same cell type, chemical phenotype, and connections. (CUMBO).

(C) uberon-0007651.description: (C): An anatomical structure that connects two structures.

(C) uberon-0007844.description: (C): Skeletal element that is composed of cartilage tissue and may be permanent or transient.

(C) uberon-0001007.description: (C): Anatomical system that has as its parts the organs devoted to the ingestion, digestion, and assimilation of food and the discharge of residual wastes.

(C) uberon-0007375.description: (C): A multi-tissue structure consisting of bone and soft tissue that forms a part of the roof of the oral cavity. In mammals this is the combination of the primary palate (premaxilla) and the secondary palate. In early tetrapods it consists of the vomer, pterygoid, parasphenoid, palatine and ectopterygoid bones.

(C) uberon-0008814.description: (C): A transient embryonic complex that comprises the pharyngeal arches, bulges of tissues of mesoderm and neural crest derivation through which pass nerves and pharyngeal arch arteries. The arches are separated internally by pharyngeal pouches, evaginations of foregut endoderm, and externally by pharyngeal clefts, invaginations of surface ectoderm. The development of the system ends when the stucture it contributes to are forming, which may include (depending on species) the thymus, thyroid, parathyroids, maxilla, mandible, aortic arch, cardiac outflow tract, external and middle ear[GO,modified].

(C) uberon-0003889.description: (C): Initial section of the oviduct through which the ova pass from the ovary to the uterus.

(C) uberon-0004708.description: (C): An appendage that is part of an appendage girdle complex.

(C) uberon-0000033.description: (C): The head is the anterior-most division of the body [GO].

(C) uberon-0001456.description: (C): A subdivision of the head that has as parts the layers deep to the surface of the anterior surface, including the mouth, eyes, and nose (when present). In vertebrates, this includes the facial skeleton and structures superficial to the facial skeleton (cheeks, mouth, eyeballs, skin of face, etc).

(C) uberon-0000440.description: (C): A small, often microscopic, tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod, generally having a mechanical function, and usually but not necessarily composed of dense collagenous tissue. On histological section, a trabecula can look like a septum, but in three dimensions they are topologically distinct, with trabeculae being roughly rod or pillar-shaped and septa being sheet-like. Trabeculae are usually composed of dense fibrous tissue, i.e. mainly of collagen, and in most cases provide mechanical strengthening or stiffening to a soft solid organ, such as the spleen. They can be composed of other materials, such as bone or muscle[WP].

(C) uberon-0010183.description: (C): A trabecula that is part of a liver.

(C) uberon-0001265.description: (C): A trabecula that is part of a spleen.

(C) uberon-0002511.description: (C): The supporting bundles of muscular fibers lining the walls of the ventricles of the heart.

(C) uberon-0001005.description: (C): An airway through which respiratory air passes in organisms.

(C) uberon-0002167.description: (C): Lung which consists of the right upper lobe, middle lobe and right lower lobe.[FMA].

(C) uberon-0002168.description: (C): Lung which consists of the left upper lobe and left lower lobe.[FMA].

(C) uberon-0000101.description: (C): A lung lobe is one of the rounded projections that compose the lung[GO].

(C) uberon-0006562.description: (C): The pharynx is the part of the digestive system immediately posterior to the mouth[GO].

(C) uberon-0014892.description: (C): A muscle organ that consists of skeletal muscle tissue ensheathed in epimysium, that develops from myotome and that is innervated by some somatic motor neuron. Skeletal muscles are typically attached (via a tendon) to a bone but there are exceptions (e.g. intrinsic tongue muscles).

(C) uberon-0001103.description: (C): A thin musculomebranous barrier that separates the abdominal and thoracic cavities. Often used for breathing control.

(C) uberon-0003914.description: (C): Epithelial tubes transport gases, liquids and cells from one site to another and form the basic structure of many organs and tissues, with tube shape and organization varying from the single-celled excretory organ in Caenorhabditis elegans to the branching trees of the mammalian kidney and insect tracheal system.

(C) uberon-0005153.description: (C): A bud is a protrusion that forms from an epithelial sheet by localized folding.

(C) pato-0002255.description: (C): Texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being marked with one or more channels.

(C) pato-0002287.description: (C): An elasticity which is relatively high.

(C) pato-0002288.description: (C): An elasticity which is relatively low.

(C) pato-0002299.description: (C): A cylindrical shape that is hollow.

(C) pato-0002326.description: (C): An orientation inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's placement at an angle.

(C) pato-0002327.description: (C): An angle which is relatively high.

(C) pato-0002328.description: (C): An angle which is relatively low.

(C) pato-0002422.description: (C): Pertaining to the individual parts making up an aggregate fruit like a many-lobed 'berry,' such as a raspberry.

(C) pato-0002462.description: (C): A composition quality inhering in an bearer by virtue of the bearer's consisting of collagen.

(C) pato-0002468.description: (C): A structure quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being capable of swelling or stretching.

(C) pato-0015008.description: (C): A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the extent to which the bearer is capable of being stretched or swollen.

(C) pato-0002539.description: (C): A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a shape like a ring (a circular shape enclosing a space).

(C) pato-0010001.description: (C): A structural quality inhering in the bearer by virtue of the bearer consisting of multiple structures lacking any physical connection to each other.

(C) uberon-0000000.description: (C): An occurrent [span:Occurrent] that exists in time by occurring or happening, has temporal parts and always involves and depends on some entity.

(C) uberon-0034922.description: (C): A cluster of cells, largely surrounded by a morphological boundary.

(C) uberon-0000009.description: (C): A layer of dense irregular connective tissue that lines organs and supports the mucosa, as well as joins the mucosa to the bulk of underlying smooth muscle. [WP,unvetted].

(C) uberon-0004923.description: (C): A part of a wall of an organ that forms a layer.

(C) uberon-0000344.description: (C): A lining of mostly endodermal origin, covered in epithelium, which is involved in absorption and secretion. They line various body cavities that are exposed to the external environment and internal organs. It is at several places continuous with skin: at the nostrils, the lips, the ears, the genital area, and the anus. The sticky, thick fluid secreted by the mucous membranes and gland is termed mucus. The term mucous membrane refers to where they are found in the body and not every mucous membrane secretes mucus[WP].

(C) uberon-0011216.description: (C): A subdivision of an anatomical system.

(C) uberon-0000014.description: (C): Any portion of the organ that covers that body and consists of a layer of epidermis and a layer of dermis.

(C) uberon-0010314.description: (C): An anatomical structure that has some part that develops from the neural crest.
(C) uberon-0010314.label_original: structure with developmental contribution from neural crest

(C) uberon-0000015.description: (C): A non-material anatomical entity of two dimensions. Anatomical boundaries are contiguous structures.

(C) uberon-0000466.description: (C): Anatomical entity that has no mass.

(C) uberon-0000471.description: (C): Multi-tissue structure that is part of a compound organ.

(C) uberon-0003923.description: (C): Pancreatic bud that gives rise to the accessory pancreatic duct.

(C) uberon-0000409.description: (C): A gland in which the principal secretory cells are serous secreting cells.

(C) uberon-0005177.description: (C): An organ or element that part of the trunk region. The trunk region can be further subdividied into thoracic (including chest and thoracic cavity) and abdominal (including abdomen and pelbis) regions.

(C) uberon-0007329.description: (C): A duct that collects and carries secretions of the exocrine pancreas to the intestine.

(C) uberon-0003924.description: (C): Pancreatic bud that gives rise to the major pancreatic duct.

(C) uberon-0000971.description: (C): The smallest morphological and functional unit of the compound eye that consists of a usually limited and often constant number of rhabdomeric photoreceptor cells, cornea-secreting epithelial cells, and interommatidial pigment cells, and may additionally contain crystalline cone cells.

(C) uberon-0015165.description: (C): An eye consisting of multiple light-sensing organs.

(C) uberon-0000047.description: (C): An eye with one concave chamber. Note that 'simple' does not imply a reduced level of complexity or acuity.

(C) uberon-0015212.description: (C): Any structure that is placed on one side of the left-right axis of a bilaterian.

(C) uberon-0000066.description: (C): The stage of development at which the animal is fully formed, including immaturity and maturity. Includes both sexually immature stage, and adult stage.

(C) uberon-0000030.description: (C): A thin layer of loose connective tissue which lies beneath the epithelium and together with the epithelium constitutes the mucosa[WP]. The lamina propria contains capillaries and a central lacteal (lymph vessel) in the small intestine, as well as lymphoid tissue. Lamina propria also contains glands with the ducts opening on to the mucosal epithelium, that secrete mucus and serous secretions.

(C) uberon-0011825.description: (C): Irregular connective tissue, the intercellular matrix of which contains a sparse irregular network of collagen and elastic fiber bundles. Examples: areolar tissue, neuroglial tissue, mucoid tissue.

(C) uberon-0000031.description: (C): A lamina propria that is part of a respiratory airway.

(C) uberon-0004779.description: (C): A lamina propria that is part of a respiratory system [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000379.description: (C): A mucosa that is part of a respiratory airway.

(C) uberon-0011676.description: (C): A major subdivision of an organism that divides an organism along its main body axis (typically anterio-posterior axis). In vertebrates, this is based on the vertebral column.
(C) uberon-0011676.label_original: subdivision of organism along main body axis

(C) uberon-0007811.description: (C): The anteriormost subdivision of the body that includes the head, jaws, pharyngeal region and the neck (if present). In vertebrates this is the subdivision that includes the cervical vertebrae.

(C) uberon-0000481.description: (C): Anatomical structure that has as its parts two or more portions of tissue of at least two different types and which through specific morphogenetic processes forms a single distinct structural unit demarcated by bona-fide boundaries from other distinct structural units of different types.

(C) uberon-0000060.description: (C): Organ component adjacent to an organ cavity and which consists of a maximal aggregate of organ component layers.

(C) uberon-0001136.description: (C): Simple squamous epithelium of mesodermal origin which lines serous membranes. Examples: mesothelium of pleura, mesothelium of peritoneum[FMA]. Wikipedia: The mesothelium is a membrane that forms the lining of several body cavities: the pleura (thoracal cavity), peritoneum (abdominal cavity including the mesentery) and pericardium (heart sac). Mesothelial tissue also surrounds the male internal reproductive organs (the tunica vaginalis testis) and covers the internal reproductive organs of women (the tunica serosa uteri).

(C) uberon-0002204.description: (C): Anatomical system that consists of the muscular and skeletal systems.

(C) uberon-0003714.description: (C): Portion of tissue in the nervous system which consists of neurons and glial cells, and may also contain parts of the vasculature.

(C) uberon-0003869.description: (C): A presumptive structure that has the potential to develop into a ganglion.

(C) uberon-0000046.description: (C): Eye-spots which may be set into a pit to reduce the angles of light that enters and affects the eyespot, to allow the organism to deduce the angle of incoming light.

(C) uberon-0000055.description: (C): A tubular structure that contains, conveys body fluid, such as blood or lymph.

(C) uberon-0006314.description: (C): Liquid components of living organisms. includes fluids that are excreted or secreted from the body as well as body water that normally is not.

(C) uberon-0005179.description: (C): An organ or element that is part of the pelvic region. Examples: reproductive organs (in some organisms), urinary bladder, bones of the pelvis.

(C) uberon-0006555.description: (C): A tube that is part of a excretory system.

(C) uberon-0036295.description: (C): The upper tract of the renal system. The renal pelvis is the large cavity in the middle of each kidney. Urine drains from each kidney through a long tube called the ureter, into the bladder, where it is stored until it is passed from the body through the urethra.

(C) uberon-0001088.description: (C): Excretion that is the output of a kidney.

(C) uberon-0005081.description: (C): The portion of the ureteric bud that contributes to the morphogenesis of the ureter. The ureter ureteric bud is the initial structure that forms the ureter[GO].

(C) uberon-0000164.description: (C): The ventral part of the cloaca remaining after septation of the rectum, which further develops into part of the bladder, part of the prostatic part of the male urethra and the urethra and vestibule in females.

(C) uberon-0000063.description: (C): A part of an organ that constitutes a distinct modular sub-unit. In some cases, the organ may also contain other sub-units of identical or similar types, in other cases this may be a distinct entity.

(C) uberon-0004921.description: (C): A proximal-distal subdivision of the digestive tract.

(C) uberon-0013765.description: (C): Any of the organs or elements that are part of the digestive system. Examples: tongue, esophagus, spleen, crop, lunge feeding organ, tooth elements.

(C) uberon-0004907.description: (C): The region of the digestive tract extending from the beginning of the intestines to the anus[GO - gut definition].

(C) uberon-0000064.description: (C): A multicellular structure that is a part of an organ.

(C) uberon-0002553.description: (C): Anatomical space which contains portions of one or more body substances and is bounded by the internal surface of one maximally connected anatomical structure. Examples: cranial cavity, pharyngeal recess space, nasal cavity, tooth socket, cavity of serous sac, lumen of stomach, lumen of artery, fornix of vagina.

(C) uberon-0000071.description: (C): End of the life of an organism.

(C) uberon-0006984.description: (C): A two dimensional anatomical structure that is the boundary between an anatomical structure and an anatomical substance, an anatomical space or the organism's environment. Examples include the surface of your skin, the surface of the lining of your gut; the surface of the endothelium of you aorta that is in contact with blood.n.

(C) uberon-0002095.description: (C): Anatomical organ component composed of a double layer of serous membrane that suspends a viscus from the body wall or connects adjacent viscera and in doing so conveys blood vessels, lymphatics and nerves to and from the viscera. Examples: greater omentum, broad ligament of uterus, sigmoid mesocolon.

(C) uberon-0034921.description: (C): An multicellular anatomical structure that has subparts of multiple organs as a part.

(C) uberon-0000105.description: (C): A spatiotemporal region encompassing some part of the life cycle of an organism.

(C) uberon-0000092.description: (C): Stage succeeding embryo, including mature structure.

(C) uberon-0000111.description: (C): A stage at which the ectoderm, endoderm, and mesoderm develop into the internal organs of the organism.

(C) uberon-0000069.description: (C): A distinct juvenile stage many animals undergo before metamorphosis into adults. Animals with indirect development such as insects, amphibians, or cnidarians typically have a larval phase of their life cycle.

(C) uberon-0000070.description: (C): A life cycle stage of holometabolous insects in which the organism is a pupa and starts with the larval-pupal apolysis and ends with pupal-adult apolysis.

(C) uberon-0000104.description: (C): An entire span of an organism's life. In metazoans, commences with the zygote stage and ends with the death of the organism.

(C) uberon-0000072.description: (C): An section of a respiratory tract.

(C) uberon-0000073.description: (C): Any part or collection of parts of the central or peripheral nervous system. Parts may span both CNS and PNS.

(C) uberon-0000075.description: (C): Anatomical cluster consisting of the skeletal elements and articular elements that are part of an individual subdivision of the organism.

(C) uberon-0004765.description: (C): Organ consisting of skeletal tissue. Encompasses whole bones, fused bones, cartilaginious elements, teeth, dermal denticles.

(C) uberon-0000076.description: (C): The surface (external) layer of ectoderm which begins to proliferate shortly after separation from the neuroectoderm.

(C) uberon-0000490.description: (C): Epithelium which consists of a single layer of epithelial cells. Examples: endothelium, mesothelium, glandular squamous epithelium.[FMA].

(C) uberon-0005291.description: (C): A portion of tissue that is part of an embryo.

(C) uberon-0000078.description: (C): An anatomical structure that develops from the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.

(C) uberon-0003101.description: (C): Gonochoristic organism that can produce male gametes.

(C) uberon-0000474.description: (C): The organs and associated structures associated with bearing offspring in a female animal.

(C) uberon-0005753.description: (C): The metanephros develops from the most caudal part of the nephrogenic cord that is itself derived from the intermediate plate mesoderm.

(C) uberon-0005080.description: (C): The portion of the ureteric bud tube that contributes to the morphogenesis of the metanephros[GO].

(C) uberon-0007499.description: (C): An epithelial tube that is open at one end only.

(C) uberon-0000085.description: (C): A spherical embryonic mass of blastomeres formed before the blastula and resulting from cleavage of the fertilized ovum.

(C) uberon-0000086.description: (C): A glycoprotein membrane surrounding the plasma membrane of an oocyte. It is a vital constitutive part of the latter, external but not extraneous to it. The zona pellucida first appears in multilaminar primary oocytes.

(C) uberon-0000107.description: (C): The first few specialized divisions of an activated animal egg; Stage consisting of division of cells in the early embryo. The zygotes of many species undergo rapid cell cycles with no significant growth, producing a cluster of cells the same size as the original zygote. The different cells derived from cleavage are called blastomeres and form a compact mass called the morula. Cleavage ends with the formation of the blastula.

(C) uberon-0004716.description: (C): The embryo and its adnexa (appendages or adjunct parts) or associated membranes (i.e. the products of conception) The conceptus includes all structures that develop from the zygote, both embryonic and extraembryonic. It includes the embryo as well as the embryonic part of the placenta and its associated membranes - amnion, chorion (gestational sac), and yolk sac[WP].

(C) uberon-0005764.description: (C): An acellular anatomical structure that is the bounding layer of a anatomical structure.

(C) uberon-0002050.description: (C): Anatomical structure that is part of an embryo.

(C) uberon-0000088.description: (C): The mesectodermal cell layer arising from the trophectoderm that erodes the uterine mucosa and contributes to the formation of the placenta.

(C) uberon-0004345.description: (C): Outermost layer of cells in the blastodermic vesicle, which will develop into the trophoblast layer and then contact the endometrium and take part in establishing the embryo's means of nutrition.

(C) uberon-0000091.description: (C): A flattened, almost circular bilaminar plate of cells formed when the inner cell mass (aka embryoblast) forms two epithelial layers, each of a distinct lineage, separated by an extracellular basement membrane: the external (dorsal) layer is called the epiblast and the internal (ventral) layer is called the hypoblast (aka primitive endoderm); together, they compose the bilaminar embryonic disc.

(C) uberon-0000094.description: (C): Nonparenchymatous organ that primarily consists of dense connective tissue organized into a sheet which interconnects two or more organs, separates two or more body spaces from one another, or surrounds an organ or body part. Examples: interosseous membrane of forearm, obturator membrane, tympanic membrane, fibrous pericardium, fascia lata, dura mater. [FMA].

(C) uberon-0011823.description: (C): Dense connective tissue is mainly composed of collagen type I. Crowded between the collagen fibers are rows of fibroblasts, fiber-forming cells, that manufacture the fibers. Dense connective tissue forms strong, rope-like structures such as tendons and ligaments. Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones; ligaments connect bones to bones at joints. Ligaments are more stretchy and contain more elastic fibers than tendons. Dense connective tissue also make up the lower layers of the skin (dermis), where it is arranged in sheets.

(C) uberon-0005428.description: (C): Vagal neural crest is adjacent to the first seven somites gives rise to both ganglionic and ectomesenchymal derivatives[ZFA].

(C) uberon-0009912.description: (C): A portion of an organ, such as the liver, lung, breast, or brain.

(C) uberon-0002201.description: (C): A vasculature that is part of a trunk [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0006876.description: (C): A vasculature that is part of a organ.

(C) uberon-0000106.description: (C): A stage at which the organism is a single cell produced by means of sexual reproduction.

(C) uberon-0000108.description: (C): An early stage of embryonic development in animals. It is produced by cleavage of a fertilized ovum and consists of a spherical layer of around 128 cells surrounding a central fluid-filled cavity called the blastocoel. The blastula follows the morula and precedes the gastrula in the developmental sequence.

(C) uberon-0000109.description: (C): A stage defined by complex and coordinated series of cellular movements that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development of most animals. The details of gastrulation vary from species to species, but usually result in the formation of the three primary germ layers, ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.

(C) uberon-0000110.description: (C): Staged defined by the formation of a tube from the flat layer of ectodermal cells known as the neural plate. This will give rise to the central nervous system.

(C) uberon-0000113.description: (C): The stage of being a sexually mature adult animal.

(C) uberon-0003580.description: (C): A portion of connective tissue that is part of a lower respiratory tract [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0003837.description: (C): A portion of connective tissue that is part of a thorax [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0004883.description: (C): The mass of tissue made up of mesenchymal cells in the lung.

(C) uberon-0004815.description: (C): An epithelium that is part of a lower respiratory tract [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000118.description: (C): Structure derived from foregut that becomes a lung[GO].

(C) uberon-0005911.description: (C): Epithelium that derives from the endoderm. Examples: urothelium, transitional epithelium of ureter, epithelium of prostatic gland.[FMA].

(C) uberon-0005597.description: (C): A pair of lateral diverticula just over the liver rudiment representing the primordia of the lungs, formed by the floor of the foregut just anterior to the liver diverticulum.

(C) uberon-0004872.description: (C): Layer of lateral plate mesoderm that forms the circulatory system and future gut wall - overlies endoderm[WP].
(C) uberon-0004872.label_original: splanchnic layer of lateral plate mesoderm

(C) uberon-0005162.description: (C): A structure consisting of multiple cell components but which is not itself a cell and does not have (complete) cells as a part.

(C) uberon-0011215.description: (C): A multi cell part structure that is part of a central nervous system.
(C) uberon-0011215.label_original: central nervous system cell part cluster

(C) uberon-0002020.description: (C): A nervous system structure composed primarily of nerve cell bodies (somas). May also include dendrites and the initial unmyelinated portion of axons.

(C) uberon-0000126.description: (C): Nucleus that receives projections from or contains neurons that send projections through one of the cranial nerves.

(C) uberon-0002308.description: (C): A neural nucleus that is part of the brain.

(C) uberon-0000159.description: (C): The terminal part of the large intestine, continuous proximally with the rectum and distally terminates with the anus.

(C) uberon-0001353.description: (C): The anus and surrounding regions. Encompasses both internal and external regions, where present.

(C) uberon-0001245.description: (C): Orifice at the opposite end of an animal's digestive tract from the mouth. Its function is to expel feces, unwanted semi-solid matter produced during digestion, which, depending on the type of animal, may be one or more of: matter which the animal cannot digest, such as bones; food material after all the nutrients have been extracted, for example cellulose or lignin; ingested matter which would be toxic if it remained in the digestive tract; and dead or excess gut bacteria and other endosymbionts.

(C) uberon-0001988.description: (C): Portion of semisolid bodily waste discharged through the anus[MW,modified].

(C) uberon-0005409.description: (C): The part of the digestive system that excludes the hepatobiliary system.

(C) uberon-0000163.description: (C): Endoderm-lined chamber that develops as pouch-like dilation of the caudal end of the hindgut and receives the allantois ventrally and two mesonephric ducts laterally; caudally it ends blindly at the cloacal membrane formed by the union of proctodeal (anal pit) ectoderm and cloacal endoderm, with no intervening mesoderm[MP].

(C) uberon-0035804.description: (C): The primordial mouth region of the developing head.

(C) uberon-0000166.description: (C): The orifice that connects the mouth to the exterior of the body.

(C) uberon-0000167.description: (C): Anatomical cavity at the start of the digestive tract that that is enclosed by the mouth. The boundaries and contents vary depending on the species. In vertebrates, the boundaries are the oral opening, the cheeks, the palate and (if present) the palatoglossal arch - if this is not present then the mouth and pharynx form the oropharyngeal cavity. The buccal cavity contains the teeth, tongue and palate (when present).

(C) uberon-0000464.description: (C): Non-material anatomical entity of three dimensions, that is generated by morphogenetic or other physiologic processes; is surrounded by one or more anatomical structures; contains one or more organism substances or anatomical structures.

(C) uberon-0000168.description: (C): A section dividing a colon along a proximal-distal axis.

(C) uberon-0000170.description: (C): The pair of anatomical structures comprised of a left lung and right lung.

(C) uberon-0002224.description: (C): The part of the coelemic cavity lumen that is enclosed by the walls of the thorax.

(C) uberon-0000171.description: (C): Organ that functions in gaseous exchange between an organism and its environment. In plants, microorganisms, and many small animals, air or water makes direct contact with the organism's cells or tissue fluids, and the processes of diffusion supply the organism with dioxygen (O2) and remove carbon dioxide (CO2). In larger animals the efficiency of gaseous exchange is improved by specialized respiratory organs, such as lungs and gills, which are ventilated by breathing mechanisms.

(C) uberon-0000174.description: (C): A portion of organism substance that is the product of an excretion process that will be eliminated from the body. An excretion process is elimination by an organism of the waste products that arise as a result of metabolic activity.

(C) uberon-0002390.description: (C): Anatomical system that is involved in the production of hematopoietic cells.

(C) uberon-0001969.description: (C): The liquid component of blood, in which erythrocytes are suspended.

(C) uberon-0002193.description: (C): Anatomical cluster consisting of the hematopoietic system and the lymphoid system, or its analogs.

(C) uberon-0000209.description: (C): The bone forming the forehead and roof of the eye orbit.

(C) uberon-0010428.description: (C): A bone that is shaped as a broad flat plate and composed of two thin layers of compact tissue enclosing between them a variable quantity of cancellous tissue, which is the location of red bone marrow.

(C) uberon-0011164.description: (C): A bone that is part of a neurocranium [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0001697.description: (C): Subdivision of skeleton that is an anterolateral part of the cranium and structurally supports the eye. Includes bones formed and located in sclerotic layer of eyeball.

(C) uberon-0003113.description: (C): Subdivision of skeleton that includes all dermal bones in the cranial skeleton[ZFA,modified].

(C) uberon-0000211.description: (C): Dense regular connective tissue connecting two or more adjacent skeletal elements or supporting an organ.

(C) uberon-0001092.description: (C): The first vertebral bone in the vertebral column.

(C) uberon-0001131.description: (C): A foramen within a vertebral element through which the spinal cord runs. It is formed by the anterior segment, and the posterior part, the vertebral arch.

(C) uberon-0005744.description: (C): Anatomical space that is an opening in a bone, usually for passage of blood vessels or nerves.

(C) uberon-0000220.description: (C): The Atlanto-occipital joint (articulation between the atlas and the occipital bone) consists of a pair of condyloid joints. The atlanto-occipital joint is a synovial joint. The ligaments connecting the bones are: Two Articular capsules; Posterior atlantoöccipital membrane; Anterior atlantoöccipital membrane; Lateral atlantoöccipital.

(C) uberon-0001676.description: (C): The bone at the lower, posterior part of the skull.

(C) uberon-0006072.description: (C): That portion of the spine comprising the cervical vertebrae. The neck area of the spine.

(C) uberon-0011233.description: (C): Synovial sac which surrounds parts of one or more tendons. Examples: synovial tendon sheath of manual digit 2, radial bursa.
(C) uberon-0011233.label_original: synovial membrane of synovial tendon sheath

(C) uberon-0011234.label_original: fibrous membrane of synovial tendon sheath

(C) uberon-0000307.description: (C): Organism at the blastula stage - an early stage of embryonic development in animals. It is produced by cleavage of a fertilized ovum and consists of a spherical layer of around 128 cells surrounding a central fluid-filled cavity called the blastocoel. The blastula follows the morula and precedes the gastrula in the developmental sequence.

(C) uberon-0000317.description: (C): Mucosa that is part of a colon. The mucosa of the colon is lined by a simple columnar epithelium with a thin brush border and numerous goblet cells.

(C) uberon-0001207.description: (C): A mucosa that is part of a large intestine [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000320.description: (C): A mucosa that is part of a duodenum [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0001204.description: (C): A mucosa that is part of a small intestine [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000323.description: (C): An embryo that is at the late embryonic stage; this stage covers late steps of the embryogenesis with a fully formed embryo still developing before birth or egg hatching.

(C) uberon-0007220.description: (C): An embryo stage that covers late steps of the embryogenesis with a fully formed embryo still developing before birth or egg hatching.

(C) uberon-0003294.description: (C): A gland that is part of a foregut [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0006924.description: (C): A glandular epithelium that lines the stomach. The stomach's glandular epithelium is characterized by the presence of gastric glands.

(C) uberon-0000326.description: (C): Pancreatic juice is slightly alkaline and contains numerous enzymes and inactive enzyme precursors including alpha-amylase, chymotrypsinogen, lipase, procarboxypeptidase, proelastase, prophospholipase A2, ribonuclease, and trypsinogen. Its high concentration of bicarbonate ions helps to neutralize the acid from the stomach.

(C) uberon-0000456.description: (C): A portion of organism substance that is produced by exocrine glands.

(C) uberon-0000328.description: (C): The wall of the digestive tract. This encompasses all parts of the digestive tract with the exception of the lumen (cavity).

(C) uberon-0000332.description: (C): Bone marrow in which the fat cells predominate in the meshes of the reticular network.

(C) uberon-0007195.description: (C): The stroma of the bone marrow is all tissue not directly involved in the primary function of hematopoiesis. The yellow bone marrow belongs here, and makes the majority of the bone marrow stroma, in addition to stromal cells located in the red bone marrow. Yellow bone marrow is found in the Medullary cavity. Still, the stroma is indirectly involved in hematopoiesis, since it provides the hematopoietic microenvironment that facilitates hematopoiesis by the parenchymal cells. For instance, they generate colony stimulating factors, affecting hematopoiesis.

(C) uberon-0000333.description: (C): A gland that is part of the intestinal mucosa. Examples include the intestinal crypts, duodenal gland[cjm].

(C) uberon-0003408.description: (C): A gland that is part of a digestive tract [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000353.description: (C): Functional part of an organ in the body. This is in contrast to the stroma, which refers to the structural tissue of organs, being exactly, connective tissues.

(C) uberon-0003891.description: (C): Connective, non-functional supportive framework of a biological cell, tissue, or organ. Contrast with parenchyma.

(C) uberon-0000355.description: (C): A mucosa that is part of a pharynx [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0004785.description: (C): The mucous membrane lining the respiratory tract.

(C) uberon-0000361.description: (C): The red vascular substance consisting of connective tissue and blood vessels, containing primitive blood cells, macrophages, megakaryocytes, and fat cells. Red marrow is found in the cavities of many bones. It manufactures and releases leukocytes and erythrocytes into the bloodstream.

(C) uberon-0004364.description: (C): Thickened trophoblast of the blastocyst in rodents that becomes the fetal portion of the placenta.
