(OP) ro-0004023.label_original: causal relationship with disease as subject

(OP) ro-0004020.description: (OP): A relation that holds between the disease and a material entity where the physical basis of the disease is a disorder of that material entity that affects its function.
(OP) ro-0004020.label_original: disease has basis in dysfunction of

(OP) ro-0004021.description: (OP): A relation that holds between the disease and a process where the physical basis of the disease disrupts execution of a key biological process.
(OP) ro-0004021.label_original: disease has basis in disruption of

(OP) ro-0004022.description: (OP): A relation that holds between the disease and a feature (a phenotype or other disease) where the physical basis of the disease is the feature.

(OP) ro-0040035.description: (OP): This relation groups  relations between diseases and any other kind of entity.

(OP) ro-0004024.description: (OP): A relationship between a disease and a process where the disease process disrupts the execution of the process.

(OP) ro-0004026.description: (OP): A relationship between a disease and an anatomical entity where the disease has one or more features that are located in that entity.

(OP) ro-0004027.description: (OP): A relationship between a disease and an anatomical entity where the disease is triggered by an inflammatory response to stimuli occurring in the anatomical entity

(OP) ro-0004029.description: (OP): A relationship between a disease and some feature of that disease, where the feature is either a phenotype or an isolated disease.

(OP) ro-0004030.description: (OP): A relationship between a disease and an anatomical structure where the material basis of the disease is some pathological change in the structure. Anatomical structure includes cellular and sub-cellular entities, such as chromosome and organelles.
(OP) ro-0004030.label_original: disease arises from alteration in structure

(OP) ro-0007000.description: (OP): A relation between two entities, in which one of the entities is any natural or human-influenced factor that directly or indirectly causes a change in the other entity.

(OP) ro-0007001.description: (OP): A relation between an entity and a disease of a host, in which the entity is not part of the host itself, and the condition results in pathological processes.

(OP) ro-0008501.description: (OP): An interaction relationship wherein a plant or algae is living on the outside surface of another plant.

(OP) ro-0008503.description: (OP): A sub-relation of parasite of in which a parasite steals resources from another organism, usually food or nest material

(OP) ro-0008505.description: (OP): An interaction relationship wherein one organism creates a structure or environment that is lived in by another organism.

(OP) ro-0008507.description: (OP): An interaction relationship in which organism a lays eggs on the outside surface of organism b. Organism b is neither helped nor harmed in the process of egg laying or incubation.

(OP) ro-0008509.description: (OP): x 'has roost' y if and only if: x is an organism, y is a habitat, and y can support rest behaviors x.

(OP) ro-0008510.description: (OP): A trophic interaction in which one organism acquires nutrients through a symbiotic relationship with another organism

(OP) ro-0008511.description: (OP): A symbiotrophic interaction in which one organism acquires nutrients through a parasitic relationship with another organism

(OP) ro-0009001.description: (OP): 'has substance added' is a relation existing between a (physical) entity and a substance in which the entity has had the substance added to it at some point in time.

(OP) ro-0009002.description: (OP): 'has substance removed' is a relation existing between two physical entities in which the first entity has had the second entity (a substance) removed from it at some point in time.

(OP) ro-0009003.description: (OP): 'immersed in' is a relation between a (physical) entity and a fluid substance in which the entity is wholely or substantially surrounded by the substance.

(OP) ro-0009004.description: (OP): 'has consumer' is a relation between a material entity and an organism in which the former can normally be digested or otherwise absorbed by the latter without immediate or persistent ill effect.

(OP) ro-0009005.description: (OP): 'has primary substance added' indicates that an entity has had the given substance added to it in a proportion greater than any other added substance.

(OP) ro-0009006.description: (OP): A relation between an assay and a characteristic, in which the assay generates a data item which is a measure of a characteristic.

(OP) ro-0010001.description: (OP): A generically dependent continuant *b* generically depends on an independent continuant *c* at time *t* means: there inheres in *c* a specifically deendent continuant which concretizes *b* at *t*.

(OP) ro-0010002.description: (OP): *b* is carrier of *c* at time *t* if and only if *c* *g-depends on* *b* at *t*

(OP) ro-0011003.description: (OP): The entity A has an activity that regulates the quantity or abundance or concentration of the entity B.

(OP) ro-0011004.description: (OP): The entity A is not immediately upstream of the entity B but A has an activity that regulates an activity performed by B.

(OP) ro-0011007.description: (OP): The entity A has an activity that down-regulates by repression the quantity of B. The down-regulation is due to A having an effect on an intermediate entity (typically a DNA or mRNA element) which can produce B.    For example, protein A (transcription factor) indirectly decreases by repression the quantity of protein B (gene product) if and only if A negatively regulates the process of transcription or translation of a nucleic acid element that produces B.

(OP) ro-0011023.description: (OP): The entity A does not physically interact with the entity B, and A has an activity that down-regulates the quantity or abundance or concentration of B.

(OP) ro-0011008.description: (OP): The entity A has an activity that up-regulates by expression the quantity of B. The up-regulation is due to A having an effect on an intermediate entity (typically a DNA or mRNA element) which can produce B.    For example, protein A (transcription factor) indirectly increases by expression the quantity of protein B (gene product) if and only if A positively regulates the process of transcription or translation of a nucleic acid element that produces B.

(OP) ro-0011024.description: (OP): The entity A does not physically interact with the entity B, and A has an activity that up-regulates the quantity or abundance or concentration of B.

(OP) ro-0011009.description: (OP): The entity A has an activity that directly positively regulates the quantity of B.

(OP) ro-0011021.description: (OP): The entity A, immediately upstream of B, has an activity that directly regulates the quantity of B.

(OP) ro-0011010.description: (OP): The entity A has an activity that directly negatively regulates the quantity of B.

(OP) ro-0011013.description: (OP): The entity A is not immediately upstream of the entity B and has an activity that up-regulates an activity performed by B.

(OP) ro-0011014.description: (OP): An entity A directly interacts with B and A has an activity that decreases the amount of an entity B by degradating it.

(OP) ro-0011015.description: (OP): An entity A physically interacts with B and A has an activity that increases the amount of an entity B by stabilizing it.

(OP) ro-0011016.description: (OP): The entity A is not immediately upstream of the entity B and has an activity that down-regulates an activity performed by B.

(OP) ro-0011022.description: (OP): The entity A is not immediately upstream of the entity B, but A has an activity that regulates the quantity or abundance or concentration of B.

(OP) ro-0012000.description: (OP): a relation between a process and a continuant, in which the process is regulated by the small molecule continuant

(OP) ro-0012004.description: (OP): a relation between a continuant and a process, in which the continuant is a small molecule that regulates the process

(OP) ro-0012001.description: (OP): a relation between a process and a continuant, in which the process is activated by the small molecule continuant

(OP) ro-0012005.description: (OP): a relation between a continuant and a process, in which the continuant is a small molecule that activates the process

(OP) ro-0012002.description: (OP): a relation between a process and a continuant, in which the process is inhibited by the small molecule continuant

(OP) ro-0012006.description: (OP): a relation between a continuant and a process, in which the continuant is a small molecule that inhibits the process

(OP) ro-0012007.description: (OP): The relationship that links anatomical entities with a process that results in the adhesion of two or more entities via the non-covalent interaction of molecules expressed in, located in, and/or adjacent to, those entities.

(OP) ro-0012009.description: (OP): p is constitutively upstream of q iff p is causally upstream of q, p is required for execution of q or a part of q, and the execution of p is approximately constant.

(OP) ro-0012010.description: (OP): p removes input for q iff p is causally upstream of q, there exists some c such that p has_input c and q has_input c, p reduces the levels of c, and c is rate limiting for execution of q.

(OP) ro-0012013.description: (OP): x 'positively regulates in other organism' y if and only if: (x is the realization of a function to increase the frequency, rate or extent of y) AND (the agents of x are produced by organism o1 and the agents of y are produced by organism o2).

(OP) ro-0012014.description: (OP): x 'negatively regulates in other organism' y if and only if: (x is the realization of a function to reduce the frequency, rate or extent of y) AND (the agents of x are produced by organism o1 and the agents of y are produced by organism o2).

(OP) ro-0013001.description: (OP): A relationship between a neuron and a region, where the neuron has a functionally relevant number of input and/or output synapses in that region.

(OP) ro-0013002.description: (OP): A relationship between a neuron and a region, where the neuron has a functionally relevant number of input synapses in that region.

(OP) ro-0013003.description: (OP): A relationship between a neuron and a region, where the neuron has a functionally relevant number of output synapses in that region.

(OP) ro-0013004.description: (OP): A relationship between a neuron and a region, where the neuron has a functionally relevant number of input and/or output synapses distributed throughout that region (rather than confined to a subregion).

(OP) ro-0013005.description: (OP): A relationship between a neuron and a region, where the neuron has a functionally relevant number of input synapses distributed throughout that region (rather than confined to a subregion).

(OP) ro-0013006.description: (OP): A relationship between a neuron and a region, where the neuron has a functionally relevant number output synapses distributed throughout that region (rather than confined to a subregion).

(OP) ro-0013007.description: (OP): Relation between a sensory neuron and some structure in which it receives sensory input via a sensory dendrite.

(OP) ro-0013008.description: (OP): A relationship between an anatomical structure (including cells) and a neuron that has a functionally relevant number of chemical synapses to it.

(OP) ro-0013009.description: (OP): A relationship between a neuron and a cell that it has a functionally relevant number of chemical synapses to.

(OP) ro-0013010.description: (OP): A relationship between a neuron and a region, where all of the functionally relevant input and output synapses are in that region.

(OP) ro-0014001.description: (OP): A relationship between a disease and an infectious agent where the material basis of the disease is an infection with some infectious agent.

(OP) ro-0015001.description: (OP): A relation between a material entity and some data in which the data is taken as exemplifying the material entity.

(OP) ro-0015003.description: (OP): A relation between a group and another group it is part of but does not fully constitute.

(OP) ro-0015015.description: (OP): A relation between a cell and molecule or complex such that every instance of the cell has a high number of instances of that molecule expressed on the cell surface.

(OP) ro-0015016.description: (OP): A relation between a cell and molecule or complex such that every instance of the cell has a low number of instances of that molecule expressed on the cell surface.

(OP) ro-0016002.description: (OP): A relationship that holds between an organism and a disease. Here a disease is construed broadly as a disposition to undergo pathological processes that exists in an organism because of one or more disorders in that organism.

(OP) ro-0016004.description: (OP): X has exposure medium Y if X is an exposure event (process), Y is a material entity, and the stimulus for X is transmitted or carried in Y.

(OP) ro-0017002.description: (OP): A relation between information and an entity such that the information serves as a rule or guide if the entity is an occurrent, or the information serves as a model if the entity is a continuant.

(OP) ro-0017003.description: (OP): A relation between entities in which one increases or decreases as the other does the same.

(OP) ro-0017004.description: (OP): A relation between entities in which one increases as the other decreases.

(OP) ro-0017005.description: (OP): A relation between a container and measurement datum that specifies the actual amount of material in the container.

(OP) ro-0017006.description: (OP): A relation that relates a container to a measurement datum that specifies the maximum capacity of the container. Capacity can refer to either weight or volume.

(OP) ro-0017008.description: (OP): A primitive relation that holds between entities x and y in which y is at x's full disposal.

(OP) ro-0017502.description: (OP): A relation between a material entity and an occurrent in which the material entity is collected during the existence of the occurrent.

(OP) ro-0018001.description: (OP): Helper relation for OWL definition of RO:0018002 myristoylates

(OP) ro-0018002.description: (OP): A molecularly-interacts-with relationship between two entities, where the subject catalyzes a myristoylation activity that takes the object as input

(OP) ro-0018027.description: (OP): a relation between a ligand (material entity) and a receptor (material entity) that implies the binding of the ligand to the receptor activates some activity of the receptor

(OP) ro-0018028.description: (OP): a relation between a ligand (material entity) and a receptor (material entity) that implies the binding of the ligand to the receptor inhibits some activity of the receptor to below basal level

(OP) ro-0018029.description: (OP): a relation between a ligand (material entity) and a receptor (material entity) that implies the binding of the ligand to the receptor reduces some activity of the receptor to basal level

(OP) ro-0018031.description: (OP): A is a direct conjugate base of B if and only if A is chemical entity that is a Brønsted–Lowry Base (i.e., can receive a proton) and by receiving a particular proton transforms it into B.

(OP) ro-0018033.description: (OP): A is a deprotonated form of B if and only if A is chemical entity that is a Brønsted–Lowry Base (i.e., can receive a proton) and by adding some nonzero number of protons transforms it into B.    This is a transitive relationship and follows this design pattern: https://oborel.github.io/obo-relations/direct-and-indirect-relations.

(OP) ro-0018032.description: (OP): A is a direct conjugate acid of B if and only if A is chemical entity that is a Brønsted–Lowry Acid (i.e., can give up a proton) and by removing a particular proton transforms it into B.

(OP) ro-0018034.description: (OP): A is a protonated form of B if and only if A is chemical entity that is a Brønsted–Lowry Acid (i.e., can give up a proton) and by removing some nonzero number of protons transforms it into B.    This is a transitive relationship and follows this design pattern: https://oborel.github.io/obo-relations/direct-and-indirect-relations.

(OP) ro-0018035.description: (OP): A and B are a matched small molecular pair (MMP) if their chemical structures define by a single, relatively small, well-defined structural modification.    While this is normally called 'matched molecular pair' in the cheminformatics literaturel, it is labeled as 'matched small molecular pair' so as to reduce confusion with peptides and other macromolecules, which are also referenced as 'molecules' in some contexts.    This relationship is symmetric, meaning if A is a MMP with B iff B is a MMP with A.    This relationship is not transitive, meaning that A is a MMP with B and B is a MMP with C, then A is not necessarily an MMP with C.
(OP) ro-0018035.label_original: is matched small molecular pair with

(OP) ro-0018036.description: (OP): Two chemicals are tautomers if they can be readily interconverted.    This commonly refers to prototropy in which a hydrogen's position is changed, such as between ketones and enols. This is also often observed in heterocyclic rings, e.g., ones containing nitrogens and/or have aryl functional groups containing heteroatoms.

(OP) ro-0018037.description: (OP): Group A is a substituent group from Chemical B if A represents the functional part of A and includes information about where it is connected. A is not itself a chemical with a fully formed chemical graph, but is rather a partial graph with one or more connection points that can be used to attach to another chemical graph, typically as a functionalization.

(OP) ro-0018038.description: (OP): Chemical A has functional parent Chemical B if there is chemical transformation through which chemical B can be produced from chemical A.     For example, the relationship between a salt and a freebased compound is a 'has functional parent' relationship.

(OP) ro-0018039.description: (OP): Chemicals A and B are enantiomers if they share the same molecular graph except the change of the configuration of substituents around exactly one chiral center.    A chemical with no chiral centers can not have an enantiomer. A chemical with multiple chiral centers can have multiple enantiomers, but its enantiomers are not themselves enantiomers (they are diastereomers).

(OP) ro-0018040.description: (OP): Chemical A has parent hydride Chemical B if there exists a molecular graphical transformation where functional groups on A are replaced with hydrogens in order to yield B.

(OP) ro-0019003.description: (OP): Relates one individual to another which is capable of standing in for the first individual in its other relations to other individuals.

(OP) ro-0019501.description: (OP): Relates a gene to condition, such that a variation in this gene predisposes to the development of a condition.

(OP) ro-0020103.description: (OP): x directly supplies and drains y if and only if x is a capillary, y is an anatomical entity, and x directly supplies and drains y.

(OP) ro-0020202.description: (OP): A relationship between a ratio or proportion and its dividend.

(OP) ro-0020203.description: (OP): A relationship between a ratio or proportion and its divisor.

(OP) ro-0020326.description: (OP): A relationship between a biomarker 'b' and a disease or condition of clinical interest 'd', where the presence or occurrence of 'b' provides clinical information about 'd'.

(OP) ro-0020327.description: (OP): A relationship between a biomarker 'b' and a disease or condition of clinical interest 'd', where the presence or occurrence of 'b' is used to infer the presence or occurrence of 'd' or determine its subtype.

(OP) ro-0020328.description: (OP): A relationship between a serially-measured biomarker 'b' and a disease or condition of clinical interest 'd', where 'b' is used to infer the status of 'd'.

(OP) ro-0020329.description: (OP): A relationship between a biomarker 'b' and an exposure agent 'e', where 'b' is used to show that a biological response to 'e' has occurred.

(OP) ro-0020334.description: (OP): A relationship between a biomarker 'b' and an exposure agent 'e', where the effect of exposure to 'e' is correlated with the presence or occurrence of 'b', and the observation of 'b' is used to infer exposure to 'e'.

(OP) ro-0020330.description: (OP): A relationship between a biomarker 'b' and an exposure agent 'e', where 'b' is used to identify individuals who are likely to experience a favorable or unfavorable effect from exposure to 'e'.

(OP) ro-0020331.description: (OP): A relationship between a biomarker 'b' and a disease or condition of clinical interest 'd', where the presence or occurrence of 'b' is used to infer the likelihood of a clinical event, disease recurrence or progression in patients who have 'd'.

(OP) ro-0020332.description: (OP): A relationship between a biomarker 'b' and an exposure agent 'e', where 'b' is used to indicate the likelihood, presence, or extent of toxicity as an adverse effect of exposure to 'e'.

(OP) ro-0020333.description: (OP): A relationship between a biomarker 'b' and a disease or condition of clinical interest 'd', where the presence or occurrence of 'b' is used to infer the potential for developing 'd' in an individual that currently does not have 'd'.

(OP) ro-0020335.description: (OP): A relationship between a serially-measured biomarker 'b' and an exposure agent 'e', where 'b' is used to provide evidence of a biological effect of 'e'.

(OP) ro-0020336.description: (OP): A relationship between a serially-measured biomarker 'b' and an exposure agent 'e', where 'b' is used to provide evidence of exposure to 'e'.

(OP) ro-0020338.description: (OP): A relation that holds between two distinct chemical entities that are held in close proximity to each other specifically via the force of covalent interactions.

(OP) ro-0020339.description: (OP): A relation that holds between two distinct chemical entities that are held in close proximity to each other specifically via the force of non-covalent interactions.

(OP) ro-HOM0000000.description: (OP): Relation between biological objects that resemble or are related to each other sufficiently to warrant a comparison.

(OP) ro-HOM0000001.description: (OP): Similarity that results from common evolutionary origin.

(OP) ro-HOM0000002.description: (OP): Similarity that results from independent evolution.

(OP) ro-HOM0000003.description: (OP): Similarity that is characterized by the organization of anatomical structures through the expression of homologous or identical patterning genes.

(OP) ro-HOM0000004.description: (OP): Homoplasy that involves different underlying mechanisms or structures.

(OP) ro-HOM0000005.description: (OP): Homoplasy that involves homologous underlying mechanisms or structures.

(OP) ro-HOM0000006.description: (OP): Homology that is defined by similarity with regard to selected structural parameters.

(OP) ro-HOM0000007.description: (OP): Homology that is defined by common descent.

(OP) ro-HOM0000008.description: (OP): Homology that is defined by sharing of a set of developmental constraints, caused by locally acting self-regulatory mechanisms of differentiation, between individualized parts of the phenotype.

(OP) ro-HOM0000009.description: (OP): Homoplasy that involves phenotypes similar to those seen in ancestors within the lineage.

(OP) ro-HOM0000010.description: (OP): Structural homology that is detected by similarity in content and organization between chromosomes.

(OP) ro-HOM0000011.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves genes that diverged after a duplication event.

(OP) ro-HOM0000017.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves genes that diverged after a speciation event.

(OP) ro-HOM0000012.description: (OP): Paralogy that involves sets of syntenic blocks.

(OP) ro-HOM0000013.description: (OP): Syntenic homology that involves chromosomes of different species.

(OP) ro-HOM0000014.description: (OP): Structural homology that involves complex structures from which only a fraction of the elements that can be isolated are separately homologous.

(OP) ro-HOM0000015.description: (OP): Structural homology that is detected at the level of the 3D protein structure, but maybe not at the level of the amino acid sequence.
(OP) ro-HOM0000015.label_original: in protein structural homology relationship with

(OP) ro-HOM0000016.description: (OP): Structural homology that involves a pseudogenic feature and its functional ancestor.
(OP) ro-HOM0000016.label_original: in non functional homology relationship with

(OP) ro-HOM0000062.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves functional equivalent genes with retention of the ancestral function.

(OP) ro-HOM0000018.description: (OP): Historical homology that is characterized by an interspecies (horizontal) transfer since the common ancestor.

(OP) ro-HOM0000019.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves two members sharing no other homologs in the lineages considered.

(OP) ro-HOM0000020.description: (OP): Orthology that involves two genes that did not experience any duplication after the speciation event that created them.

(OP) ro-HOM0000022.description: (OP): Paralogy that results from a whole genome duplication event.

(OP) ro-HOM0000023.description: (OP): Paralogy that results from a lineage-specific duplication subsequent to a given speciation event.

(OP) ro-HOM0000024.description: (OP): Paralogy that results from a duplication preceding a given speciation event.

(OP) ro-HOM0000025.description: (OP): 1:many orthology that involves a gene in species A and one of its ortholog in species B, when duplications more recent than the species split have occurred in species B but not in species A.

(OP) ro-HOM0000034.description: (OP): Orthology that involves two genes when duplications more recent than the species split have occurred in one species but not the other.
(OP) ro-HOM0000034.label_original: in 1 to many orthology relationship with

(OP) ro-HOM0000026.description: (OP): 1:many orthology that involves a gene in species A and its ortholog in species B, when duplications more recent than the species split have occurred in species A but not in species B.

(OP) ro-HOM0000027.description: (OP): Iterative homology that involves structures arranged along the main body axis.

(OP) ro-HOM0000066.description: (OP): Biological homology that involves parts of the same organism.

(OP) ro-HOM0000028.description: (OP): Biological homology that is characterized by changes, over evolutionary time, in the rate or timing of developmental events of homologous structures.

(OP) ro-HOM0000029.description: (OP): Heterochronous homology that is produced by a retention in adults of a species of traits previously seen only in juveniles.

(OP) ro-HOM0000030.description: (OP): Heterochronous homology that is produced by a maturation of individuals of a species past adulthood, which take on hitherto unseen traits.

(OP) ro-HOM0000031.description: (OP): Paedomorphosis that is produced by precocious sexual maturation of an organism still in a morphologically juvenile stage.

(OP) ro-HOM0000032.description: (OP): Paedomorphosis that is produced by a retardation of somatic development.

(OP) ro-HOM0000033.description: (OP): Convergence that results from co-evolution usually involving an evolutionary arms race.

(OP) ro-HOM0000037.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves a structure that has no other homologs in the species in which it is defined, and several homologous structures in another species.
(OP) ro-HOM0000037.label_original: in 1 to many homology relationship with

(OP) ro-HOM0000036.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves two members of a larger set of homologs.
(OP) ro-HOM0000036.label_original: in many to many homology relationship with

(OP) ro-HOM0000042.description: (OP): Historical homology that is based on recent shared ancestry, characterizing a monophyletic group.

(OP) ro-HOM0000043.description: (OP): Historical homology that is based on distant shared ancestry.

(OP) ro-HOM0000044.description: (OP): Homocracy that involves morphologically and phylogenetically disparate structures that are the result of parallel evolution.

(OP) ro-HOM0000045.description: (OP): Historical homology that is characterized by topological discordance between a gene tree and a species tree attributable to the phylogenetic sorting of genetic polymorphisms across successive nodes in a species tree.

(OP) ro-HOM0000046.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves not recombining and subsequently differentiated sex chromosomes.

(OP) ro-HOM0000047.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves the chromosomes able to pair (synapse) during meiosis.

(OP) ro-HOM0000048.description: (OP): Orthology that involves two genes that experienced duplications more recent than the species split that created them.
(OP) ro-HOM0000048.label_original: in many to many orthology relationship with

(OP) ro-HOM0000049.description: (OP): Paralogy that involves genes from the same species.

(OP) ro-HOM0000050.description: (OP): Paralogy that involves genes from different species.

(OP) ro-HOM0000051.description: (OP): Paedomorphosis that is produced by delayed growth of immature structures into the adult form.

(OP) ro-HOM0000052.description: (OP): Peramorphosis that is produced by a delay in the offset of development.

(OP) ro-HOM0000053.description: (OP): Xenology that results, not from the transfer of a gene between two species, but from a hybridization of two species.

(OP) ro-HOM0000054.description: (OP): Orthology that involves functional equivalent genes with retention of the ancestral function.

(OP) ro-HOM0000055.description: (OP): Paralogy that is characterized by duplication of adjacent sequences on a chromosome segment.

(OP) ro-HOM0000057.description: (OP): Parallelism that involves morphologically very similar structures, occurring only within some members of a taxon and absent in the common ancestor (which possessed the developmental basis to develop this character).

(OP) ro-HOM0000058.description: (OP): Homocracy that involves recognizably corresponding characters that occurs in two or more taxa, or as a repeated unit within an individual.

(OP) ro-HOM0000060.description: (OP): Between-species paralogy that involves single copy paralogs resulting from reciprocal gene loss.

(OP) ro-HOM0000061.description: (OP): Xenology that involves genes that ended up in a given genome as a result of a combination of vertical inheritance and horizontal gene transfer.

(OP) ro-HOM0000065.description: (OP): Similarity that is characterized by interchangeability in function.

(OP) ro-HOM0000063.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves orthologous pairs of interacting molecules in different organisms.

(OP) ro-HOM0000068.description: (OP): Xenology that is characterized by multiple horizontal transfer events, resulting in the presence of two or more copies of the foreign gene in the host genome.

(OP) ro-HOM0000069.description: (OP): Paralogy that is characterized by extra similarity between paralogous sequences resulting from concerted evolution.

(OP) ro-HOM0000071.description: (OP): Structural homology that involves structures with the same or similar relative positions.

(OP) ro-HOM0000072.description: (OP): Biological homology that involves an ectopic structure and the normally positioned structure.

(OP) ro-HOM0000074.description: (OP): Iterative homology that involves two structures, one of which originated as a duplicate of the other and co-opted the expression of patterning genes of the ancestral structure.

(OP) ro-HOM0000075.description: (OP): Historical homology that involves orthologous pairs of transcription factors and downstream regulated genes in different organisms.

(DP) ro-0002029.description: (DP): Then percentage of organisms in a population that die during some specified age range (age-specific mortality rate), minus the percentage that die in during the same age range in a wild-type population.

(AP) ro-0002422.description: (AP): Used to annotate object properties to describe a logical meta-property or characteristic of the object property.
(AP) ro-0002422.label_original: logical macro assertion on an object property

(AP) ro-0002161.description: (AP): x never in taxon T if and only if T is a class, and x does not instantiate the class expression 'in taxon some T'. Note that this is a shortcut relation, and should be used as a hasValue restriction in OWL.

(AP) ro-0002172.description: (AP): An assertion that holds between an ontology class and an organism taxon class, which is intepreted to yield some relationship between instances of the ontology class and the taxon.

(AP) ro-0002171.description: (AP): A is mutually_spatially_disjoint_with B if both A and B are classes, and there exists no p such that p is part_of some A and p is part_of some B.

(AP) ro-0002420.description: (AP): A logical macro assertion whose domain is an IRI for a class
(AP) ro-0002420.label_original: logical macro assertion on a class

(AP) ro-0002173.description: (AP): S ambiguous_for_taxon T if the class S does not have a clear referent in taxon T. An example would be the class 'manual digit 1', which encompasses a homology hypotheses that is accepted for some species (e.g. human and mouse), but does not have a clear referent in Aves - the referent is dependent on the hypothesis embraced, and also on the ontogenetic stage.  [PHENOSCPAE:asilomar_mtg]

(AP) ro-0002174.description: (AP): S dubious_for_taxon T if it is probably the case that no instances of S can be found in any instance of T.

(AP) ro-0002175.description: (AP): S present_in_taxon T if some instance of T has some S. This does not means that all instances of T have an S - it may only be certain life stages or sexes that have S

(AP) ro-0002416.description: (AP): An assertion that involves at least one OWL object that is intended to be expanded into one or more logical axioms. The logical expansion can yield axioms expressed using any formal logical system, including, but not limited to OWL2-DL.

(AP) ro-0002419.description: (AP): An assertion that holds between an OWL Annotation Property P and a non-negative integer N, with the interpretation: for any P(i j) it must be the case that | { k : P(i k) } | = N.

(AP) ro-0002423.label_original: logical macro assertion on an annotation property

(AP) ro-0002421.description: (AP): A logical macro assertion whose domain is an IRI for a property
(AP) ro-0002421.label_original: logical macro assertion on a property

(AP) ro-0002474.description: (AP): An assertion that holds between an OWL Object Property and a dispositional interpretation that elucidates how OWL Class Axioms or OWL Individuals that use this property are to be interpreted in a dispositional context. For example,  A binds B may be interpreted as A have a mutual disposition that is realized by binding to the other one.

(AP) ro-0002475.description: (AP): A is has_no_connections_with B if there are no parts of A or B that have a connection with the other.

(AP) ro-0002484.description: (AP): Connects an ontology entity (class, property, etc) to a URL from which curator guidance can be obtained. This assertion is inherited in the same manner as functional annotations (e.g. for GO, over SubClassOf and part_of)

(AP) ro-0002504.description: (AP): S always_present_in_taxon T if every fully formed member of taxon T has part some S, or is an instance of S

(AP) ro-0002535.label_original: temporal logical macro assertion on a class

(AP) ro-0002539.description: (AP): Count of number of days intervening between the start of the stage and the time of fertilization according to a reference model. Note that the first day of development has the value of 0 for this property.

(AP) ro-0002540.description: (AP): Count of number of days intervening between the end of the stage and the time of fertilization according to a reference model. Note that the first day of development has the value of 1 for this property.

(AP) ro-0002541.description: (AP): Count of number of years intervening between the start of the stage and the time of birth according to a reference model. Note that the first year of post-birth development has the value of 0 for this property, and the period during which the child is one year old has the value 1.

(AP) ro-0002542.description: (AP): Count of number of years intervening between the end of the stage and the time of birth according to a reference model. Note that the first year of post-birth development has the value of 1 for this property, and the period during which the child is one year old has the value 2

(AP) ro-0002543.description: (AP): Count of number of months intervening between the start of the stage and the time of birth according to a reference model. Note that the first month of post-birth development has the value of 0 for this property, and the period during which the child is one month old has the value 1.

(AP) ro-0002544.description: (AP): Count of number of months intervening between the end of the stage and the time of birth according to a reference model. Note that the first month of post-birth development has the value of 1 for this property, and the period during which the child is one month old has the value 2

(AP) ro-0002545.description: (AP): Defines the start and end of a stage with a duration of 1 month, relative to either the time of fertilization or last menstrual period of the mother (to be clarified), counting from one, in terms of a reference model. Thus if month_of_gestation=3, then the stage is 2 month in.

(AP) ro-0002546.description: (AP): A relationship between a stage class and an anatomical structure or developmental process class, in which the stage is characterized by the appearance of the structure or the occurrence of the biological process

(AP) ro-0002547.description: (AP): Count of number of days intervening between the start of the stage and the time of coitum.

(C) unit-0010056.description: (C): A unit of energy that is equal to one thousand million electronvolts.

(C) unit-0010058.description: (C): Derived unit which is equal to the total kinetic energy of an atomic nucleus in MeV divided by the number of nucleons in the nucleus

(C) unit-0010059.description: (C): A derived unit equal to the energy deposited by ionizing radiation per micron of path length in matter

(C) unit-0010060.description: (C): A derived absorbed dose unit which is equal to one gray absorbed per minute.

(C) unit-0010061.description: (C): A derived absorbed dose unit which is equal to one centigray absorbed per minute.

(C) unit-0010062.description: (C): A derived absorbed dose unit which is equal to one milligray absorbed per minute.

(C) unit-0010063.description: (C): A derived absorbed dose unit which is equal to one milligray absorbed per day.

(C) unit-0010064.description: (C): A derived absorbed dose unit which is equal to one milligray absorbed per hour.

(C) unit-0010065.description: (C): A derived absorbed dose unit which is equal to one milligray absorbed per second.

(C) unit-0010066.description: (C): A length unit which is equal to one thousand meters.

(C) unit-0010067.description: (C): A mass unit density which is equal to mass of an object in milligrams divided by the volume in deciliters.

(C) unit-0010068.description: (C): A mass unit density which is equal to mass of an object in micrograms divided by the volume in deciliters.

(C) unit-0010069.description: (C): A pressure unit which is equal to 100,000 pascal or the pressure or stress on a surface caused by a force of 100,000 newtons spread over a surface of 1 m^[2].

(C) unit-0010070.description: (C): A gram per milliliter unit which is equal to one picogram per one milliliter.

(C) unit-0010071.description: (C): An area density unit which is equal to the mass of an object in micrograms divided by the surface area in square centimeters.

(C) unit-0010072.description: (C): A mass unit density which is equal to mass of an object in nanograms divided by the volume in microliters.

(C) unit-0010073.description: (C): A count unit that denotes a count of cells.

(C) unit-0010074.description: (C): A rate unit which represents a measurement of the number of an organism's heartbeats per one minute.

(C) unit-0010075.description: (C): A ratio unit which denotes the quantity of infectious agents to infection targets.

(C) unit-0010076.description: (C): A rate unit which represents a measurement of the number of breaths taken by an organism per one minute.

(C) unit-0010077.description: (C): A count unit of how many Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycles it took to detect a real signal from a sample. Equivalent to the PCR cycle number at which a sample's reaction curve intersects the threshold line.

(C) unit-0010080.description: (C): A concentration unit which denotes the minimum amount of a substance in a solution that still yields a positive reading, as determined by serial dilution.

(C) obi-0001933.description: (C): An information content entity that specifies a value within a classification scheme or on a quantitative scale.

(C) obi-0100051.description: (C): A material entity that has the specimen role.

(C) obi-0000245.description: (C): An entity that can bear roles, has members, and has a set of organization rules. Members of organizations are either organizations themselves or individual people. Members can bear specific organization member roles that are determined in the organization rules. The organization rules also determine how decisions are made on behalf of the organization by the organization members.

(C) caro-0001010.description: (C): Material anatomical entity that is a member of an individual species or is a viral or viroid particle.

(C) obi-0000047.description: (C): Is a material entity that is created or changed during material processing.

(C) obi-0600036.description: (C): a process through which a new type of cell culture or cell line is created, either through the isolation and culture of one or more cells from a fresh source, or the deliberate experimental modification of an existing cell culture (e.g passaging a primary culture to become a secondary culture or line, or the immortalization or stable genetic modification of an existing culture or line).

(C) obi-0000094.description: (C): A planned process which results in physical changes in a specified input material

(C) obi-0000067.description: (C): a role that inheres in a material entity that is realized in an assay in which data is generated about the bearer of the evaluant role

(C) obi-0000441.description: (C): an objective specification to determine a specified type of information about an evaluated entity (the material entity bearing evaluant role)

(C) obi-0000079.description: (C): a processed material that provides the needed nourishment for microorganisms or cells grown in vitro.

(C) obi-0000112.description: (C): a role borne by a material entity that is gained during a specimen collection process and that can be realized by use of the specimen in an investigation

(C) obi-0000659.description: (C): A planned process with the objective of collecting a specimen.

(C) obi-0000185.description: (C): An assay that produces a picture of an entity.

(C) obi-0000272.description: (C): A plan specification which has sufficient level of detail and quantitative information to communicate it between investigation agents, so that different investigation agents will reliably be able to independently reproduce the process.

(C) obi-0000419.description: (C): enzyme and has_function some GO:0003964 (RNA-directed DNA polymerase  activity)

(C) obi-0000453.description: (C): Measure function is a function that is borne by a processed material  and realized in a process in which information about some entity is expressed relative to some reference.

(C) obi-0000639.description: (C): is an objective to transform a material entity into spatially separated components.

(C) obi-0000678.description: (C): A material separation objective aiming to separate material into multiple portions, each of which contains a similar composition of the input material.

(C) obi-0000681.description: (C): A material separation objective aiming to separate a material entity that has parts of different types, and end with at least one output that is a material with parts of fewer types (modulo impurities).

(C) obi-0000684.description: (C): A objective specification to obtain a material entity for potential use as an input during an investigation.

(C) obi-0000671.description: (C): a material obtained from an organism in order to be a representative of the whole

(C) obi-0600005.description: (C): a process with the objective to obtain a material entity that was part of an organism for potential future use in an investigation

(C) obi-0000740.description: (C): A material sample role is a specimen role borne by a material entity that is the output of a material sampling process.

(C) obi-0000744.description: (C): A specimen gathering process with the objective to obtain a specimen that is representative of the input material entity

(C) obi-0000806.description: (C): An objective specification maintains some or all of the qualities of a material over time.

(C) obi-0000811.description: (C): a quality of a DNA molecule that inheres in its bearer due to the order of its DNA nucleotide residues.

(C) obi-0000832.description: (C): A device in which a measure function inheres.

(C) obi-0000845.description: (C): The primary structure of an RNA molecule that is completely defined by the set of its nucleic residue parts and the linear order induced by the peptide bonds that hold them together

(C) obi-0000973.description: (C): A measurement datum that representing the primary structure of a macromolecule(it's sequence) sometimes associated with an indicator of confidence of that measurement.

(C) obi-0001010.description: (C): An extract that is the output of an extraction process in which nucleic acid molecules are isolated from a specimen.

(C) obi-0666667.description: (C): a material separation to recover the nucleic acid fraction of an input material

(C) obi-0001108.description: (C): An device that is used to determine the order of nucleotides in nucleic acid sequences.

(C) obi-0001137.description: (C): An device that is used to determine the order of amino acids in protein sequences.

(C) obi-0001573.description: (C): A sequence data item that is about the primary structure of DNA

(C) obi-0001912.description: (C): A processed material that serves as a liquid vehicle for freezing cells for long term quiescent stroage, which contains chemicls needed to sustain cell viability across freeze-thaw cycles.

(C) obi-0002076.description: (C): A material entity that has two or more specimens as its parts.

(C) obi-0003024.description: (C): A cytometry assay that measures the abundance and/or characteristics of lymphocytes

(C) obi-0100010.description: (C): A material entity which results from viral transformation process using EBV as transformation agent when applied to B-cell entity
(C) obi-0100010.label_original: Epstein Barr virus transformed B cell

(C) obi-0100060.description: (C): A processed material comprised of a collection of cultured cells that has been continuously maintained together in culture and shares a common propagation history.

(C) obi-0600024.description: (C): a protocol application in which cells are kept alive in a defined environment outside of an organism.  part of cell_culturing

(C) obi-0400103.description: (C): A DNA sequencer is an instrument that determines the order of deoxynucleotides in deoxyribonucleic acid sequences.

(C) obi-0600047.description: (C): An assay the uses chemical or biochemical means to infer the sequence of a biomaterial

(OP) obi-0000417.description: (OP): This relation obtains between a planned process and a objective specification when the criteria specified in the objective specification are met at the end of the planned process.

(OP) obi-0000833.description: (OP): This relation obtains between an objective specification and a planned process when the criteria specified in the objective specification are met at the end of the planned process.

(OP) obi-0000643.description: (OP): the relation of the cells in the finger of the skin to the finger, in which an indeterminate number of grains are parts of the whole by virtue of being grains in a collective that is part of the whole, and in which removing one granular part does not nec- essarily damage or diminish the whole. Ontological Whether there is a fixed, or nearly fixed number of parts - e.g. fingers of the hand, chambers of the heart, or wheels of a car - such that there can be a notion of a single one being missing, or whether, by contrast, the number of parts is indeterminate - e.g., cells in the skin of the hand, red cells in blood, or rubber molecules in the tread of the tire of the wheel of the car.

(OP) obi-0001938.description: (OP): A relation between an information content entity and a value specification that specifies its value.

(DP) dwc-maximumDistanceAboveSurfaceInMe.label_original: Maximum Distance Above Surface In Meters

(DP) dwc-minimumDistanceAboveSurfaceInMe.label_original: Minimum Distance Above Surface In Meters

(C) uberon-0002544.description: (C): A subdivision of the autopod that has as part a series of phalanges together with associated vasculature, musculature, integument and nerves. It is continuous with the metapodial subdivision of the autopod, but does not include the metapodials. In species such as humans, fully formed digits are distinct, whereas in other species the digits may be connected by interdigital webbing, or may be completely unseparated (for example, in cetaceans).

(C) uberon-0003221.description: (C): Endochondral bones that are often elongate and arranged in rows of articulating elements, and form the visible part of the digits.

(C) uberon-0002228.description: (C): An intersegmental rod-shaped bone that forms in the peritoneal membrane and attach to the vertebral parapophyses.

(C) uberon-0010758.description: (C): A major subdivision of an organism that divides an organism along an axis perpedicular to the main body anterior-posterior axis. In vertebrates, this is typically a fin or limb segment. In insects, this includes segments of appendages such as antennae, as well as segments of the insect leg.
(C) uberon-0010758.label_original: subdivision of organism along appendicular axis

(C) uberon-0001091.description: (C): Skeletal element within the mouth (or in some species, upper part of the digestive tract) that is composed of dentine and is used in procuring or masticating food.

(C) uberon-0000002.description: (C): Lower, narrow portion of the uterus where it joins with the top end of the vagina.

(C) uberon-0000996.description: (C): A fibromuscular tubular tract leading from the uterus to the exterior of the body in female placental mammals and marsupials, or to the cloaca in female birds, monotremes, and some reptiles[WP].

(C) uberon-0000003.description: (C): Orifice of the olfactory system. The naris is the route by which odorants enter the olfactory system[MAH].

(C) uberon-0005725.description: (C): A sensory system that is capable of olfaction (the sensory perception of smell).

(C) uberon-0001707.description: (C): An anatomical cavity that is part of the olfactory apparatus. This includes the space bounded anteriorly by the nares and posteriorly by the choanae, when these structures are present.

(C) uberon-0000004.description: (C): The olfactory organ of vertebrates, consisting of nares, olfactory epithelia and the structures and skeletal framework of the nasal cavity.

(C) uberon-0002268.description: (C): An organ that houses olfactory neurons and is responsible for the sense of smell. Examples include the vertebrate nose and the Drosophila dorsal organ.

(C) uberon-0006813.description: (C): Structural framework that provides support to the nasal sacs and ducts.

(C) uberon-0003050.description: (C): A thick plate of cells derived from the neural ectoderm in the head region of the embryo that develops into the olfactory region of the nasal cavity.

(C) uberon-0000007.description: (C): The pituitary gland is an endocrine gland that secretes hormones that regulate many other glands [GO]. An endocrine gland located ventral to the diencephalon and derived from mixed neuroectodermal and non neuroectodermal origin [ZFIN].

(C) uberon-0002196.description: (C): The glandular, anterior lobe of the pituitary gland. The anterior pituitary regulates several physiological processes including stress, growth, and reproduction[WP]. The anterior lobe of the hypophysis (pituitary gland). This lobe contains cells that produce prolactin, growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone and proopiomelanocortin[ZFA].

(C) uberon-0002198.description: (C): The posterior part of the pituitary gland that secretes hormones involved in blood pressure regulation such as oxytocin and antidiuretic hormon.

(C) uberon-0000021.description: (C): Anatomical projection that protrudes from the skin. Examples: hair, nail, feather, claw, hoof, horn, wattle, spur, beak, antler, bristle and some scales.

(C) uberon-0013703.description: (C): Anatomical projection that is part of the integumentl system.

(C) uberon-0000022.description: (C): One of the epidermal growths that form the distinctive outer covering, or plumage, on birds. Feathers are formed in tiny follicles in the epidermis, or outer skin layer, that produce keratin proteins.

(C) uberon-0000024.description: (C): Forelimb that is used to produce lift for flight through the air.

(C) uberon-0002102.description: (C): A (free) limb that is connected to a pectoral girdle. The extent of this structure includes autopod, stylopod and zeugopod regions when present, but excludes the pectoral girdle and its parts.

(C) uberon-0001466.description: (C): A digit that is part of a pes (foot).

(C) uberon-0002389.description: (C): A digit that is part of a manus (hand).

(C) uberon-0000029.description: (C): Any of the rounded masses of lymphoid tissue that are surrounded by a capsule of connective tissue, are distributed along the lymphatic vessels, and contain numerous lymphocytes which filter the flow of lymph.

(C) uberon-0001473.description: (C): A vessel that contains or conveys lymph, that originates as an interfibrillar or intercellular cleft or space in a tissue or organ, and that if small has no distinct walls or walls composed only of endothelial cells and if large resembles a vein in structure[BTO].

(C) uberon-0001744.description: (C): Portion of connective tissue with various types of white blood cells enmeshed in it, most numerous being the lymphocytes[WP].

(C) uberon-0002465.description: (C): The lymphatic system in vertebrates is a network of conduits that carry a clear fluid called lymph. It also includes the lymphoid tissue through which the lymph travels. Lymphoid tissue is found in many organs, particularly the lymph nodes, and in the lymphoid follicles associated with the digestive system such as the tonsils. The system also includes all the structures dedicated to the circulation and production of lymphocytes, which includes the spleen, thymus, bone marrow and the lymphoid tissue associated with the digestive system[WP].

(C) uberon-0002006.description: (C): Peripheral portion of the lymph node, underneath the capsule[WP].

(C) uberon-0002007.description: (C): The medullary portion of the lymph node, which contains large blood vessels, sinuses and medullary cords that contain antibody-secreting plasma cells.

(C) uberon-0002194.description: (C): Capsule surrounding lymph node composed of connective tissue with some plain muscle fibers.

(C) uberon-0002391.description: (C): Lymph is the fluid that is formed when interstitial fluid enters the conduits of the lymphatic system through lymph capillaries[WP].

(C) uberon-0034953.description: (C): A population of lymphatic endothelial cell precursors that will form the lymph vessels.

(C) uberon-0000035.description: (C): An ovarian follicle that has one layer of granulosa cells.

(C) uberon-0005170.description: (C): A layer of the ovarian follicle that consists of granulosa cells.

(C) uberon-0001305.description: (C): A spherical aggregation of cells in the ovary that contains a single oocyte[WP,modified].

(C) uberon-0003981.description: (C): Primordial follicles are indiscernible to the naked eye and develop to primary, secondary, and finally mature vesicular follicles.

(C) uberon-0000036.description: (C): A maturing ovarian follicle that has two more more layers of granulosa cells, up to the onset of antrum formation.

(C) uberon-0000037.description: (C): A follicle that has reached the most mature stage of folliculogenesis, characterized by the presence of the antrum.

(C) uberon-0000039.description: (C): Region of ovarian follicle filled with follicular fluid.

(C) uberon-0000038.description: (C): The fluid surrounding the ovum and granulosa cells in the ovarian follicle.

(C) uberon-0000040.description: (C): A hemopoietic organ found in elasmobranchs. Along with the spleen and special tissue around the gonads, this structure produces red blood cells and it is nestled along the top and bottom of the esophagus.

(C) uberon-0000041.description: (C): Multi-tissue structure composed of enameloid, dentine surrounding a pulp cavity, and bone of attachment anchoring the element into the dermis[VSAO].

(C) uberon-0007380.description: (C): Dermal bone that is thin, flexible, and platelike, and that develops in overlapping skinfolds that cover the body and often the head of fish and the bases of the fins.

(C) uberon-0001751.description: (C): Collagen-rich odontogenic tissue characteristic of teeth and tooth-like skeletal elements (e.g., odontodes); mature dentine is mineralized and develops from predentine tissue; often (but not always) tubular and acellular.

(C) uberon-0011692.description: (C): Skeletal tissue that is hypermineralized and aprismatic and deposited by a combination of ameloblasts and odontoblasts that are excluded from the matrix. Enameloid develops from pre-enameloid tissue.

(C) uberon-0000044.description: (C): Sensory ganglia located on the dorsal spinal roots within the vertebral column. The spinal ganglion cells are pseudounipolar. The single primary branch bifurcates sending a peripheral process to carry sensory information from the periphery and a central branch which relays that information to the spinal cord or brain. (MSH) * ganglion found on the posterior root of each spinal nerve, composed of the unipolar nerve cell bodies of the sensory neurons of the nerve. (CSP).

(C) uberon-0002261.description: (C): The dorsal roots contain afferent sensory axons. The dorsal roots of each side continue outwards, along the way forming a dorsal root ganglion (also called a spinal ganglion).

(C) uberon-0002420.description: (C): An individual member of a collection of basal ganglia. Basal ganglia are subcortical masses of gray matter in the forebrain and midbrain that are richly interconnected and so viewed as a functional system. The nuclei usually included are the caudate nucleus (caudoputamen in rodents), putamen, globus pallidus, substantia nigra (pars compacta and pars reticulata) and the subthalamic nucleus. Some also include the nucleus accumbens and ventral pallidum[NIF,modified].

(C) uberon-0000048.description: (C): Simple eye that has a small aperture (which may be adjustable) and deep pit. It is only found in the nautiloids.

(C) uberon-0000049.description: (C): Simple eye that consists of a lens of one refractive index.

(C) uberon-0000050.description: (C): Simple eye that has two or more lenses. Some marine organisms bear more than one lens; for instance the copeopod Pontella has three. The outer has a parabolic surface, countering the effects of spherical aberration while allowing a sharp image to be formed. Copilla's eyes have two lenses, which move in and out like a telescope.

(C) uberon-0000051.description: (C): The deepest portions of the vagina, extending into the recesses created by the vaginal portion of cervix[WP,unvetted].

(C) uberon-0000052.description: (C): A C-shaped bundle of fibres (axons) in the brain, and carries signals from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies and septal nuclei. It is typically divided into the columns (crus), body, commissure and the pre-commissural and post-commissural fornix (MM).

(C) uberon-0007702.description: (C): An axon tract that is part of a brain.

(C) uberon-0002206.description: (C): One of two hemispherical bulges on the base of the posterior hypothalamus (Butler and Hodos, Comparative Vertebrate Neuroanatomy, 2nd ed., 2005, pg 455).

(C) uberon-0002663.description: (C): Collection of nerve cells in the medial forebrain lying generally in front of the anterior commissure (Maryann Martone).

(C) uberon-0002421.description: (C): Hippocampus (proper) plus dentate gyrus and subiculum[definition derived from NIF comments and ontology alignment].

(C) uberon-0000053.description: (C): An oval area in the retina, usually located temporal to the posterior pole of the eye and slightly below the level of the optic disk. It is characterized by the presence of a yellow pigment diffusely permeating the inner layers, contains the fovea centralis in its center, and provides the best phototopic visual acuity. It is devoid of retinal blood vessels, except in its periphery, and receives nourishment from the choriocapillaris of the choroid. (From Cline et al., Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed).

(C) uberon-0000054.description: (C): Thickened areas of the saccule or utricle where the termination of the vestibular nerve occurs[MESH,modified].

(C) uberon-0001846.description: (C): Complex labyrinthine structure that comprises sensory endorgans specialized for vestibular, auditory, and acoustico-vestibular sensation.

(C) uberon-0000067.description: (C): A stage that is part of the embryo stage.

(C) uberon-0000074.description: (C): A capillary tuft which forms a close network with the visceral epithelium (podocytes) and the mesangium to form the filtration barrier and is surrounded by Bowman's capsule in nephrons of the vertebrate kidney[GO].

(C) uberon-0005749.description: (C): The capillary loops of the kidney that normally function as a filtration unit[MP].

(C) uberon-0001230.description: (C): A cup-like sac at the expanded beginning of a tubular component of a nephron that contains the glomerulus.

(C) uberon-0001047.description: (C): A large synaptic bouton found in areas like olfactory bulb, cerebellar cortex and thalamus, that contacts many post-synaptic targets.

(C) uberon-0001229.description: (C): The structure containing the glomerular capsule and the glomerulus that serves as the initial blood-filtering component of a nephron.

(C) uberon-0000082.description: (C): A kidney at the most advanced stage of development in a mammal.

(C) uberon-0000089.description: (C): Missing definition for term UBERON:0000089. Please replace it using linked reference.

(C) uberon-0004750.description: (C): A layer of cells formed at one pole of macrolecithal eggs such as the yolky egg of birds. The yolk prevents the division from taking place through the egg, resulting in meroblastic cleavage during the many cleavage divisions. At the animal pole (containing less yolk than the vegetal pole), the zygote divides and subdivides, forming the blastoderm, which gradually spreads around the yolk and forms the embryo. The blastoderm is composed of two layers, the epiblast and the hypoblast, which enclose the fluid-filled blastocoel cavity.

(C) uberon-0000090.description: (C): Fluid-filled central region of a blastocyst.

(C) uberon-0000093.description: (C): A depression or fissure in the surface of an organ.

(C) uberon-0000100.description: (C): The orifice of invagination of the endomesodermal cells during the embryonic stages of an organism.

(C) uberon-0004735.description: (C): The cavity of a gastrula forming a primitive gut.

(C) uberon-0000103.description: (C): Instant starting or ending a life cycle stage. These can be arbitrary/fiat.

(C) uberon-0000116.description: (C): Primitive gas exchange portion of the lung composed of type I and type II cells[GO].

(C) uberon-0002299.description: (C): Spherical outcropping of the respiratory bronchioles and primary site of gas exchange with the blood. Alveoli are particular to mammalian lungs. Different structures are involved in gas exchange in other vertebrates[WP].

(C) uberon-0000119.description: (C): Portion of tissue, that consists of single layer of cells connected to each other by cell junctions. Examples: layer of glial cells; epithelium.

(C) uberon-0000120.description: (C): Cell layer consisting of lining cells that separates the central nervous system and the bloodstream. The BBB may consist of endothelial cells or glial cells. An endothelial barrier may have arisen independently several times during evolution. In bichir and lungfish the barrier is formed by brain endothelial cells, while in sturgeon it is formed by a complex perivascular glial sheath, but with no detectable tight junctions.

(C) uberon-0000121.description: (C): A layer of thin, concentrically arranged cells with interspersed collagen that lies within the epineurium. The perineurium is a component of the blood–nerve barrier and is essential for protecting axons and their associated Schwann cells from ionic flux, toxins and infection.

(C) uberon-0003209.description: (C): Barrier between the perineurium of peripheral nerves and the vascular endothelium of endoneurial capillaries. The perineurium acts as a diffusion barrier, but ion permeability at the blood-nerve barrier is still higher than at the blood-brain barrier[GO].

(C) uberon-0000124.description: (C): A loose connective tissue sheath surrounding each peripheral nerve. Composed mainly of colagen and fibroblasts, it forms a substantial covering over nerve trunks, then thins to an incomplete layer around smaller branches near their terminations. The epineurium is continuous centrally with the dura. Peripherally, it usually ends near the termination of a nerve fiber, but it may continue as the capsule of Meissner corpuscles and a few other encapsulated endings. Nolte, J. The Human Brain 3rd edition.

(C) uberon-0000123.description: (C): The loose connective tissue within the perineurium that continues into nerve fascicles and surrounds individual fibers. (Nolte, J. The Human Brain 3rd edition).

(C) uberon-0006804.description: (C): Loose connective tissue which consists of an irregular network of cells and reticular fibers and is spatially associated with myeloid and lymphoid cells. Examples: stroma of bone marrow, stroma of spleen, stroma of lymph node.[FMA].

(C) uberon-0000127.description: (C): The group of motor neurons residing in the pons that innervate the muscles of facial expression.

(C) uberon-0001647.description: (C): Cranial nerve that branches into the supraorbital (supplying the skin of the eye region and the lateral line organs here), the palatine (to the roof of the buccal cavity), and the hyomandibular (dividing into the jugular and mental branches).

(C) uberon-0010123.description: (C): A gray matter that has the potential to develop into a facial nucleus.

(C) uberon-0000128.description: (C): Prominent oval structure in the medulla oblongata, present in pairs, the lower portion of the brainstem. They contain the olivary nuclei.

(C) uberon-0000130.description: (C): Foramen that pierces the transverse processes of the seven cervical vertebrae. In the upper six vertebrae, the foramen gives passage to the vertebral artery, vertebral vein, and a plexus of sympathetic nerves. The seventh foramen lacks the artery, but contains the vein and sympathetic nerves.

(C) uberon-0001077.description: (C): The transverse or costal processes of a vertebra, two in number, project one at either side from the point where the lamina joins the pedicle, between the superior and inferior articular processes. They serve for the attachment of muscles and ligaments. [WP,unvetted].

(C) uberon-0001588.description: (C): The vertebral vein is formed in the suboccipital triangle, from numerous small tributaries which spring from the internal vertebral venous plexuses and issue from the vertebral canal above the posterior arch of the atlas. They unite with small veins from the deep muscles at the upper part of the back of the neck, and form a vessel which enters the foramen in the transverse process of the atlas, and descends, forming a dense plexus around the vertebral artery, in the canal formed by the foramina transversaria of the cervical vertebrae. This plexus ends in a single trunk, which emerges from the foramen transversarium of the sixth cervical vertebra, and opens at the root of the neck into the back part of the innominate vein near its origin, its mouth being guarded by a pair of valves. On the right side, it crosses the first part of the subclavian artery. [WP,unvetted].

(C) uberon-0012373.description: (C): A nerve plexus that is part of a sympathetic nervous system.

(C) uberon-0000144.description: (C): The medial portion of the articular surface of the humerus is named the trochlea, and presents a deep depression between two well-marked borders; it is convex from before backward, concave from side to side, and occupies the anterior, lower, and posterior parts of the extremity. It is directly inferior to the most prominent anterior humeral fossia, the Coronoid fossia. It articulates with the ulna.

(C) uberon-0005055.description: (C): An organ part that is part of a long bone [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0004404.description: (C): A distal epiphysis that is part of a humerus [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000151.description: (C): Paired fin that is located in the thoracic region of the body.

(C) uberon-0002534.description: (C): Fin that is one of a pair located ventrally on the organism.

(C) uberon-0010710.description: (C): Paired fin skeleton that consists of the supporting endochondral proximal and distal radials and the dermal fins rays or lepidotrichia. The pectoral fin skeleton is located in the thoracic region of the body and articulates with the scapula and coracoid.

(C) uberon-0000152.description: (C): Paired fin located in the abdominal position of the body.

(C) uberon-0010711.description: (C): Paired fin skeleton located in the abdominal position that consists of supporting endochondral radialsB and dermal fin rays or lepidotrichia.

(C) uberon-0000155.description: (C): A layer of the ovarian follicle that consists of theca cells.

(C) uberon-0000156.description: (C): The theca externa is the outer layers of the theca folliculi. It contains abundant collagen and is mainly supportive.

(C) uberon-0000157.description: (C): Theca interna cells express receptors for luteinizing hormone, which when activated will stimulate the production of androstenedione from cholesterol by the enzyme desmolase. Androstenedione ultimately gives the granulosa cells the precursor substrate for estrogen manufacturing.

(C) uberon-0000172.description: (C): A bodily fluid consisting of the expulsed contents of the stomach disgorged through the mouth or nose that happens as a result of a vomit reflex.

(C) uberon-0036017.description: (C): A bodily fluid consisting of the contents of the digestive tract expulsed through the anterior portion of the digestive tract.

(C) uberon-0000173.description: (C): Amniotic fluid is a bodily fluid consisting of watery liquid surrounding and cushioning a growing fetus within the amnion. It allows the fetus to move freely without the walls of the uterus being too tight against its body. Buoyancy is also provided. The composition of the fluid changes over the course of gestation. Initially, amniotic fluid is similar to maternal plasma, mainly water with electrolytes. As the fetus develops, proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, phospholipids originating from the lungs, fetal cells, and urea are deposited in the fluid.

(C) uberon-0000305.description: (C): The thin innermost layer of the extraembryonic membranes that contains the amniotic fluid; the membrane forms a closed sac in which the embryo and later, the fetus, is suspended and protected.

(C) uberon-0000175.description: (C): Pleural effusion is a bodily fluid that is produced in exess and accumulates in the pleural cavity, the fluid-filled space that surrounds the lungs. Excessive amounts of such fluid can impair breathing by limiting the expansion of the lungs during inhalation.

(C) uberon-0000176.description: (C): A bodily fluid secreted from the body via the mouth or nose.

(C) uberon-0001826.description: (C): The mucous membrane that lines the nasal cavity[MP].

(C) uberon-0000177.description: (C): Pus is a bodily fluid consisting of a whitish-yellow or yellow substance produced during inflammatory responses of the body that can be found in regions of pyogenic bacterial infections. Pus is produced from the dead and living cells which travel into the intercellular spaces around the affected cells.

(C) uberon-0000180.description: (C): A region of the posterior torso (lower back) beneath the ribs and above the ilium.

(C) uberon-0000199.description: (C): The narrow part of the shaft of the radius just below the head.

(C) uberon-0001423.description: (C): The major preaxial endochondral bone in the anterior zeugopod[Phenoscape].

(C) uberon-0018664.description: (C): The neck region of a bone organ.

(C) uberon-0004413.description: (C): A proximal epiphysis that is part of a radius [Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0000200.description: (C): A ridge on the cerebral cortex. It is generally surrounded by one or more sulci .

(C) uberon-0034768.description: (C): A part of an organism or organ that is continuous with its surroundings and distinguished from its surroundings based on morphology.

(C) uberon-0013118.description: (C): A depression or fissure in the surface of the brain. It surrounds the gyri, creating the characteristic appearance of the brain in humans and other large mammals.

(C) uberon-0000201.description: (C): A blood brain barrier that is composed of endothelial cells.

(C) uberon-0000202.description: (C): A blood brain barrier composed of glial cells.

(C) uberon-0000204.description: (C): Ventral part (base region) of the telencephalon.

(C) uberon-0000205.description: (C): A thin protuberance on the surface of the body of an echinoderm containing diverticula of the water vascular system lined by ciliated peritoneum. Along with tube feet, provide the principle gas exchange surfaces..

(C) uberon-0002535.description: (C): Anatomical surface structure found in many aquatic organisms. It is a respiration organ whose function is the extraction of oxygen from water and the excretion of carbon dioxide. The microscopic structure of a gill is such that it presents a very large surface area to the external environment. Gills usually consist of thin filaments of tissue, branches, or slender tufted processes which have a highly folded surface to increase surface area. A high surface area is crucial to the gas exchange of aquatic organisms as water contains only 1/20 parts dissolved Oxygen compared to air. With the exception of some aquatic insects, the filaments and lamellae (folds) contain blood or coelomic fluid, from which gases are exchanged through the thin walls. Oxygen is carried by the blood to other parts of the body. Carbon dioxide passes from the blood through the thin gill tissue into the water. Gills or gill-like organs, located in different parts of the body, are found in various groups of aquatic animals, including mollusks, crustaceans, insects, fish, and amphibians.

(C) uberon-0000206.description: (C): A gill that develops in the walls of the pharynx along a series of gill slits opening to the exterior. In fish, the gills are located on both sides of the pharynx.

(C) uberon-0000207.description: (C): A chitinous extracellular secretion of the four underlying cone cells and the pigment cells.

(C) uberon-0000210.description: (C): In humans: bone forming side and roof of cranium. Each bone is irregularly quadrilateral in form, and has two surfaces, four borders, and four angles.

(C) uberon-0004339.description: (C): Upper part of skull, consisting of parietals, frontals, post-parietals, and in some species the squamosal and a portion of the alisphenoid.

(C) uberon-0000212.description: (C): A specialized claw or nail on the foot of certain primates, used for personal grooming.

(C) uberon-0001705.description: (C): A horn-like keratin structure covering the dorsal aspect of the terminal phalanges of fingers and toes[WP].

(C) uberon-0000218.description: (C): A neural arch that is part of a vertebral bone 2.

(C) uberon-0003861.description: (C): Posterior part of a vertebra that consists of a pair of pedicles and a pair of laminae, and supports seven processes: four articular processes, two transverse processes one spinous process[WP]. ZFA: A neural arch encloses the neural canal and typically meets its partner to form a neural spine.

(C) uberon-0000221.description: (C): A craniometric point on the posterior root of the zygomatic process of the temporal bone directly above the auricular point.

(C) uberon-0006983.description: (C): Non-material anatomical entity of zero dimension, which forms a boundary of an anatomical line or surface.

(C) uberon-0004655.description: (C): The zygomatic process of the temporal bone is a long, arched process projecting from the lower part of the squamous portion of the temporal bone. It articulates with the zygomatic bone. This process is at first directed lateralward, its two surfaces looking upward and downward; it then appears as if twisted inward upon itself, and runs forward, its surfaces now looking medialward and lateralward.

(C) uberon-0000301.description: (C): A closed space between the embryo and the amnion which contains the amniotic fluid and is formed by the fusion of the parts of the anterior and posterior amniotic folds.

(C) uberon-0009742.description: (C): The cavity of the developing embryo that is formed within the epiblast tissue prior to the closing of the proamniotic canal by the amniotic folds.

(C) uberon-0000303.description: (C): An adductor muscle that attaches to the hip and femur. In humans, it is a part of the adductor group of the thigh, that as the name suggests adducts the thigh. The adductor longus muscle forms the medial wall of the femoral triangle[WP, generalized].

(C) uberon-0004252.description: (C): Any muscle organ that is part of a hindlimb stylopod (upper leg)[Automatically generated definition].

(C) uberon-0001275.description: (C): A paired endochondral bone making up the anteroventral region of the tripartite pelvic girdle forming part of the ventral edge of the acetabulum. The origin site of many proximal hindlimb muscles. [PHENOSCAPE:ad].

(C) uberon-0000981.description: (C): Endochondral longbone connecting the pelvic girdle with posterior zeugopodium skeleton.[VSAO, modified].

(C) uberon-0003262.description: (C): A mesenchyme that is part of a amnion.
