(C) uberon-0009976.description: (C): An intrinsic circulatory network that transports hormones from the median eminence of the hypothalamus to the adenohypophysis.

(C) uberon-0009977.description: (C): Predeciduous teeth present at birth. They may be well formed and normal or may represent hornified epithelial structures without roots. They are found on the gingivae over the crest of the ridge and arise from accessory buds of the dental lamina ahead of the deciduous buds or from buds of the accessory dental lamina. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992).

(C) uberon-0009979.description: (C): An articular prominence of a bone, typically present in pairs, resembling a pair of knuckles. Examples: Condyle of humerus, condyle of femur.

(C) uberon-0009985.description: (C): The lateral condyle is one of the two projections on the lower extremity of femur. It is the more prominent and is the broader both in its antero-posterior and transverse diameters.

(C) uberon-0009986.description: (C): The lateral epicondyle of the femur, smaller and less prominent than the medial epicondyle, gives attachment to the fibular collateral ligament of the knee-joint. Directly below it is a small depression from which a smooth well-marked groove curves obliquely upward and backward to the posterior extremity of the condyle.

(C) uberon-0009987.description: (C): The medial epicondyle of the femur is a bony protrusion located on the medial side of the bone's distal end. Located above the medial condyle, it bears an elevation, the adductor tubercle, which serves for the attachment of the superficial part, or 'tendinous insertion', of the adductor magnus. This tendinous part here forms an intermuscular septum which forms the medial separation between the thigh's flexors and extensors. Behind it, and proximally to the medial condyle is a rough impression which gives origin to the medial head of the Gastrocnemius.

(C) uberon-0009988.description: (C): The distal end of the humerus, including the trochlea, capitulum and the olecranon, coronoid and radial fossae.

(C) uberon-0009990.description: (C): The medial condyle is the medial portion of the upper extremity of tibia. It is the site of insertion for the Semimembranosus muscle[WP].

(C) uberon-0009992.description: (C): The ganglion found on the root of each cranial nerve, containing the cell bodies of afferent (sensory) neurons.

(C) uberon-0009993.description: (C): A chorionic villus that is a solid outgrowth of the cytotrophoblast that protrudes into the syncytiotrophoblast.

(C) uberon-0009994.description: (C): A chorionic villus that is has a core of loose connective tissue, which in humans grows into the primary villi about the third week of development.

(C) uberon-0009995.description: (C): Tertiary chorionic villi contain embryonic blood vessels that develop from mesenchymal cells in the loose connective tissue core. These blood vessels connect up with vessels that develop in the chorion and connecting stalk and begin to circulate embryonic blood about the third week of development in humans.

(C) uberon-0010001.description: (C): A small cluster of cells of various types which form a discrete structure, largely delimited by a morphological boundary and whose components work together to make the whole structure capable of a specific function.

(C) uberon-0014732.description: (C): An anatomical structure consisting of multiple cell cluster organs, that has a largely bona-fide boundary and that does not contain portions of tissue.

(C) uberon-0010002.description: (C): Corpuscular, organoid structures composed of PNECs, found as distinctive innervated clusters only within intrapulmonary airways, where they appear concentrated at airway branch points; NEBs reach from the basement membrane to the airway lumen and are thought to function as oxygen sensors.

(C) uberon-8600018.description: (C): A regulatory system of the body that integrates the nervous system and the endocrine system. This system is formed by specialized neuroendocrine cells located mainly in the nervous system and neuroendocrine glands. However, they can also be found as either single cells or small clusters of cells dispersed throughout the surface epithelium of different tissues. The neuroendocrine system functions through the release of neurotransmitters and neurohormones, enabling communication between the endocrine and nervous systems to govern vitally important processes that include growth, reproduction, metabolism and energy homeostasis, electrolyte and water balance, and responses to stress.

(C) uberon-0010005.description: (C): The vascularized and branched structures arising from the rodent trophoblast-derived epithelium that allow an increase its surface area for the efficient exchange of nutrients and wastes between the maternal and fetal circulation.

(C) uberon-0010006.description: (C): The spaces of the placenta occupied by maternal blood, into which the fetal labyrinth villi project.

(C) uberon-0010007.description: (C): The spaces of the placenta occupied by fetal blood, primarily within the fetal labyrinth villi.

(C) uberon-0010008.description: (C): Round structure consisting of chorionic villi[PMID]. A separation of the decidua basalis of the placenta, separated by placental septa. Each cotyledon consists of a main stem of a chorionic villus as well as its branches and subbranches. The cotyledons receive fetal blood from chorionic vessels, which branch off cotyledon vessels into the cotyledons, which, in turn, branch into capillaries. The cotyledons are surrounded by maternal blood, which can exchange oxygen and nutrients with the fetal blood in the capillaries[WP].

(C) uberon-0010014.description: (C): An elongate paired tissue ventral to the kidneys and partialy enveloping the anterior gonads in Elasmobranchii. Apparently important to the immune system.

(C) uberon-0010015.description: (C): The ventralmost of the two bodies of the elasmopbranch hemopoietic organ betweean the esophageal mucosa and muscularis.

(C) uberon-0010016.description: (C): Coiled structure in the lumen of the small intestine that increases the length of the route through the digestive tract.[WP,cjm,Kardong].

(C) uberon-0010017.description: (C): A series of crescentic folds of mucous membrane somewhat spirally arranged on the interior of the gallbladder and continuing into the cystic duct.

(C) uberon-0010018.description: (C): The spiral valve alternately blocks & unblocks the entrances to the left and right pulmonary arches (sending unoxygenated blood to the skin & lungs).

(C) uberon-0010034.description: (C): A single midventral prominence deriving from the ventral bases of pharyngeal arches 2, 3 and 4 - provides the covering of the posterior of the tongue //The furcula is at first separated from the tuberculum impar by a depression, but later by a ridge, the copula, formed by the forward growth and fusion of the ventral ends of the second, third, and part of the fourth branchial arches[WP].

(C) uberon-0010049.description: (C): Oral gland in reptiles situated immediately above the lip.

(C) uberon-0010050.description: (C): Oral gland in reptiles situated immediately below the lip.

(C) uberon-0010051.description: (C): The dosralmost of the two bodies of the elasmopbranch hemopoietic organ betweean the esophageal mucosa and muscularis.

(C) uberon-0010066.description: (C): The tympanic part of the temporal bone is a curved plate of bone lying below the squama and in front of the mastoid process.

(C) uberon-0010076.description: (C): Tissue cavity consisting of intercommunicating trabecular spaces in the cancellous bone.

(C) uberon-0010137.description: (C): A polarized epithelium is an epithelium where the epithelial sheet is oriented with respect to the planar axis.

(C) uberon-0010146.description: (C): The Skene's ducts are a pair of ducts leading from the Skene's glands to the surface of the vulva, to the left and right of the urethral opening.

(C) uberon-0010148.description: (C): A gelatinous secretion used in the mating of some species. It is deposited by a male into a female genital tract and later hardens into a plug or glues the tract together.

(C) uberon-0035784.description: (C): A portion of semen in a coagulated state.

(C) uberon-0011831.description: (C): A duct that is part of a vestibular gland.

(C) uberon-0010151.description: (C): A duct that is part of a bulbo-urethral gland.

(C) uberon-0010154.description: (C): The inner mucosa of the fourth stomach chamber of a ruminant produces rennet.
(C) uberon-0010154.label_original: inner lining mucosa of the abomasum

(C) uberon-0010156.description: (C): The Sphenofrontal suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the frontal bone.

(C) uberon-0010157.description: (C): The Sphenoparietal suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the parietal bone.

(C) uberon-0010158.description: (C): The Sphenozygomatic suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the zygomatic bone.

(C) uberon-0010159.description: (C): The occipitomastoid suture is the cranial suture between the occipital bone and the mastoid portion of the temporal bone. It is continuous with the lambdoidal suture.

(C) uberon-0010160.description: (C): An anatomical cavity that surrounded_by a lymphatic vessel.

(C) uberon-0010163.description: (C): The eyebrow is an area of thick, delicate hairs above the eye that follows the shape of the lower margin of the brow ridges. Their main function is to protect the eye, but they are also important to human communication and facial expression. It is not uncommon for people to modify their eyebrows by means of hair addition or removal, make up, or piercings.

(C) uberon-0010165.description: (C): A collection of hairs that is part of a face.

(C) uberon-0010164.description: (C): An anatomical cluster that composed_primarily_of a strand of hair.

(C) uberon-0014382.description: (C): A collection of hairs that is part of a craniocervical region.
(C) uberon-0014382.label_original: collection of hairs on head or neck

(C) uberon-0010171.description: (C): A strand of hair that is part of a face.

(C) uberon-0010167.description: (C): The collection of hair that grows on the chin, cheeks and neck of human beings. Usually, only pubescent or adult males are able to grow beards. However, women with hirsutism may develop a beard. When differentiating between upper and lower facial hair, a beard specifically includes the moustache, which refers to hair above the upper lip and around it.

(C) uberon-0010168.description: (C): A collection of hair on face that is part of a eyelash.

(C) uberon-0010169.description: (C): Facial hair grown on the outer surface of the upper lip. It may or may not be accompanied by a type of beard, a facial hair style grown and cropped to cover most of the lower half of the face.

(C) uberon-0016446.description: (C): A strand of hair that is part of a head.

(C) uberon-0010173.description: (C): The point in the ascending aorta where the aortic sinuses end and the aorta becomes a tubular structure.

(C) uberon-0010174.description: (C): A phagocytic sleeve that is part of a sheathed arteriole of the spleen, and is sometimes referred to as a splenic ellipsoid. It is a spindle-shaped thickening in the walls of the second part of the arterial branches forming the penicilli in the spleen.

(C) uberon-0010175.description: (C): A vein or veins draining a bone and emerging from a nutrient foramen.

(C) uberon-0010176.description: (C): The medullary or nutrient artery, usually accompanied by one or two veins, sends branches upward and downward to the bone marrow, which ramify in the medullary membrane, and give twigs to the adjoining canals.

(C) uberon-0010181.description: (C): The straight venules of kidney are branches from the plexuses at the apices of the medullary pyramids, formed by the terminations of the arteriae rectae. They run outward in a straight course between the tubes of the medullary substance, and joining, as above stated, the interlobular veins, form venous arcades; these in turn unite and form veins which pass along the sides of the pyramids. Contains fenestrated capillaries.

(C) uberon-0012249.description: (C): The part of the cervix uteri that protrudes into the vagina and is lined with stratified squamous epithelium.

(C) uberon-0010185.description: (C): A structure formed from the primary sex cords in females, counterpart of the rete testis in males.

(C) uberon-0010193.description: (C): A portal vein that empties into capillaries within the kidneys.

(C) uberon-0010195.description: (C): A portal system that transports blood returning from capillary beds within tail or hindlimbs through paired renal portal veins that empty into capillaries within the kidneys.

(C) uberon-0010197.description: (C): The initial part of the entire common carotid artery ending with the point where the artery bifurcates into an external carotid artery and an internal carotid artery.

(C) uberon-0010198.description: (C): A segment of the embryonic dorsal aorta between points of juncture with the third and fourth arch arteries; it regresses early in development to allow the carotid axis to take its definitive appearance.

(C) uberon-0010205.description: (C): One of the several veins that drain the mesencephalon; the posterior ones are tributaries to the great cerebral vein; the lateral ones are tributaries to the basal vein. The main veins are: pontomesencephalic vein [TA] (vena pontomesencephalica [TA]), interpeduncular veins [TA] (venae interpedunculares [TA]), intercollicular vein [TA] (vena intercollicularis [TA]), and lateral mesencephalic vein [TA] (vena mesencephalica lateralis [TA])[MedLex]. The major vein of the midbrain, which crosses the midbrain medially to meet it's partner the mesencephalic artery[XAO].

(C) uberon-0010207.description: (C): A fold of the mucous membrane of the conjunctiva in many animals. At rest, it is hidden in the medial canthus. It can extend to cover part or all of the cornea to help clean the cornea.

(C) uberon-0010209.description: (C): The plica semilunaris is a small fold of bulbar conjunctiva on the medial canthus of the eye. It is loose, so that eye movements are not restricted.

(C) uberon-0010210.description: (C): A semisolid gelatinous mass of coagulated blood that consists of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets entrapped in a fibrin network.

(C) uberon-0010211.description: (C): Highly vascularized tissue that replaces the initial fibrin clot in a wound. Vascularization is by ingrowth of capillary endothelium from the surrounding vasculature. The tissue is also rich in fibroblasts (that will eventually produce the fibrous tissue) and leucocytes.

(C) uberon-0010215.description: (C): Paired primordial elevations, on either side of the embryonic larynx, within which the arytenoid cartilages are formed.

(C) uberon-0010223.description: (C): A pupil that is part of a left eye.

(C) uberon-0010224.description: (C): A pupil that is part of a right eye.

(C) uberon-0010228.description: (C): A portion of organism substance that is produced a rumen.

(C) uberon-0010229.description: (C): A muscular structure at the lower end of the esophagus that, when closed, forms a tube allowing milk to go directly into the abomasum. (This prevents milk from being fermented or soured by the ruminal microorganisms).

(C) uberon-0010233.description: (C): The connective tissue that supports the lobules and follicles of the thyroid gland.

(C) uberon-0010234.description: (C): The palatopharyngeus or palatopharyngeal or pharyngopalatinus muscle is a long, fleshy fasciculus, narrower in the middle than at either end, forming, with the mucous membrane covering its surface, the palatopharyngeal arch.

(C) uberon-0010235.description: (C): The musculus uvulae (azygos uvulae) is a muscle of the soft palate. It arises from the posterior nasal spine of the palatine bones and from the palatine aponeurosis. It descends to be inserted into the uvula and functions to move and shape it. It is innervated by the pharyngeal branch of the vagus nerve via the pharyngeal plexus[WP].

(C) uberon-0014780.description: (C): Attached to the posterior border of the hard palate is a thin, firm fibrous lamella called the palatine aponeurosis, which supports the muscles and gives strength to the soft palate. It is thicker above than below, where it becomes very thin and difficult to define. Laterally it is continuous with the pharyngeal aponeurosis. It serves as the insertion for the Tensor veli palatini and Levator veli palatini, and the origin for the Musculus uvulae, Palatopharyngeus, and Palatoglossus. It provides support for the soft palate.

(C) uberon-0010238.description: (C): A fleshy protuberance at the pylorus of some species such as ruminants and pigs, that projects into the lumen of the pyloric canal.

(C) uberon-0010239.description: (C): A variant of the ascending colon in ruminants and pigs.

(C) uberon-0010240.description: (C): A salivary gland best developed in carnivores; located above the zygomatic arch and below the eye. Enlargement or mucocele of the gland causes exophthalmos.

(C) uberon-0010242.description: (C): The racemose, mucous or serous glands in the submucous tissue of the cheeks.

(C) uberon-0010244.description: (C): A tapetum lucidum that is part of the choroid. The choroidal tapetum lucidum lies immediately adjacent to the choriocapillaris and external to the retinal epithelium.

(C) uberon-0010245.description: (C): A tapetum lucidum that is part of the retina, within the cytoplasm of the retinal epithelium.

(C) uberon-0010246.description: (C): A choroid tapetum lucidum that is made of a palisade of cells containing stacks of flat hexagonal crystals of guanine.

(C) uberon-0010247.description: (C): A choroid tapetum lucidum that consists of layers of cells containing organized, highly refractive crystals. These crystals are diverse in shape and makeup.

(C) uberon-0010248.description: (C): A choroid tapetum lucidum that is an array of extracellular fibers.

(C) uberon-0010249.description: (C): The posterior meningeal artery are small vessels which are branches of the ascending pharyngeal artery which supply the dura mater. It passes through the mastoid foramen before entering the cranium via the jugular foramen.

(C) uberon-0010251.description: (C): A meningeal branch to the dura mater arising from the anterior ethmoidal artery.

(C) uberon-0010250.description: (C): The middle meningeal artery is typically the third branch of the first part (retromandibular part) of the maxillary artery; one of the two terminal branches of the external carotid artery. After branching off the maxillary artery in the infratemporal fossa, it runs through the foramen spinosum to supply the dura mater and the calvaria. The middle meningeal artery is the largest of the three (paired) arteries which supply the meninges, the others being the anterior meningeal artery and the posterior meningeal artery. In approximately half of subjects it branches into an accessory meningeal artery. The middle meningeal artery runs beneath the pterion. It is vulnerable to injury at this point, where the skull is thin. Rupture of the artery may give rise to an epidural hematoma.

(C) uberon-0010263.description: (C): Embryoid bodies are structures resembling embryos, occurring in several types of germ cell tumors.

(C) uberon-0010266.description: (C): Digestive gland of crustaceans with functions approximately analogous to liver and pancreas of vertebrates - enzyme secretion, food absorption and storage.

(C) uberon-0010268.description: (C): Missing definition for term UBERON:0010268. Please replace it using linked reference.

(C) uberon-0010271.description: (C): Cranial nerve VI innervated; ventral and posterior to the eye.

(C) uberon-0010283.description: (C): The cul-de-sac enclosed between the limbs of the inverted U of the venous mesocardium lies behind the left atrium.[WP,unvetted].

(C) uberon-0010289.description: (C): Circular cartilage ringing the posterior portion of the eye in the sclera. Supports the eye.

(C) uberon-0010292.description: (C): The episclera is the outermost layer of the sclera. It is composed of loose, fibrous, elastic tissue and attaches to Tenon's capsule. A vascular plexus is found between the conjunctiva and the sclera consisting of two layers of vessels, the superficial episcleral vessels and the deep episcleral vessels.

(C) uberon-0010293.description: (C): On the external surface of the optic choroid is a thin membrane, the suprachoroid lamina, composed of delicate non-vascular lamellae-each lamella consisting of a network of fine elastic fibers among which are branched pigment cells.

(C) uberon-0010302.description: (C): A single extraembryonic epithelium, which closes the germband dorsally.

(C) uberon-0010307.description: (C): The space formed by the junction of the bulbar and palpebral portions of the conjunctiva, that of the upper lid being the superior conjunctival fornix (fornix conjunctivae superior) and that of the lower lid, the inferior conjunctival fornix (fornix conjunctivae inferior); the fornix is loose and flexible, allowing the free movement of the lids and eyeball.

(C) uberon-0010308.description: (C): Scleral element located at the posterior pole of the scleral cartilage surrounding the foramen through which the optic nerve fibers pass. the internal architecture of this bone reveals a cancellous marrow cavity with fatty tissue.

(C) uberon-0010309.description: (C): An ossified element investing the upper eyelid.

(C) uberon-0010310.description: (C): Thin cartilage element that stiffens the nictitating membrane.

(C) uberon-0010311.description: (C): A sesamoid bone that lies adjacent to the tendon of one of the muscles responsible for adducting the nictitating membrane (the pyramidal nictitating muscle).

(C) uberon-0010317.label_original: obsolete germ layer / neural crest derived structure

(C) uberon-0010325.description: (C): Cranial skeleton derived from neural crest cells.

(C) uberon-0010326.description: (C): Permanent cartilage structure projecting from the site of origin of the recti muscles. Supports eyeball and aids rotation.

(C) uberon-0010327.label_original: obsolete early digestive tract associated mesenchyme

(C) uberon-0010328.description: (C): Mesenchyme that is part of a limb bud.

(C) uberon-0010356.description: (C): A primary ossification center is the first area of a bone to start ossifying. It usually appears during prenatal development in the central part of each developing bone. In long bones the primary centers occur in the diaphysis/shaft and in irregular bones the primary centers occur usually in the body of the bone. Most bones have only one primary center (e.g. all long bones) but some irregular bones such as the os coxa (hip) and vertebrae have multiple primary centers.

(C) uberon-0010357.description: (C): A secondary ossification center is the area of ossification that appears after the primary ossification center has already appeared - most of which appear during the postnatal and adolescent years. Most bones have more than one secondary ossification center. In long bones, the secondary centres appear in the epiphyses.

(C) uberon-0010366.description: (C): A vasculature that is part of a conjunctiva.

(C) uberon-0010367.description: (C): A vein that is part of a conjunctiva.

(C) uberon-0010379.description: (C): The superior tarsal muscle is a smooth muscle adjoining the levator palpebrae superioris muscle that helps to raise the upper eyelid.

(C) uberon-0010380.description: (C): The neurons that innervate the esophagus, stomach, small and large bowel.

(C) uberon-0010384.description: (C): An anatomical space that is enclosed by a hypopharynx.

(C) uberon-0010386.description: (C): A lymphoid follicle that is part of a Peyer's patch.

(C) uberon-0010387.description: (C): The Peyer's patch area normally occupied by T lymphocytes.

(C) uberon-0010389.description: (C): A bone which corresponds to the inner plate of the pterygoid process of the human skull, but which, in all vertebrates below mammals, is not connected with the posterior nares, but serves to connect the palatine bones with the point of suspension of the lower jaw.

(C) uberon-0010391.description: (C): The subserous connective tissue of the pelvic floor of the supracervical portion of the uterus. The parametrium extends laterally between the layers of the broad ligament.

(C) uberon-0010395.description: (C): An unstimulated network of follicular dendritic cells and small resting B cells in the lymph node cortex.

(C) uberon-0010748.description: (C): A lymphoid follicle that is part of a lymph node.

(C) uberon-0010396.description: (C): Lymphatic vessel that enters the lymph node. The afferent lymph vessels enter at all parts of the periphery of the lymph node, and after branching and forming a dense plexus in the substance of the capsule, open into the lymph sinuses of the cortical part. In doing this they lose all their coats except their endothelial lining, which is continuous with a layer of similar cells lining the lymph paths.

(C) uberon-0010397.description: (C): Lymphatic vessel that exits the lymph node. The efferent lymphatic vessel commences from the lymph sinuses of the medullary portion of the lymph nodes and leave the lymph nodes either to veins or greater nodes. Efferent lymphatic vessels are also found in the thymus and spleen. This is in contrast to afferent lymphatic vessels, which are found only in lymph nodes.

(C) uberon-0010398.description: (C): The border region surrounding the spleen B cell follicles and the periarteriolar lymphoid sheath that separates it from the marginal zone that mediates lymphocyte entry into the white pulp from the blood.

(C) uberon-0010401.description: (C): A blood vessel surrounded by the periarteriolar lymphoid sheath that connects the trabecular artery to the trabecular vein.

(C) uberon-0010402.description: (C): Any layer of the epidermis that is superior to the stratum basale.

(C) uberon-0010403.description: (C): The part of the future brain that is derived from the mantle layer of the neural tube.

(C) uberon-0010404.description: (C): A cell layer below the ependyma in the lateral ventricles of the brain. This region contains adult neural stem cells which have the potential to generate new neurons and glial cells via neurogenesis. It is an adult version of the embryonic forebrain germinal zone.

(C) uberon-0010405.description: (C): Column of motor neurons which innervate muscles in the limb; motor neurons in the lateral motor column are further organized into pools, each of which innervates a specific muscle in the limb.

(C) uberon-0010406.description: (C): Nerve fibers that utilize acetylcholine as a neurotransmitter to the intestinal system.

(C) uberon-0010408.description: (C): The angular artery is the terminal part of the facial artery; it ascends to the medial angle of the eye's orbit, imbedded in the fibers of the angular head of the Quadratus labii superioris, and accompanied by the angular vein.

(C) uberon-0010410.description: (C): Encapsulated adipose tissue found in the groin.

(C) uberon-0010411.description: (C): Encapsulated adipose tissue found on the dorsal side of the peritoneum.

(C) uberon-0010412.description: (C): Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the epididymis.

(C) uberon-0010413.description: (C): Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the extension of the subserous coat of the uterus laterally between the layers of the broad ligament.

(C) uberon-0014394.description: (C): Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the uterus.

(C) uberon-0015143.description: (C): Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the mesentery.

(C) uberon-0010414.description: (C): Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the fold of peritoneal tissue that extends from the stomach to the posterior abdominal wall after associating with the transverse colon.

(C) uberon-0010415.description: (C): One of the discrete functional units of the somatosensory cortex that processes tactile information derived from the vibrissae.

(C) uberon-0010416.description: (C): A part of the lymph node cortex in which B lymphocytes home to primary follicles to survey follicular dendritic cells (FDCs); antigen stimulated B cells proliferate and differentiate within the follicles forming distinctive germinal centers.

(C) uberon-0010417.description: (C): The paracortex and interfollicular cortex of the lymph node in which T lymphocytes home to survey dendritic cells.

(C) uberon-0010419.description: (C): One of the tubular invaginations of the epidermis enclosing the hair roots and from which grow the vibrissae located on the muzzle and face of many species.

(C) uberon-0010420.description: (C): A part of the secondary follicle in which naive B cells reside along with some helper T cells, macrophages and follicular dendritic cells; these are displaced by the expanding germinal centre and form a 'mantle' around it.
(C) uberon-0010420.label_original: lymph node germinal center mantle zone

(C) uberon-0010755.description: (C): The part of the secondary follicle that surrounds the germinal center.

(C) uberon-0010421.description: (C): The area of the (spleen) secondary B follicle that surrounds the germinal center and harbors the small recirculating B lymphocytes.

(C) uberon-0010423.description: (C): A primary nodular lymphoid tissue that is part of a tonsil.

(C) uberon-0010426.description: (C): Opening/conduit between the nasal cavity and the oropharynx via the roof of the mouth.

(C) uberon-0010496.description: (C): A narrow, elongated muscle of the rotator cuff.

(C) uberon-0010505.description: (C): The outermost of the two layers of the cranial dura mater which normally always adheres to the periosteum of the bones of the cranial vault.

(C) uberon-0010507.description: (C): The intracranial dura mater, consisting of two layers: the outer periosteal layer which normally always adheres to the periosteum of the bones of the cranial vault; and the inner meningeal layer which in most places is fused with the outer. The two layers separate to accommodate meningeal vessels and large venous (dural) sinuses. The meningeal layer is also involved in the formation of the various dural folds, such as the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli and is comparable to and continuous with the dural mater of the spinal cord. The cranial epidural space is then a potential space between the bone and the combined periosteum/periosteal layer of the dura mater realised only pathologically and is neither continuous with or comparable to the vertebral epidural space.

(C) uberon-0010506.description: (C): The inner layer of the dura mater surrounding the brain. It is mostly fused with the outer layer, the endocranium that is adherent to the inner aspect of the cranial bones. These two layers form the dura mater. The latter covers and protects the brain and the spinal cord.

(C) uberon-0010509.description: (C): A strand of hair that is part of a coat of hair.

(C) uberon-0010510.description: (C): A truncal hair that has a single constriction and bend about midway along the hair shaft, and contains two or more air cells in the medulla.

(C) uberon-0010511.description: (C): A truncal hairs that is straight, but shorter than a guard hair, and contain two or more air cells in the medulla.

(C) uberon-0010512.description: (C): A long, straight truncal hair that contains two air cells in the medulla[MP]. A strand of hair from the top layer consisting of longer, often coarser, straight shafts of hair that stick out through the underfur. This is usually the visible layer for most mammals and contains most of the pigmentation.

(C) uberon-0010513.description: (C): A truncal hair that has two or more sharp bends with diameter constrictions at the bends, and contain one air cell in the medulla.

(C) uberon-0016447.description: (C): A strand of hair that is part of a trunk.

(C) uberon-0010514.description: (C): A strand of hair from the fine underhair of the coat.

(C) uberon-0010515.description: (C): A layer of transparent, immovable disc-shaped skin or scale covering the eyes of some animals for protection, especially in animals without eyelids. The brille has evolved from a fusion of the upper and lower eyelids.

(C) uberon-0010516.description: (C): A male anatomical structure found some groups of animals, used in mating. Male cartilaginous fish have claspers formed from the posterior portion of their pelvic fin which serve as intromittent organs used to channel semen into the female's cloaca during mating. The act of mating in some fish including sharks usually includes one of the claspers raised to allow water into the siphon through a specific orifice. The clasper is then inserted into the vagina, where it opens like an umbrella to anchor its position. The siphon then begins to contract expelling water and sperm. Male chimaeras have cephalic claspers on their heads, which are thought to aid in holding the female during mating.

(C) uberon-0010517.description: (C): A mace-like spiny-headed rod found on the mid-dorsal surface of heads of male Holocephali. Thought to aid in holding the female during copulation.

(C) uberon-0010518.description: (C): The rod-like extension of the medial portion of the pelvic fin in male Elasmobranchii and Holocephali. Claspers are used as intromittent organs (not in clasping), the grooves on their facing surfaces together forming a tube for the transmission of sperm when the claspers are held together. The anterior proximal opening is called the apopyle, the posterior distal opening the rhipidion.

(C) uberon-0010519.description: (C): An electric organ that is part of a tail.

(C) uberon-0010520.description: (C): An electric organ that is part of a head.

(C) uberon-0010524.description: (C): A muscle located in the lower limb that arises from the lower third of the anterior surface of the fibula; from the lower part of the interosseous membrane; and from an intermuscular septum between it and the peroneus brevis and inserted into the dorsal surface of the base of the metatarsal bone of the 5th digit. It is innervated by the deep fibular nerve. Its action is that of weak dorsiflexion of the ankle joint and to evert the foot at the ankle joint.

(C) uberon-0010526.description: (C): The peroneus brevis muscle (or fibularis brevis) lies under cover of the peroneus longus, and is a shorter and smaller muscle.

(C) uberon-0010540.description: (C): A pre-cartilage condensation that has the potential to develop into a tarsal bone.

(C) uberon-0010543.description: (C): The subdivision of the skeleton that consists of all the skeletal elements at the distalmost end of the autopodium - i.e. the bones of the digits or their cartilaginous precursors[VSAO,modified].

(C) uberon-0012150.description: (C): A subdivision of the autopod skeleton consisting of both acropodial skeleon and metapodial skeleton, but excluding the mesopodial/basopodial skeleton.
