(C) uberon-0035933.description: (C): The junction of the precentral gyrus and postcentral gyrus on the medial surface of the cerebral cortex. It lies across the boundary between the frontal lobe and the parietal lobe.

(C) uberon-0035935.description: (C): Part of the optic radiation which sweeps back on itself into the temporal lobe, just lateral to the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle.

(C) uberon-0035937.description: (C): The arcuate fasciculus (Latin, curved bundle) is the neural pathway connecting the posterior part of the temporoparietal junction with the frontal cortex in the brain and is now considered as part of the Superior longitudinal fasciculus.

(C) uberon-0035941.description: (C): The thickening of the lower surface of the tectorial membrane into which the hair bundles of the outer hair cells are embedded.

(C) uberon-0035942.description: (C): The space between the upper jaw skeleton and lower jaw skeleton (including teeth) that is formed when when biting.
(C) uberon-0035942.label_original: space between upper and lower jaws

(C) uberon-0035943.description: (C): A temporal boundary connecting two life cycle stages that follow in immediate succession. A temporal boundary is an abstract, instantaneous entity.

(C) uberon-0035944.description: (C): A life cycle temporal boundary that marks the end of the life cycle of the organism.

(C) uberon-0035945.description: (C): A life cycle temporal boundary that marks the start of the life cycle of the organism.

(C) uberon-0035946.description: (C): A life cycle temporal boundary that marks the start of the neonate stage of the organism.

(C) uberon-0035955.description: (C): Historically the term cerebrum has been used for several different parts of the CNS including the whole brain, the cerebral hemispheres and the sum of cerebral cortex and adjacent cerebral white matter. A thorough discussion of the definitional history is to be found in Anthoney-1994.

(C) uberon-0035957.description: (C): The posteriormost orbital pillar, in front of the otic capsule.

(C) uberon-0035958.description: (C): The anteriormost orbital pillar, in front of the otic capsule.

(C) uberon-0035961.description: (C): 1: The trunk of an elephant; also: any long flexible snout. 2: Any of various elongated or extensible tubular processes as the sucking organ of a butterfly of the oral region of an invertebrate.

(C) uberon-0035962.description: (C): Supravaginal portion of cervix: the part of the cervix uteri that does not protrude into the vagina.

(C) uberon-0035963.description: (C): Epithelial lining fluid forms a thin fluid layer that covers the mucosa of the alveoli, the small airways, and the large airways.

(C) uberon-0035967.description: (C): The mucous membrane apical to the attached gingiva.

(C) uberon-0035964.description: (C): The promontory of the tympanic cavity, better known as the cochlear promontory is a rounded hollow prominence, formed by the projection outward of the first turn of the cochlea. It is placed between the fenestrae, and is furrowed on its surface by small grooves, for the lodgement of branches of the tympanic plexus. A minute spicule of bone frequently connects the promontory to the pyramidal eminence.

(C) uberon-0035966.description: (C): The perforated part of the sclera through which pass the axons of the retinal ganglion cells.

(C) uberon-0035968.description: (C): A receptor in the transitional zone between mucous membrane and skin.

(C) uberon-0035971.description: (C): Division of subicular cortex characterized by projections from the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus and to a lesser extent the anteroventral nucleus, bordered ventrally and laterally by the presubiculum and dorsally and medially by the retrosplenial granular a cortex.. The border is characterized by an abrupt change in the cyto- and chemoarchitecture.

(C) uberon-0035972.description: (C): A group of nerve cells that bridges the midline of the thalamus between the anterodorsal nucleus of the thalamus of the left and right sides. According to Crosby (1962), it is more developed and consistently present in rodents than in primates (adapted from Brain Info).

(C) uberon-0035973.description: (C): Distinct cell group in caudoventral regions of the pontine periventricular gray, adjacent to the ventromedial border of the caudal dorsal tegmental nucleus.

(C) uberon-0035975.label_original: intergeniculate leaflet of the lateral geniculate complex

(C) uberon-0035976.description: (C): A small cluster of neurons in the pontine reticular formation in some mammals, containing the majority of motoneurons innervating thenretractor bulbi muscles of the eye.

(C) uberon-0035977.description: (C): A group of cells near the surface of the brain between the supraoptic nucleus and the cortical amygdalar nucleus in the rat ( Swanson-1998 ) and the mouse ( Paxinos-2001 ). It is one of five subdivisions of the medial amygdalar nucleus.
(C) uberon-0035977.label_original: bed nucleus of the accessory olfactory tract

(C) uberon-0035999.description: (C): Collections of neurons in the central nervous system that have been demonstrated by histochemical fluorescence to contain the neurotransmitter dopamine ( Fuxe-1970 ).

(C) uberon-0036007.description: (C): A group of cells that fluoresce for dopamine and are distributed in clusters that, in the primate, are ventral and medial to the mammillothalamic tract of the hypothalamus; a few extend into the reuniens nucleus of the thalamus (Felten-1983). In the mouse A13 is located ventral to the mammillothalamic tract of the thalamus in the zona incerta (adapted from Brain Info).

body: [nucleus of the brachium of the inferior colliculus](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_0036012)
(C) uberon-0036012.label_original: nucleus of the brachium of the inferior colliculus

(C) uberon-0036015.description: (C): A yellowish pungent liquid that is a mixture of the castor sacs (an anal gland in the taxon Castoreum) and urine.

(C) uberon-0036016.description: (C): A sweet viscid material elaborated out of the nectar of flowers in the honey sac of various bees.

(C) uberon-0036018.description: (C): A mass of undigested parts of a bird's food that some bird species occasionally regurgitate from their proventriculus.

(C) uberon-0036019.description: (C): A non-glandular region of the anal wall in which castoreum is produced.

(C) uberon-0036066.description: (C): The endocardial cushion that forms on the ventral surface of the AV canal.

(C) uberon-0036067.description: (C): The endocardial cushion that forms on the dorsal surface of the AV canal.

(C) uberon-0036068.description: (C): The lower portion of the larynx, extending from just beneath the vocal cords down to the top of the trachea.

(C) uberon-0036069.description: (C): One of two longitudinal ridges that develop caudal to the pharynx and fuses to give rise to the tracheoesophageal septum.

(C) uberon-0036070.description: (C): The tracheoesophageal septum is formed from the tracheoesophageal folds which fuse in the midline to form a structure called tracheoesophageal septum. It divides the esophagus from the trachea. It divides the foregut tube into the laryngotracheal tube ventrally and esophagus dorsally. Developmental abnormalities can lead to a tracheoesophageal fistula.

(C) uberon-0036071.description: (C): A skeletal muscle found in crocodilians that is analogous to the diaphragm of mammals.

(C) uberon-0036144.description: (C): An infrequent rudimentary duct, or protrusion of the mucous membrane into the incisive canal, on either side of the anterior extremity of the nasal crest.

(C) uberon-0036145.description: (C): Macroscopic waste clearance system that utilizes a unique system of perivascular tunnels, formed by astroglial cells, to promote efficient elimination of soluble proteins and metabolites from the central nervous system.

(C) uberon-0036147.description: (C): A muscle that is part of an oral siphon.

(C) uberon-0036149.description: (C): Area of skin in the hypoastric region of the abdomen.

(C) uberon-0036151.description: (C): A placenta in which the chorionic sac meets the uterine endometrium over its entire surface. The villi of the chorion are distributed evenly throughout the surface of the chorion, and they extend into processes in the uterine endometrium.

(C) uberon-0036152.description: (C): A placenta in which the villi clumped together into circular patches called cotyledons. The fetal cotyledon meets with maternal regions called caruncles to form the placentome where maternal-fetal exchanges take place.

(C) uberon-0036153.description: (C): A placenta in which the chorionic villi have aggregated to form a broad band that circles about the center of the chorion. Such zones may be complete circles (such as those in dogs and cats) or incomplete (such as those in bears and seals). It is thought that zonary placentae form from diffuse placentae in which the villi at the ends regress, leaving only those in the center to function. At the edges of the zonary placenta is the hemophagous organ, which is green. The color is due to the degradation of hemoglobin into bilivirdin. This green organ provides iron for the developing fetus.

(C) uberon-0036154.description: (C): A placenta in which part of the chorion remains smooth, while the other part interacts with the endometrium to form the placenta. The maternal blood cells are in direct contact with the fetal chorion.

(C) uberon-0036161.description: (C): A placenta in which all three maternal layers are retained.

(C) uberon-0036162.description: (C): A placenta in which the only maternal layer retained is the uterine endothelium.

(C) uberon-0036163.description: (C): A placenta in which no maternal layers are retained.

(C) uberon-0036164.description: (C): A rostral part of the parahippocampal gyrus.

(C) uberon-0036167.description: (C): Sattler's layer is layer of medium diameter blood vessels of the choroid.

(C) uberon-0036172.description: (C): The Palmaris brevis is a thin, quadrilateral muscle, placed beneath the integument of the ulnar side of the hand. It arises by tendinous fasciculi from the transverse carpal ligament and palmar aponeurosis; the fleshy fibers are inserted into the skin on the ulnar border of the palm of the hand. The muscle is innervated by the superficial branch of the ulnar nerve, containing fibers from the eighth cervical and first thoracic nerves.

(C) uberon-0036173.description: (C): The Abductor minimi digiti (Abductor digiti quinti) is situated on the ulnar border of the palm of the hand. It arises from the pisiform bone and from the tendon of the Flexor carpi ulnaris, and ends in a flat tendon, which divides into two slips; one is inserted into the ulnar side of the base of the first phalanx of the little finger; the other into the ulnar border of the aponeurosis of the Extensor digiti quinti proprius. In case of polydactyly it may insert to the sixth finger instead, if there is one.

(C) uberon-0036174.description: (C): The flexor digiti minimi brevis is a muscle in the hand that flexes the little finger. It lies in the same plane as the abductor digiti minimi, on its radial side.
(C) uberon-0036174.label_original: flexor digiti minimi brevis of hand

(C) uberon-0036176.description: (C): The opponens minimi digiti (opponens digiti quinti in older texts) is a muscle in the hand. It is of a triangular form, and placed immediately beneath the palmaris brevis, abductor minimi digiti, and flexor brevis minimi digiti. It arises from the convexity of the hamulus of the hamate bone, and contiguous portion of the transverse carpal ligament; it is inserted into the whole length of the metacarpal bone of the little finger, along its ulnar margin.

(C) uberon-0036185.description: (C): The blood-testis barrier (abbreviated as BTB) is a physical barrier between the blood vessels and the seminiferous tubules of the animal testes. The barrier is formed by tight connections between the Sertoli cells, which are sustentacular cells (supporting cells) of the seminiferous tubules, and nourish the spermatogonia. The barrier prevents passage of cytotoxic agents (bodies or substances that are toxic to cells) into the seminiferous tubules.

(C) uberon-0036212.description: (C): A surface structure that is the narrowed downward continuation of the conchal space bounded anteriorly by the borders of the tragus, posteriorly by theantitragus, and along its lower lateral margins and inferior boundary by the connection between the first two.

(C) uberon-0036218.description: (C): The most anterior region of the forebrain including both the telencephalon and the hypothalamus in the prosomeric model.

(C) uberon-0036219.description: (C): A region of the pododerm above the hoof where hair growth ends.

(C) uberon-0036243.description: (C): Fluid that lines the vaginal walls that consists of multiple secretions that collect in the vagina from different glands.

(C) uberon-0036245.description: (C): Parenchymal tissue that consists of the alveoli, grape-like clusters where milk is stored, and branching ducts, which are tubular canals carrying gladular secretions.

(C) uberon-0036246.description: (C): The small synovial joint connecting the inclus and the stapes, located between the lenticular process on the long crus of the incus and the head of the stapes.

(C) uberon-0036248.description: (C): Any synovial joint that connects auditory ossicles.

(C) uberon-0036247.description: (C): The saddle-shaped synovial joint connecting the incus and the malleus.

(C) uberon-0036249.description: (C): The acellular membrane that forms the outer two thirds of the basilar membrane of the conchlea.
(C) uberon-0036249.label_original: zona pectinata of basilar membrane of cochlea

(C) uberon-0036252.description: (C): The space between the digits of the hand or foot.

(C) uberon-0036254.description: (C): A pear-shaped bony inlet comprising the most anterior and narrowest bony portion of the nasal airway.

(C) uberon-0036256.description: (C): An embryonic lymph sac that forms near the junction of the iliac veins with the posterior cardinal veins.

(C) uberon-0036259.description: (C): A lymphatic propulsor that lies tightly against the truncus arteriosus, the major outflow tract of the amphibian heart.

(C) uberon-0036261.description: (C): An extracoelomic lateral abdominal space that accumulates body fluid.

(C) uberon-0036262.description: (C): Any of the eight ligaments pertaining to the uterus including the anterior, posterior, lateral, sacro-uterine and round ligaments.

(C) uberon-0036263.description: (C): The upper part of the larynx, including the epiglottis; the area above the vocal cords.

(C) uberon-0036266.description: (C): The part of vertebra located between the inferior and superior articular processes of the facet joint.

(C) uberon-0036270.description: (C): An elastic ligament lying between the lateral pharyngeal muscles and the thyroglossus muscle.

(C) uberon-0036271.description: (C): A fetal membrane, part of the yolk sac, that appears during some placentation processes.

(C) uberon-0036272.description: (C): A non-vascular omphalopleure that supports uptake and metabolism of nutrients.

(C) uberon-0036273.description: (C): A vascular omphalopleure that is important for respiration.

(C) uberon-0036274.description: (C): The anterior and posterior borders of the tonsillar fossa. They are composed of muscle tissue.

(C) uberon-0036661.label_original: wall of ventricular system of brain

(C) uberon-0036658.label_original: wall of central canal of spinal cord

(C) uberon-0037461.description: (C): Very thin, soft, usually unpigmented, downy hair that is sometimes found on the body of a fetal or new-born human.

(C) uberon-0037462.description: (C): Short, thin, slight-colored, and barely noticeable hair that develops on most of a person's body during childhood.

(C) uberon-0037463.description: (C): Thick and long hair, as compared with vellus hair growing elsewhere.

(C) uberon-0037464.description: (C): The terminal hair that develops on the human body during and after puberty. It is differentiated from the head hair and less visible vellus hair, which is much finer and lighter in color.

(C) uberon-0037468.description: (C): The part of the human abdomen below the ribs and above the hips, often narrower than the areas above and below.

(C) uberon-0037494.description: (C): Gastric lymph node located around the cardia of stomach.

(C) uberon-0037500.description: (C): An axillary lymph node that is placed along the lower margin of the posterior wall of the axilla in the course of the subscapular artery.

(C) uberon-0037501.description: (C): An axiallary lymph node along the lower border of the Pectoralis minor, in relation with the lateral thoracic artery. Their afferents drain the skin and muscles of the anterior and lateral thoracic walls, and the central and lateral parts of the mamma; their efferents pass partly to the central and partly to the subclavicular groups of axillary glands.

(C) uberon-0037502.description: (C): An axillary lymph node that is imbedded in the adipose tissue near the base of the axilla.

(C) uberon-0037503.description: (C): An axillary lymph node that is situated partly posterior to the upper portion of the Pectoralis minor and partly above the upper border of this muscle.

(C) uberon-0037530.description: (C): Pancreaticosplenioc lymph node located along the inferior margin of pancreas.

(C) uberon-0037580.description: (C): Gastric lymph node located along the lesser curvature of stomach.

(C) uberon-0038685.description: (C): Left gastric lymph node located along the cardiac half of the lesser curvature of stomach in the lesser omentum.

(C) uberon-0038691.description: (C): Hepatic lymph node located along the common hepatic artery.

(C) uberon-0038694.description: (C): Hepatic lymph node located along the portal vein.

(C) uberon-0038696.description: (C): Superior pancreatic lymph node located along the distal segment of splenic artery.

(C) uberon-0038698.description: (C): Superior pancreaticoduodenal lymph node located on the posterior aspect of superior portion of head of pancreas.

(C) uberon-0038746.description: (C): Gastric lymph node located along the greater curvature of stomach.

(C) uberon-0038849.description: (C): Lymph node located in either head and neck region.

(C) uberon-0038934.label_original: superior deep lateral cervical lymph node

(C) uberon-0038935.label_original: inferior deep lateral cervical lymph node

(C) uberon-0038951.description: (C): Pylorioc lymph node located near the bifurcation of gastroduodenal artery and superior to the pylorus.

(C) uberon-0038952.description: (C): Pylorioc lymph node located in the angle between the superior and descending parts of duodenum.

(C) uberon-0039167.description: (C): A tracheobronchial lymph node situated in the hilum of a lung.

(C) uberon-0039169.description: (C): The anterior intercostal branches of internal thoracic artery supply the upper five or six intercostal spaces.

(C) uberon-0039170.label_original: mammary branch of internal thoracic artery

(C) uberon-0039185.description: (C): A lower continuation of the vertebral vein and vertebral venous plexus that passes through the foramen of the transverse process of the 7th cervical vertebra and empties into the brachiocephalic vein.

(C) uberon-0039186.description: (C): A vein that commences in a plexus around the transverse processes of the upper cervical vertebræ, descends in company with the ascending cervical artery between the Scalenus anterior and Longus capitis muscles, and opens into the terminal part of the vertebral vein.

(C) uberon-0039187.description: (C): The suprascapular vein is a vein running above the scapula. It empties into the external jugular vein.

(C) uberon-0039188.description: (C): The superior laryngeal vein is a vein which drains the larynx into the superior thyroid vein.

(C) uberon-0039215.description: (C): An artery that commonly arises from the terminal branch of the ileocolic artery, or less commonly from the posterior cecal artery or an ileal artery.[1][2] It descends behind the termination of the ileum and enters the mesoappendix of the vermiform appendix. It runs near the free margin of the mesoappendix and ends in branches which supply the appendix.

(C) uberon-0039230.description: (C): The prepyloric vein is the last connecting branch onto the right gastric vein, marking the end of the stomach, and draining the proximal part of the duodenum

(C) uberon-0039232.description: (C): The conus artery is generally considered to be the first branch of the right coronary artery (RCA) in the right sinus of Valsalva. However, one study has shown that in approximately 50% of humans, the conus artery arises from a discrete ostium in the right sinus of Valsalva.

(C) uberon-0039256.description: (C): vein ascending the posterior aspect of the body of the pubis to drain into the inferior epigastric vein; this vein frequently (about 20% of patients) serves as an accessory or replaced obturator vein.

(C) uberon-0039288.description: (C): The fissure between the labia majora

(C) uberon-0039418.description: (C): An anatomical conduit in the pelvis through which the internal pudendal artery, internal pudendal veins, and the pudendal nerve pass.

(C) uberon-0039421.description: (C): A vein that drains the prepuce and skin of the penis, and, running backward in the subcutaneous tissue, inclines to the right or left, and opens into the corresponding superficial external pudendal vein, a tributary of the great saphenous vein..

(C) uberon-0700019.description: (C): A parallel fiber results from the axon of a cerebellar granule cell ascending through the molecular layer where it synapses on the dendritic branches of Purkinje cells and stellate cells.

(C) uberon-0700020.description: (C): A parallel fiber that results from the bifurcation of a cerebellar granule cell axon in the molecular layer into two diametrically opposed branches, that are oriented parallel to the long axis of the folium.

(C) uberon-2002218.description: (C): A parallel fiber results from the axon of a cerebellar granule cell ascending through the molecular layer where it does not bifurcate and synapses on the dendritic branches of Purkinje cells and stellate cells. The parallel fibers in teleost fish do not bifurcate in contrast to other vertebrates.

(C) uberon-1000000.description: (C): Subdivision of the head consisting of the area along the lower edge of the chin.

(C) uberon-1000001.description: (C): A collection of hairs that grows on the vertex (top of head).

(C) uberon-1000002.description: (C): The middle part of the head, located approximately equidistant from the left and the right sides of the head.

(C) uberon-1000003.description: (C): A longitudinal flap of skin that hangs beneath the lower jaw or neck.

(C) uberon-1000004.description: (C): A collection of hairs that grows on the external ear.
(C) uberon-1000004.label_original: collection of hair on external ear

(C) uberon-1000005.description: (C): Area along the edge of the external ear.

(C) uberon-1000006.description: (C): A collection of hairs that grows on the forehead.

(C) uberon-1000007.description: (C): A bulge, knob, or swelling that protrudes from the forehead.

(C) uberon-1000008.description: (C): Subdivision of the head consisting of the left half of the face, vertically divided.

(C) uberon-1000009.description: (C): A ridge or peak located along the middle part of the head, located approximately equidistant from the left and the right sides of the head.

(C) uberon-1000010.description: (C): A benign tumor on the skin, usually with darker pigment.

(C) uberon-1000011.description: (C): Anatomical structure consisting of either corner of the mouth.

(C) uberon-1000012.description: (C): Subdivision of the head consisting of the area along the front edge of the external nose.

(C) uberon-1000013.description: (C): The extreme point of curvature of the external nose.

(C) uberon-1000014.description: (C): Subdivision of the head consisting of the right half of the face, vertically divided.

(C) uberon-1000015.description: (C): A zone of skin that is part of the snout.

(C) uberon-1000016.description: (C): Subdivision of the head consisting of the pointed or rounded end or extremity of the snout.

(C) uberon-1000017.description: (C): Subdivision of the head consisting of the pointed or rounded end or extremity of the external ear.

(C) uberon-1000018.description: (C): A small collection or tuft of hairs.

(C) uberon-1000020.description: (C): A collection of hairs that grows on the snout.

(C) uberon-1000022.description: (C): A multilobulated modified sebaceous gland that is located at the base of the external ear, lined by stratified squamous epithelium, and secretes into the auditory canal.

(C) uberon-1200000.description: (C): A fold of peritoneum between the ileum and cecum. The upper border of the ileocecal fold is fixed to the ileum opposite its mesenteric attachment, and the lower border passes over the ileocecal junction to join the mesentery of the appendix (and sometimes the appendix itself as well). Behind the ileocecal fold is the inferior ileocecal fossa.

(C) uberon-1200001.description: (C): The group of nerve cell bodies located on the dorsal spinal roots within the vertebral column at the level of the sixth lumbar vertebra.

(C) uberon-1200003.description: (C): The superior, dome-shaped portion of the uterus.

(C) uberon-1500000.description: (C): Enlarged and broad extension of the scapula distal to the glenoid region that conforms to the contour of the ribs. Origin for the major shoulder muscles including the deltoid group.

(C) uberon-1500003.description: (C): Anatomical space that contains a portion of the lateral line system.

(C) uberon-1500005.description: (C): Paired cartilaginous element forming the posterior portion of the pelvic girdle [D.F. Markle, BULLETIN OF MARINE SCIENCE. 30(1): 45-53. 1980].

(C) uberon-1500006.description: (C): Paired fin radial element that is composed of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-1600006.description: (C): Radial element that is part of a paired fin.

(C) uberon-2000271.description: (C): Radial element that is composed of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-1500007.description: (C): The median, elongated basal cartilage of the pectoral fin.

(C) uberon-2201587.description: (C): Pectoral fin proximal radial element that is composed of cartilage tissue.

(C) uberon-1500008.description: (C): Pelvic fin radial that develops from the pelvic fin endoskeletal disc. Pelvic fin distal radials are paired.

(C) uberon-1600008.description: (C): Pelvic fin radial element that develops from the pelvic fin endoskeletal disc. Pelvic fin distal radial elements are paired.

(C) uberon-2000508.description: (C): Pelvic fin radial element that is composed of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-1500009.description: (C): Pelvic fin radial that is an endochondral fused radials or pterygiophores at the base of the pelvic fin.

(C) uberon-1500010.description: (C): Pelvic fin radial in the middle of the pelvic fin.

(C) uberon-2100508.description: (C): Pelvic fin radial elements are internal skeletal supports of the pelvic fin.

(C) uberon-2000001.description: (C): Small but distinctive epithelial sac containing fluid, located midventrally posterior to the yolk cell or its extension, and transiently present during most of the segmentation period. Kimmel et al, 1995. Kupffer's vesicle has been compared to the mouse embryonic node. Drummond et al, 2005.

(C) uberon-2000006.description: (C): The anterior round region of the yolk cell present after the yolk extension forms during the segmentation period. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000084.description: (C): Nutrient store for embryonic development in the form of semicrystalline phospholipoprotein and contained within yolk granules. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000023.description: (C): A group of cells that migrate at the leading edge of shield during gastrulation but do not involute. At the end of gastrulation, forerunner cells migrate deep into the embryo and organize to form Kuppfer's vesicle. Cooper and D'Amico, 1996.

(C) uberon-2000040.description: (C): Surface structure that will develop into one of the median fins. Extends from dorsal surface of fish, caudal to the 8th somite, to the ventral surface ending at the caudal side of the vent.

(C) uberon-2000044.description: (C): Portion of somite 14 that gives rise to body wall muscle masses. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000726.description: (C): Undifferentiated mesodermal component of early trunk segment 14 or metamere, derived from paraxial mesoderm; forms the myotome, sclerotome and perhaps dermatome. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000052.description: (C): Actinotrichium which is part of the dorsal fin fold.

(C) uberon-2000102.description: (C): Region of the median fin fold that develops into the dorsal fin.

(C) uberon-2000089.description: (C): Elastoidin fin ray that is slender, sometimes branched distally and present in the embryonic fin fold. Actinotrichia are translucent and exhibit birefringence.

(C) uberon-2000058.description: (C): The hatching gland rudiment at the time it underlies the forebrain during the early segmentation period. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000072.description: (C): Anteriormost undifferentiated mesodermal component of early trunk segment or metamere, derived from paraxial mesoderm; forms the myotome, sclerotome and perhaps dermatome. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000073.description: (C): Undifferentiated mesodermal component of early trunk segment 5 or metamere, derived from paraxial mesoderm; forms the myotome, sclerotome and perhaps dermatome. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000074.description: (C): Undifferentiated mesodermal component of early tail segment 26 or metamere, derived from paraxial mesoderm; forms the myotome, sclerotome and perhaps dermatome. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000078.description: (C): Actinotrichium which is part of the ventral fin fold.

(C) uberon-2000088.description: (C): Peripheral layer of the yolk cell including nuclei and non-yolky cytoplasm. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-4400006.description: (C): Fin ray that is composed of elastoidin, unmineralized, and unsegmented.

(C) uberon-2000090.description: (C): Apical ectodermal ridge that is part of the dorsal fin.

(C) uberon-2000093.description: (C): A cell arising during cleavage; the term encompasses the partially cleaved, incomplete cells at the blastodisc margin before they collectively form the yolk syncytial layer (YSL) in the midblastula. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000103.description: (C): Dermal bone that is located on the dorsal margin of the maxilla, usually at the dorso-posterior region of maxilla. The supramaxilla is a paired bone.

(C) uberon-2000104.description: (C): Dermal bone that is located dorsal to the preopercle or lies on the antero-dorsal corner of the opercle, and encloses the upper section of the preopercular canal. The suprapreopercle is paired.

(C) uberon-2000106.description: (C): The posterior elongated region of the yolk cell that forms during the segmentation period. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000120.description: (C): Ganglion that develops from a cranial ectodermal placode and contains sensory neurons that innervate a lateral line.

(C) uberon-2000125.description: (C): Neuromast that is part of the mandibular lateral line. Kimmel et al, 1995. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000259.description: (C): One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva consisting of 2 neuromast. One neuromast is positioned at the front edge of the jaw the second posteriorly on the mandible. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000127.description: (C): Dermal bone positioned as the first bone of the infraorbital series. The antorbital articulates with the lacrimal or infraorbital 1 anteroventrally and the supraorbital posterodorsally. The antorbital is a paired bone.

(C) uberon-2001709.description: (C): Anatomical cluster that is the series of dermal bones surrounding the orbit and associated with the infraorbital sensory canal.

(C) uberon-2000136.description: (C): Neuromast that is part of the otic lateral line. Kimmel et al, 1995. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000464.description: (C): One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva positioned anterior to the ear. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000139.description: (C): Brightly refractile stone-like organ within the otic vesicle and positioned over a sensory macula; two form in each vesicle during the late segmentation period. Kimmel et al, 1995. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for otolith by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000156.description: (C): Undifferentiated mesodermal component of early trunk or tail segment 20 or metamere, derived from paraxial mesoderm; forms the myotome, sclerotome and perhaps dermatome. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000157.description: (C): Posteriormost undifferentiated mesodermal component of early tail segment or metamere, derived from paraxial mesoderm; forms the myotome, sclerotome and perhaps dermatome. Kimmel et al, 1995.

body: [dorsal zone of median tuberal portion of hypothalamus](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_2000347)
(C) uberon-2000347.label_original: dorsal zone of median tuberal portion of hypothalamus

(C) uberon-2000167.description: (C): Median fin skeleton that is located posterior to the anus.

(C) uberon-4000166.description: (C): Median fin skeleton that is located posterior to the anus.

(C) uberon-2000168.description: (C): Macula that is located in the developing anterior inner ear, and gives rise to the macula utricle. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for sensory patches of the ear by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000171.description: (C): Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates dorsally with the hyosymplectic cartilage or the articulation of the hyomandibula and symplectic.

(C) uberon-2001892.description: (C): Skeletal element that is bilaterally paired and articulates dorsally with the hyosymplectic cartilage or the articulation of the hyomandibula and symplectic.

(C) uberon-2001841.description: (C): Joint that articulates the interhyal and epihyal bones, or interhyal and ceratohyal cartilages. Interhyal-epihyal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001511.description: (C): Pharyngeal arch cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates dorsally with the hyosymplectic cartilage or the articulation of the hyomandibula and symplectic.

(C) uberon-2000318.description: (C): CNS white matter that is part of the brain stem or spinal cord.

(C) uberon-2000175.description: (C): Cranial nerve which enters the brain between cranial nerves VIII and IX; contains afferents and sensory efferents to the posterior lateral line ganglion and middle ganglion. Fibers from the posterior lateral line ganglion innervate the occipital dorsal lateral line and trunk lateral lines.

(C) uberon-2001471.description: (C): The posterior lateral line system develops from cranial ectodermal placodes, situated behind the ear, that give rise to both the neuromasts and the posterior lateral line sensory nerves that innervate the neuromasts. The posterior lateral line system consists of small sensory patches (neuromasts) located superficially on the skin or just under the skin in fluid-filled canals on the head of all fishes and most amphibians. The neuromasts are innervated by several lateral line nerves, which project primarily to the hindbrain. The posterior mechanosensory lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance.

(C) uberon-2000185.description: (C): Part of the anterior commissure which abuts the preoptic region dorsally.

(C) uberon-2005270.description: (C): A muscle that moves body parts into an inferior direction or lowered position. Antagonistic to erector muscle.

(C) uberon-2000648.description: (C): Musculature that is part of the dorsal fin.

(C) uberon-2000196.description: (C): Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates with the anterior ceratohyal posteriorly and the ventral hypohyal bone ventrally.

(C) uberon-2001843.description: (C): Joint that articulates the ceratohyal and dorsal hypohyal bones. Ceratohyal-dorsal hypohyal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001845.description: (C): Joint that articulates the dorsal hypohyal and ventral hypohyal bones. Dorsal hypohyal-ventral hypohyal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001847.description: (C): Joint that articulates the dorsal hypohyal and urohyal bones. Dorsal hypohyal-urohyal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2000202.description: (C): A section of a pharyngeal arch artery that carries blood away from the gills.
(C) uberon-2000202.label_original: efferent portion of pharyngeal arch artery

(C) uberon-2000203.description: (C): An endochondral bone which is located anterior to the orbitosphenoid and medial to the paired lateral ethmoid. Rhinosphenoid is a median bone.

(C) uberon-2002226.description: (C): Diencephalic nucleus which is located in the caudal tuberculum. The preglomerular nuclei make up most of the migrated nuclei within the caudal tuberculum. From Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain.

(C) uberon-2000210.label_original: gigantocellular part of magnocellular preoptic nucleus

(C) uberon-2000223.description: (C): Infraorbital in fishes that is the first (anteriormost) bone of the infraorbital series.

(C) uberon-2000376.description: (C): Dermal bone that is located anterior, ventral or posterior to the eye. Infraorbital bones may or may not contain the infraorbital sensory canal. Infraorbital bones are numbered starting with the anteriormost element of the series.

(C) uberon-2000224.description: (C): Process that is the ventral, posteriorly-oriented bony extension of the quadrate.

(C) uberon-2000226.description: (C): Endochondral bone that separates the olfactory region from the orbit, extends medially to meet its fellow medially below the frontal bones and is bordered by the mesethmoid anteriorly. It may articulate with the autopalatine and infraorbital 1 laterally. The lateral ethmoid is paired.

(C) uberon-4300111.description: (C): Endochondral element that separates the olfactory region from the orbit, extends medially to meet its fellow medially below the frontal bones and is bordered by the mesethmoid anteriorly. It may articulate with the autopalatine and infraorbital 1 laterally. The lateral ethmoid is paired.

(C) uberon-2001608.description: (C): Joint that articulates the autopalatine and lateral ethmoid and bones. Autopalatine-lateral ethmoid joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001679.description: (C): Joint that articulates the mesethmoid and lateral ethmoid. Mesethmoid-lateral ethmoid joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001941.description: (C): Joint that articulates the orbitosphenoid cartilage or bone and lateral ethmoid cartilage or bone. Orbitosphenoid-lateral ethmoid joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2002032.description: (C): Joint that articulates the lateral ethmoid and frontal. lateral ethmoid-frontal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2000234.description: (C): Macula positioned on the floor of the utricle adjacent to the utriculosaccular foramen at the base of the common crus.

(C) uberon-2000558.description: (C): Macula that is located in the developing posterior inner ear, and gives rise to the macula neglecta and the macula saccule. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for sensory patches of the ear by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000239.description: (C): Endochondral bone that articulates laterally with the medial surface of the cleithrum and ventro-medially with the scapula and coracoid. Meoscoracoid bone is a small, arch-like bone that develops from the mesocoracoid cartilage. Mesocoracoid bone is paired.

(C) uberon-2001537.description: (C): Pectoral fin cartilage that is part of the embryonic primary pectoral girdle from which the mesocoracoid bone will ossify endochondrally.

(C) uberon-2000240.description: (C): Endochondral bone that forms the posteriormost element of the palatal complex. It overlies the quadrate and symplectic, posteriorly it articulates with the hyomandibula and anteriorly with the entopterygoid and ectopterygoid. It curves dorsally to form the posteroventral surface of the orbit. The metapterygoid is paired.

(C) uberon-2001803.description: (C): Joint that articulates quadrate and metapterygoid bones. Quadrate-metapterygoid joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001979.description: (C): Joint that articulates the hyomandibula bone and metapterygoid bone.

(C) uberon-2001710.description: (C): Joint that articulates the opercle and interopercle. Opercle-interopercle joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2002282.description: (C): Joint that articulates the preopercle and opercle. Preopercle-opercle joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2005265.description: (C): Synovial joint that articulates the hyomandibula and the opercle.

(C) uberon-2000251.description: (C): A fin that is fleshy, lacks supporting rays, and is located posterior to the dorsal fin.

(C) uberon-4500004.description: (C): Median fin skeleton supporting the adipose fin.

(C) uberon-2000264.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the opercular series and bears the preopercular sensory canal. The preopercle is a paired bone and typically L-shaped, with the horizontal limb overlying the interopercle and the vertical limb overlying the opercle.

(C) uberon-2000265.description: (C): Portion of presumptive mesoderm fated to become dorsal mesoderm.

(C) uberon-2000268.description: (C): Anal fin proximal radial element that is composed of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-2100268.description: (C): Rod-like internal median skeletal support elememts of the anal fin, which articulate with the distal radial elements.

(C) uberon-2001671.description: (C): Anal fin radial element that is composed of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-2200268.description: (C): Anal fin proximal radial element that is composed of cartilage tissue.

(C) uberon-2000276.label_original: rostrolateral thalamic nucleus of Butler & Saidel

(C) uberon-2000603.description: (C): Brain structure which is caudally attached to the rostral medulla oblongata and extends into the tectal ventricle. The valvula cerebelli consists of a granular and a molecular layer along with aggregations of large Purkinje and eurydendroid cells and is uniquely present in ray-finned fishes. From Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain.

(C) uberon-2000281.description: (C): Specialized neuronal receptor cells of the lateral line and acoustico-vestibular systems. Kimmel et al, 1995. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for hair cells by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000284.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the opercular series, lying below the opercle. The subopercle is paired and is typically a thin bone.

(C) uberon-2000289.description: (C): A dermal bone that is the lower, horizontal portion of the preopercle bone.

(C) uberon-2005268.description: (C): Joint that articulates the posterior edge of the preopercle horizontal limb with the symplectic.

(C) uberon-2000291.description: (C): Lateral line sensory nucleus located in the cerebellum that processes sensory input from the lateral line.

(C) uberon-2000300.description: (C): Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates with the ceratohyal bone posteriorly and the dorsal hypohyal bone dorsally.

(C) uberon-2001844.description: (C): Joint that articulates the ceratohyal and ventral hypohyal bones. Ceratohyal-ventral hypohyal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001846.description: (C): Joint that articulates the contralateral ventral hypohyal bones or the contralateral ceratobranchial cartilages. Inter-ventral hypohyal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001848.description: (C): Joint that articulates the ventral hypohyal and urohyal bones. Ventral hypohyal-urohyal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2000309.description: (C): The portion of the YSL that is outside of the blastoderm margin during epiboly. Kimmel et al, 1995.

body: [caudal zone of median tuberal portion of hypothalamus](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_2000634)
(C) uberon-2000634.label_original: caudal zone of median tuberal portion of hypothalamus

(C) uberon-2000336.description: (C): A dermal bone that is the upper, vertical portion of the preopercle bone.

(C) uberon-2005278.description: (C): Joint that articulates the anterior edge of the preopercle vertical limb and the hyomandibula.

(C) uberon-2000337.description: (C): Endochondral bone which is the posterodorsal region of the basioccipital bone.

(C) uberon-2001620.description: (C): Anatomical cluster that consists of a bulla formed by the exoccipital and basioccipital bones, and surrounds the lagena.

(C) uberon-2000392.description: (C): Multi-tissue structure which is part of the hypothalamus and consists of caudal and ventral zones, and is separated from the dorsal hypothalamic zone by a deep ventral sulcus. From Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain.

(C) uberon-2000348.description: (C): Endochondral bone which is the posterodorsal region of the exoccipital bone.

(C) uberon-2000350.description: (C): Epipleurals lie below the horizontal septum and are posteroventrally directed. There are ossified epipleurals in certain ostariophysans. In many lower elopocephalan teleosts including ostariophysans the epipleural bones develop an anterodorsal branch so that they are forked proximally.

(C) uberon-2000526.description: (C): Axial bone which is a segmental ossification that forms in the myoseptum.

(C) uberon-2000356.description: (C): Dermal bone that is a projection present on the inner surface of a branchial arch.

(C) uberon-2000363.description: (C): Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates medially with a median skeletal element and laterally with a ceratobranchial cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001893.description: (C): Skeletal element that is bilaterally paired and articulates medially with a median skeletal element and laterally with a ceratobranchial element.

(C) uberon-2001522.description: (C): Pharyngeal arch cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates medially with a median skeletal element and laterally with a ceratobranchial cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2000364.description: (C): Laterally flattened haemal spine of an ural vertebra that lacks its arch and supports a few principal caudal lepidotrichia distally. A hypural may articulate or fuse with its ural centrum proximally or may lie ventral to the notochord. A hypural is an unpaired median bone that ossifies perichondrally. (Modified from Monod, 1968 and Arratia and Schultze, 1992).

(C) uberon-2001364.description: (C): Hemal spines are extensions of hemal arches in the ventral skeletogenous septum of the caudal region.

(C) uberon-2002067.description: (C): Anatomical cluster including hypural 3 and more dorsal hypurals that supports the dorsal series of principal caudal lepidotrichia or rays. The upper hypural set articulates or fuses to ural centra 3, 4 or 5 (polyural terminology) or ural centrum 2 (diural terminology) depending on the teleost subgroup. The upper hypural set is composed of unpaired median bones.

(C) uberon-2002068.description: (C): Anatomical cluster including hypurals 1 and 2 that supports part of the ventral principal caudal lepidotrichia or rays and that separates from the dorsal hypural set through the hypural diastema. The lower hypural set articulates or fuses to ural centra 1 and 2 (polyural terminology) or ural centrum 1 (diural terminology) depending on the teleost subgroup. The lower hypural set is composed of unpaired median bones.

(C) uberon-2002162.description: (C): Vertebra that is incomplete or rudimentary and may bear a rudimentary neural arch and sometimes a rudimentary spine or the neural arch and spine are completely absent. Ural vertebrae are one of the last bony elements of the vertebral column, usually smaller than the preural centra. Ural vertebrae are numbered beginning from anterior (1) to posterior (2, 3, 4, etc.). Ural vertebra is an unpaired median bone.

(C) uberon-2000373.description: (C): Actinotrichium that is part of the dorsal fin skeleton.

(C) uberon-2000375.description: (C): Actinotrichium that is part of the anal fin skeleton.

(C) uberon-4000163.description: (C): Median fin that is located posterior to the anus.

(C) uberon-2000384.description: (C): Jaw muscle that connects the sphenotic to the metapterygoid and hyomandibula and promotes the elevation/abduction of the suspensorium.

(C) uberon-2000387.label_original: obsolete nucleus motorius of nervi vagi

(C) uberon-2000410.description: (C): Dermal bone placed postero-medially to the supracleithrum and/or cleithrum.

(C) uberon-2000419.description: (C): Endochondral bone that sutures with the orbitosphenoid anteriorly, the frontal bone dorsally and the sphenotic and prootic posteriorly. The pterosphenoid forms part of the orbitosphenoid region. The pterosphenoid bears foramina that accommodate branches of the trigeminal and facial nerves. The pterosphenoid is a paired bone.

(C) uberon-2001831.description: (C): Joint that articulates the pterosphenoid and orbitosphenoid. Pterosphenoid-orbitosphenoid joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2002033.description: (C): Joint that articulates the prootic and pterosphenoid. prootic-pterosphenoid joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001515.description: (C): Cartilage bar (bilaterally paired) that is first visible as an anterior extension of the auditory capsule. It grows anteriorly toward the middle of the orbit where it is connected to its mate on the other side by the epiphyseal bar.

(C) uberon-2000422.description: (C): The retroarticular is a cartilage bone that forms at the posteroventral tip of Meckel's cartilage where the interoperculomandibular ligament attaches (5.1 mm NL). In the adult it is basically triangular in shape. The retroarticular is ligamentously connected to the interopercle and preopercle posteriorly and abuts the ventral shelf of the dentary anteriorly.

(C) uberon-2000424.description: (C): One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva positioned posteriorly to the second arch skeletal element. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000425.description: (C): Cranial nerve which enters the brain between cranial nerves VI and VII; contains afferents and sensory efferents to the anterior lateral line ganglia.

(C) uberon-2001468.description: (C): The anterior lateral line system develops from cranial ectodermal placodes, situated between the eye and the ear, that give rise to both the neuromasts and the anterior lateral line sensory nerves that innervate the neuromasts. The anterior lateral line system consists of small sensory patches (neuromasts) located superficially on the skin or just under the skin in fluid-filled canals on the head of all fishes and most amphibians and are innervated by several lateral line nerves, which project to the hindbrain. The anterior lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance.

(C) uberon-2000429.description: (C): Neural arch and Weberian ossicle that is reduced in size relative to other neural arches. Scaphium has a process which articulates with the first centrum.

(C) uberon-2000437.description: (C): Actinotrichium that is part of the caudal fin skeleton.

(C) uberon-2000438.description: (C): Haemal spine of last hemal arch that is pierced by the haemal canal through which the caudal vessels pass or haemal arch of preural centrum 1. Its distal part commonly supports lepidotrichia. The parhypural is an unpaired median haemal spine.

(C) uberon-2000557.description: (C): Last caudal vertebra identified as the point at which the caudal vessels bifurcate, leaving the protection of the haemal arches of the caudal vertebrae and running laterally to the hypurals. This vertebra bears, commonly, a well-developed haemal arch and its spine (parhypural).

(C) uberon-2000442.description: (C): Endochondral bone that is median and located in the dorsal skeletogenous septum between the cranium and the dorsal fin.

(C) uberon-4300035.description: (C): Endochondral element that is median and located in the dorsal skeletogenous septum between the cranium and the dorsal fin.

(C) uberon-2000452.description: (C): Tendon bone that forms in the tendon of the sternohyoid muscles ventral to the anterior end of copula 1. The urohyal associates by ligaments to the ventral hypohyals or it articulates with the ventral hypohyals. The urohyal is an unpaired bone.

(C) uberon-2000460.description: (C): Actinotrichium that is part of the adipose fin.

(C) uberon-2000461.description: (C): Bone that is an element associated with a Weberian vertebra.

(C) uberon-2001871.description: (C): Anatomical cluster that consists of the Weberian ossicles.

(C) uberon-2000474.description: (C): Small membrane bone homologous with a cartilage bone in more basal fishes (Patterson, 1977). Situated between the exoccipital and the pterotic at point of attachment of short ligament that originates on the ventral arm of the posttemporal.

(C) uberon-2000476.description: (C): Dermal bone that is a flattened element that supports the branchiostegal membrane. Branchiostegal rays are generally present in a series articulating ventrally or ventro-medially with the anterior and posterior ceratobranchials whereas the most posterior ray articulates with the subopercle. The branchiostegal ray is paired.

(C) uberon-2002101.description: (C): Anatomical cluster that consists of the branchiostegal rays within an individual.

(C) uberon-4300150.description: (C): Membrane organ that is usually supported by branchiostegal rays and forms the ventral and posterior wall of the gill cavity.

(C) uberon-2001849.description: (C): Joint that articulates the epihyal and branchiostegal ray bones. Epihyal-branchiostegal ray joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001850.description: (C): Joint that articulates the ceratohyal and branchiostegal ray bones. Ceratohyal-branchiostegal ray joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2000480.description: (C): Hindbrain nucleus which is part of the medulla oblongata and is a mechanoreceptive area along with the medial octavolateralis nucleus. It is smaller than the medial octavolateralis nucleus and is located lateral to the facial and vagal lobes of the medulla oblongata. From Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain.

(C) uberon-2000488.description: (C): Endochondral bone that is bilaterally paired and forms part of the ventral branchial arches.

(C) uberon-2001898.description: (C): Skeletal element that is bilaterally paired and forms part of the ventral branchial arches.

(C) uberon-2001516.description: (C): Pharyngeal arch cartilage that forms the largest skeletal element of the ventral branchial arches.

(C) uberon-2000491.label_original: obsolete commissure of the caudal tuberculum

(C) uberon-2000493.label_original: obsolete decussation of medial funicular nucleus

(C) uberon-2000495.description: (C): Infraorbital that is the fifth bone of the infraorbital series.

(C) uberon-2000498.description: (C): Mandibular muscle that inserts along the dorsolateral faces of the opercles. Responsible for opercular abduction.

(C) uberon-2005267.description: (C): Muscle that moves parts of the body in a superior direction to an erect position. Antagonistic to depressor muscle.

(C) uberon-2000507.description: (C): Some or all epineural bones ossify free from the neural arches in most teleosts. In some lower teleosts, e.g., Leptolepis, Hiodon, elopiforms and albuliforms, ossification proceeds from the attachment point of the ligament to the arch, and the epineural is a process of the neural arch. In many lower teleosts epineurals are forked proximally.

(C) uberon-2001538.description: (C): Small cartilage that forms at the posterior edge of the basipterygium.

(C) uberon-2000525.description: (C): Neural arch and Weberian ossicle that has been modified in shape relative to other neural arches. Intercalarium includes three parts: an anterolateral process (the manubrium) which is embedded in the interossicular ligament and the ascending and articulating processes.

(C) uberon-2000527.description: (C): Endochondral bone of the branchial arches located medial to the epibranchials.

(C) uberon-2001909.description: (C): Skeletal element of the branchial arches located medial to the epibranchials.

(C) uberon-2001533.description: (C): Paired cartilages that project medially from the medial tips of epibranchials.

(C) uberon-2000541.description: (C): Cells (incompletely cleaved before the YSL forms), located at the surface just at the rim of the blastodisc, external to the deep blastomeres. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000544.description: (C): Actinotrichium that is part of the pectoral fin.

(C) uberon-2000549.description: (C): Dermal bone of the secondary pectoral girdle that attaches the girdle to the skull. Its dorsal process attaches to the epiotic or epioccipital, the ventral process to the intercalar and the body articulates with the supracleithrum. The postotic sensory canal or lateral line runs within or lateral to bone.

(C) uberon-2000551.description: (C): Hindbrain nucleus in the tegmental region of rhombomere 1. The cells of the nucleus are granular and lie at the ventral border of the cerebellum and brain stem.

(C) uberon-2000734.description: (C): Caudal vertebra that is one of the last caudal vertebrae anterior to the ural vertebrae that with its neural and haemal spines supports the procurrent caudal fin rays or lepidotrichia. The numbering of preural vertebrae is from caudal to rostral direction.

(C) uberon-2000576.description: (C): Endochondral bone that articulates with the autosphenotic anteriorly, the parietal dorsomedially, the prootic ventrally (and the intercalar occasionally), and the epiotic and exoccipital posteriorly. The pterotic encloses the horizontal semicircular canal of the inner ear. The lower edge of the pterotic contributes to the hyomandibular facet. The pterotic is paired.

(C) uberon-2001711.description: (C): Joint that articulates the frontal and pterotic. Frontal-pterotic joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2000585.description: (C): Cranial cartilage which is a small median cartilage located between the premaxillae and anterodorsal to the ethmoid.

(C) uberon-2000586.description: (C): Vertebra anterior to preural centrum 1; sometimes termed the 'antepenultimate' vertebra. Mabee and Bird, 2001.

(C) uberon-2000587.description: (C): Endochondral bone that sutures with the pterosphenoid anteriorly, the prootic ventrally, the frontal bone dorso-medially, and the pterotic dorso-posteriorly. Occasionally the sphenotic sutures with the parietal bone. The sphenotic separates the orbital from the otic region. The sphenotic bears a large antero-lateral or lateral or ventro-lateral process that borders the postero-dorsal margin of the orbit. The sphenotic is a paired bone.

(C) uberon-2000594.description: (C): Dermal bone that articulates dorsally with the posttemporal and ventrally with the cleithrum. Supracleithrum is part of the secondary pectoral girdle and commonly, carries part of the lateral line canal.

(C) uberon-2000596.description: (C): Actinotrichium that is part of the pelvic fin.

(C) uberon-2000602.description: (C): Neural arch that extends along the dorso-lateral surface of the last preural centra and/or ural centra and the notochord (Arratia & Schultze, 1992). An uroneural develops as a modification of the neural arch of an ural centrum (Patterson, 1968). The series of uroneurals may include from 7 to 1 elements that are numbered from rostrad to caudad. An uroneural is a paired membrane bone.

(C) uberon-2000607.label_original: obsolete ventral rhombencephalic commissure brain stem

(C) uberon-2000610.description: (C): Connective tissue partitions developing between the myotomes. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000618.description: (C): A brainstem commissure that contains major crossed descending projections from both tectal lobes.

(C) uberon-2000620.description: (C): Endochondral bone that is part of the antero-lateral region of the palate. Commonly, it articulates with the maxilla anterolaterally and with the ethmoidal region medially. It may also articulate with the dermopalatine ventro-laterally and with the entopterygoid posteriorly. The autopalatine is paired.

(C) uberon-2001784.description: (C): Joint that articulates autopalatine and vomer bones. Autopalatine-vomer joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001942.description: (C): Joint that articulates the autopalatine cartilage or bone and maxilla.

(C) uberon-2005119.description: (C): A surface structure that will eventually grow to form a barbel. The primordium is rich in taste buds. The final location for taste buds present in the primordium is the distal tip of the mature barbel.

(C) uberon-2000623.description: (C): Basipterygium element that is composed of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-2100623.description: (C): Endochondral element that is paired and supports the pelvic fin. The basipterygium has a posteromedial process called the ischiac process (Wietzman 1962).

(C) uberon-2001539.description: (C): Bilaterally paired small, rodlike cartilages on the ventral surface of the abdomen (present at 7.9 mm). Their posterior tips expand laterally, forming L-shaped cartilages. Medially, a posterior spur of cartilage develops, which will later ossify as the ischiac process (Weitzman 1962).

(C) uberon-2001842.description: (C): Joint that articulates the epihyal and ceratohyal bones. Epihyal-ceratohyal joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2000629.description: (C): Caudal part of the abducens nucleus that mediates motor function.

(C) uberon-2000637.description: (C): Postcranial axial cartilage and Weberian ossicle that is located dorsal to the scaphium. The claustrum cartilage is bilaterally paired.

(C) uberon-4300190.description: (C): Postcranial axial skeletal element and Weberian ossicle that is located dorsal to the scaphium. The claustrum skeletal element is bilaterally paired.

(C) uberon-2000638.description: (C): Part of the anterior commissure which is located immediately ventral to the supracommissural nucleus of area ventralis telencephali.

(C) uberon-2000639.label_original: commissure of the secondary gustatory nuclei

(C) uberon-2000642.label_original: obsolete decussation of the medial octavolateralis nucleus

(C) uberon-2000646.description: (C): Anal fin distal radial element that is composed of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-2100646.description: (C): Rod-like internal median skeletal support elements of the anal fin, which articulate with the lepidotrichia distally.

(C) uberon-2200646.description: (C): Anal fin distal radial element that is composed of cartilage tissue.

(C) uberon-2000654.description: (C): Rostral part of the abducens nucleus that mediates motor function.

(C) uberon-2000657.description: (C): Dermal bone that forms the ventro-medial part of the palate and the antero-ventral and ventral wall of the orbit. The entopterygoid is a paired bone.

(C) uberon-2000658.description: (C): Dorsal branchial arch bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial cartilage or bone and medially with pharyngobranchial cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001904.description: (C): Skeletal element that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial element.

(C) uberon-2001527.description: (C): Pharyngeal arch cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001412.description: (C): Endochondral bone that borders that medial edge of the posttemporal fossa. The epiotics are sutured to parietals and supraoccipital dorsally, the exoccipitals ventrally and the pterotics laterally. The epiotic is a paired bone.

(C) uberon-2000660.description: (C): A free, modified neural spine of a preural or a ural vertebra that is placed between the last developed neural spine of a preural centrum and the dorsal axis (= anterior margin of first uroneural) of the caudal skeleton . An epural commonly supports one or more dorsal procurrent rays. An epural is an unpaired median perichondrally ossified bone.

(C) uberon-2000663.description: (C): Dermal canal-bearing bone placed at the dorso-posterior region of the skull roof, lying on the posterior region of the pterotic and parietals, or the pterotic and epioccipital, or on the pterotic, epioccipital and occipital bones.

(C) uberon-2000673.description: (C): A pair of HA are connect one to each AA1. They run rostromedially until at the extreme rostro-ventral midline the two vessels merge and then run straight caudally along the ventral midline until they reach the cranial end of the ventral aorta (VA). There, the single HA passes just dorsal to the rostral end of the VA and then immediately splits again into a pair of HA. The paired HA continue caudally just to either side of the ventral midline. The HA provide blood supply to the ventral branchial region and the heart.sogai et al. 2001.

(C) uberon-2000674.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the opercular series. It is located ventro-medially to the preopercle and anterior to the subopercle. It is joined to the posterior part of the lower jaw (retroarticular) by a ligament. The interopercle is paired.

(C) uberon-2000678.description: (C): Specialized neuronal receptor cells of the lateral line and acoustico-vestibular systems. Kimmel et al, 1995. (Also see Anatomical Atlas entry for hair cells by T. Whitfield.).

(C) uberon-2000692.description: (C): Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates with the hyomandibula and the quadrate.

(C) uberon-2000694.description: (C): Tooth that forms on ceratobranchial 5 cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001239.description: (C): Ceratobranchial bone that is the most posterior, bilaterally paired ventral pharyngeal arch bone.

(C) uberon-2000698.description: (C): Endochondral bone, membrane bone, and Weberian ossicle that is an element of third vertebra. Anteriorly it attaches to the interosseus ligament and posteriorly it extends as a transformator process embedded in the tunica externa of the swimbladder.

(C) uberon-2001169.description: (C): Vertebra that is posteriorly adjacent to vertebra 2.

(C) uberon-2000699.description: (C): Process that is the dorsally directed, vertical process of the entopterygoid. The strut sometimes articulates with the orbitosphenoid.

(C) uberon-2000711.description: (C): A multilayer of deep cells of fairly uniform thickness that forms during early epiboly (at dome stage; upon conversion of the blastodisc to the blastoderm); during gastrulation the DEL (deep cell layer) gives rise to the epiblast and hypoblast. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000712.description: (C): The portion of the YSL that lies deep to the blastoderm during epiboly. Kimmel et al, 1995.

(C) uberon-2000716.description: (C): A section of a pharyngeal arch artery that delivers blood to the gills.

(C) uberon-2001243.description: (C): Epibranchial bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 1 cartilage or bone and medially with pharyngobranchial cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001528.description: (C): Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 1 cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001244.description: (C): Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and located at the articulation of epibranchial 4 cartilage or bone and the posterior tip of ceratobranchial 4 cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001245.description: (C): Epibranchial bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 4 cartilage or bone and medially with pharyngobranchial cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001860.description: (C): Joint that articulates the epibranchial 4 cartilage or bone and upper pharyngeal toothplate. Epibranchial 4-upper pharyngeal toothplate joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001531.description: (C): Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 4 cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001246.description: (C): Epibranchial bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 2 cartilage or bone and medially with pharyngobranchial cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001530.description: (C): Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 2 cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001247.description: (C): Epibranchial bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 3 cartilage or bone and medially with pharyngobranchial cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001861.description: (C): Joint that articulates the epibranchial 3 cartilage or bone and pharyngobranchial 3 cartilage or bone. Epibranchial 3-pharyngobranchial 3 joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001862.description: (C): Joint that articulates the epibranchial 3 cartilage or bone and pharyngobranchial 4 cartilage or bone. Epibranchial 3-pharyngobranchial 4 joint is paired.

(C) uberon-2001529.description: (C): Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 3 cartilage or bone.

(C) uberon-2001250.description: (C): Pharyngobranchial bone, located medial to the epibranchials and posteriorly adjacent to pharyngobranchial 1 element.

(C) uberon-2001911.description: (C): Pharyngobranchial element, located medial to the epibranchials and posteriorly adjacent to pharyngobranchial 1 element.

(C) uberon-2001536.description: (C): Pharyngobranchial cartilage, located medial to the epibranchials and posteriorly adjacent to pharyngobranchial 1 element.

(C) uberon-2001251.description: (C): Most posterior pharyngobranchial cartilage, located medial to the epibranchials.

(C) uberon-2001913.description: (C): Most posterior pharyngobranchial element, located medial to the epibranchials.

(C) uberon-2001252.description: (C): Pharyngobranchial bone, located medial to the epibranchials and posteriorly adjacent to pharyngobranchial 2 element.

(C) uberon-2001912.description: (C): Pharyngobranchial element, located medial to the epibranchials and posteriorly adjacent to pharyngobranchial 2 element.

(C) uberon-2001534.description: (C): Pharyngobranchial cartilage, located medial to the epibranchials and posteriorly adjacent to pharyngobranchial 2 element.

(C) uberon-2001253.description: (C): Neural arch that is the second after the neurocranium.

(C) uberon-2001547.description: (C): Scute that is a bony plate that forms in the midline of ventral body margin between pectoral girdle and anal fin. Abdominal scutes may be present both anterior to and posterior to the pelvic girdle and fin.

(C) uberon-2001257.description: (C): The medial portion of the spinal cord floor plate, located adjacent to the notochord.

(C) uberon-2001263.description: (C): Stage I follicles (less than 140 microns) are primary growth stage. Selman et al, 1993.

(C) uberon-2001265.description: (C): Stage II follicles (140-340 microns) are cortical alveolus stage. Selman et al, 1993.

(C) uberon-2001266.description: (C): Stage III (340-690 microns) are vitellogenesis. Selman et al, 1993.

(C) uberon-2001274.description: (C): Tendon bone located on the median side of the lower jaw, dorsal to Meckel's cartilage and medial to the angular. The coronomeckelian forms as an ossification of the tendon of the adductor mandibulae muscle. The coronomeckelian is a paired bone.

(C) uberon-4000134.description: (C): Sesamoid that develops within a tendon, distal to an articulation or joint.

(C) uberon-2001275.description: (C): Endochondral bone that is the median element of the ventral hyoid arch, generally lying between the paired ventral hypohyals.

(C) uberon-2001277.description: (C): The anterior compartment of the swim bladder is thought to have acoustic resonance properties that play a key role in audition. It is connected to the posterior chamber via the dusctus communicans. Finney et al, 2006.

(C) uberon-2001278.description: (C): The posterior compartment of the swim bladder plays a key role in buoyancy control. It is connected to the anterior chamber via the dusctus communicans. Finney et al, 2006.

(C) uberon-2001279.description: (C): Branchiostegal ray that is the anterior-most ray in the adult.

(C) uberon-2001280.description: (C): Branchiostegal ray that is the third anterior-most ray in the adult.

(C) uberon-2001281.description: (C): Branchiostegal ray that is the second anterior-most ray in the adult.

(C) uberon-2001391.description: (C): The anteror lateral line ganglia develops from cranial ectodermal placodes and contain sensory neurons that innervate the anterior lateral line system.

(C) uberon-2001314.description: (C): The posterior lateral line ganglion develops from a cranial ectodermal placode and contains sensory neurons that innervate the posterior lateral line system.

(C) uberon-2001322.description: (C): A tract originating in the epiphysis and fasiculating with the tract of the postoptic commissure. Ross et al, 1992.

(C) uberon-2001333.description: (C): Sublingual that is the single element resulting from the fusion of the sublingual dorsal ossification and sublingual ventral ossification.

(C) uberon-2001475.description: (C): Sublingual that is the dorsal element paired with the sublingual ventral ossification.

(C) uberon-2001476.description: (C): Sublingual that is the ventral element paired with the sublingual dorsal ossification.

(C) uberon-2001335.description: (C): Supradorsals are small paired nodules of cartilage positioned at the distal ends of neural arches and the proximal end of neural spines (Arratia et al., 2001).

body: [obsolete nucleus of the tract of the anterior commissure](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_2001339)
(C) uberon-2001339.description: (C): Telencephalic nucleus containing the cell bodies of neurons whose axons form the anterior commissure.
(C) uberon-2001339.label_original: obsolete nucleus of the tract of the anterior commissure

body: [nucleus of the tract of the postoptic commissure](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_2001340)
(C) uberon-2001340.description: (C): The nucleus containing the cell bodies of neurons whose axons form the postoptic commissure.
(C) uberon-2001340.label_original: nucleus of the tract of the postoptic commissure

(C) uberon-2001341.description: (C): A zone of delayed differentiation at the midbrainhindbrain boundary. The IZ separates midbrain from anterior hindbrain neuronal clusters and has been described in all vertebrates. Geling et al, 2003.

(C) uberon-2001360.description: (C): An unpaired left-sided accessory organ which plays a role in establishing lateral brain left right asymmetry. Gamse et al, 2003.

(C) uberon-2001361.description: (C): Basiventrals are bilaterally paired cartilages lateral to the notochord which are replaced by ossified parapophyses or hemal arches.

(C) uberon-2001363.description: (C): Anatomical cluster that consists of supraneural 2 bone and supraneural 3 bone and their extensions, and which is part of the Weberian apparatus.

(C) uberon-2001373.description: (C): Cells that initially are located adjacent to the spinal cord and notochord along that migrate from their initial medial position radially through the myotome to the lateral surface of the somites.
(C) uberon-2001373.label_original: obsolete migratory slow muscle precursor cell

(C) uberon-2007005.description: (C): Hemal prezygapophyses are paired, anteromedially directed processes arising from the bases of hemal arches, ligamentously joined to the hemal postzygapophyses of the preceding vertebra. Posterior caudal vertebrae close to the caudal fin lack hemal prezygopophyses.

(C) uberon-2001382.description: (C): Epibranchials 1-3 in adults are compound elements formed by the fusion of epibranchial cartilages and the so-called uncinate processes. Posteromedially directed uncinate processes develop on the posterior edge of epibranchials 1-3. These appear as separate centers of chondrification (6.2 mm) that later fuse laterally to the posterior edges of the epibranchial cartilages (6.8 mm).

(C) uberon-2001388.description: (C): An epithelial-mesenchymal boundary that is part of a regenerating fin/limb.
(C) uberon-2001388.label_original: epithelial mesenchymal boundary of regenerating fin/limb

(C) uberon-2001392.description: (C): Parapophysis that is the lateral projections from the first centrum in cyprinids, absent in catostomids, and absent in characiphysans (Fink and Fink, 1996).

(C) uberon-2001393.description: (C): Parapophysis that is lateral projection from the second centrum, absent in Siluriformes (Fink and Fink, 1996).

(C) uberon-2001395.description: (C): Neural arch 4 is expanded and fused to supraneural 3 as part of the neural complex. A reduced neural spine projects from the posterior margin of the neural complex.

(C) uberon-2001396.description: (C): The parapophysis + rib, fused to the centrum, extends laterally then angles anteroventrally. A thin plate, the os suspensorium fuses to its median surface.

(C) uberon-2001397.description: (C): Posterior to the Weberian apparatus, otophysan supraneurals form as median, unpaired, rod- or platelike elements, as in other actinopterygians.

(C) uberon-2001403.description: (C): Dermal bone that first appears as paired ossifications in the membrane (dermis) dorsolateral to the ethmoid cartilage and anterolateral to the lateral ethmoids, later having the appearance of one butterfly-shaped element. Fused to the anterodorsal margin of the mesethmoid. Bordered anteriorly by the kinethmoid and posteriorly by the frontal.

(C) uberon-2001404.description: (C): Small rounded to egg-shaped cartilage bone that sits in an anterolateral depression on the prevomer. Articulates with the autopalatine in all cypriniforms.

(C) uberon-2001406.description: (C): Sesamoid bone located in the premaxillary-ethmoid ligament, between the mesethmoid and the premaxilla. The kinethmoid is an unpaired median bone.

(C) uberon-2001407.description: (C): Infraorbital that is the second bone of the infraorbital series.
