(C) uberon-3010272.description: (C): Multi-cellular organism that does not produce gametes.

(C) uberon-3010273.description: (C): Anatomical space that is part of a cell.

(C) uberon-3010274.description: (C): Cell which has as its part a cytoskeleton that allows for tight cell to cell contact and which has apical-basal cell polarity.

(C) uberon-3010275.description: (C): Cell that is an individual member of a species.

(C) uberon-3010277.description: (C): Anatomical point that is the apex of a projection or anything long and tapered; can be bony or cartilage.

(C) uberon-3010283.description: (C): Pigmented, smaller blastomere of the animal (upper) hemisphere of the cleaving embryo.

(C) uberon-3010284.description: (C): Unpigmented, larger blastomere of the vegetal (lower) hemisphere of the cleaving embryo.

(C) uberon-3010285.description: (C): Cell type that is first to migrate inwards at the blastopore during gastrulation.

(C) uberon-3010286.description: (C): Polymorphic cell type that forms cartilage.

(C) uberon-3010288.description: (C): A connective tissue cell that secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules.

(C) uberon-3010293.description: (C): Primitive cell type that is involved in the reproduction of the organism beginning with the sexual differentiation of the gonads at NF stage 52. In males specifically, it migrates from the genital ridge cortical region into the medullary tissue, where it forms spermatogonia. In females it is embedded in the cortical region and multiplies as oogonia.

(C) uberon-3010295.description: (C): A mature male germ cell that develops from a spermatid.

(C) uberon-3010297.description: (C): A germ cell that is a primordial oocyte in a female and that develops into secondary oogonia by mitotic division.

(C) uberon-3010298.description: (C): A germ cell that is a primordial spermatocyte in a male and that develops into secondary spermatogonia by mitotic division.

(C) uberon-3010299.description: (C): A type of germ cell that results from the mitotic division of a primary oogonium.

(C) uberon-4000045.description: (C): Skeletogenic cell that has the potential to transform into an osteoblast, and develops from neural crest or mesodermal cells.

(C) uberon-4000051.description: (C): Multi-layer ganoid scale composed of ganoine and cellular bone.

(C) uberon-4000052.description: (C): Thick, rhomboid-shaped integumentary skeletal element composed of multiple tissues including ganoine and bone.

(C) uberon-4000053.description: (C): Connective tissue that is matrix-poor with large number of vacuolated cells.

(C) uberon-4000055.description: (C): Multi-tissue structure composed of ganoine, dentine, elasmodine and cellular bone.

(C) uberon-4000059.description: (C): Proteinaceous extracellular matrix that is avascular and consists primarily of glycosaminoglycans.

(C) uberon-4000070.description: (C): Multi-tissue integumentary element composed dentine, elasmodine, and hypermineralized tissue.

(C) uberon-4000074.description: (C): Multi-tissue structure composed of ganoine, dentine and bone; not known in extant taxa.

(C) uberon-4000078.description: (C): Skeletal tissue that is mineralized, has large chondrocyte-like cells, sparse extracellular matrix, and minimal perichondrium; develops from non-mineralized chondroid tissue.

(C) uberon-4000080.description: (C): Fold or elevation of the epidermis rich in keratin proteins; possibly calcified but does not contain skeletal elements.

(C) uberon-4000081.description: (C): Multi-tissue integumentary element composed of enamel or enameloid, dentine and lamellar bone, and characterized by pore-canal system.

(C) uberon-4000086.description: (C): Cartilage tissue that is part of the exoskeleton, deposited adjacent to bone after bone formation.

(C) uberon-4000090.description: (C): Skeletal subdivision that is part of the extra-oral dermal skeletal system that develops and remains invested within the integument, primarily the dermis.

(C) uberon-4000095.description: (C): Odontoblast that non-terminally differentiated, located in the odontogenic papilla and dentine tissue, and transforms from a odontoblast cell.

(C) uberon-4000096.description: (C): Odontoblast that is terminally differentiated and derived from an odontogenic papilla and associated with dentine.

(C) uberon-4000097.description: (C): Odontoid tissue that typically contains tubules and is acellular.

(C) uberon-4000104.description: (C): Odontogenic tissue that is hypermineralized acellular, noncollagenous, covered by an epidermis and often deposited in multiple layers.

(C) uberon-4000105.description: (C): Hypermineralized tissue lacking collagen (except Sharpey's fibres), developing in close proximity to the basal cells of the overlying epithelium.

(C) uberon-4000106.description: (C): Dentine tissue that lacks dentine tubules and that is penetrated by blood capillaries.

(C) uberon-4000107.description: (C): Odontogenic tissue that consists of multiple layers of collagen fibers organized in orthogonal or twisted arrangements.

(C) uberon-4000108.description: (C): Hyaline cartilage tissue that is not mineralized.

(C) uberon-4000109.description: (C): Hyaline cartilage tissue that is mineralized.

(C) uberon-4000116.description: (C): Osteoblast that is terminally differentiated, located adjacent to acellular or cellular bone tissue within periosteum, and is capable of mineralizing the matrix.

(C) uberon-4000117.description: (C): Osteoblast that is non-terminally differentiated and located in cellular bone tissue or under the periosteum in acellular bone.

(C) uberon-4000118.description: (C): Mineralized bone tissue that always includes non-terminally differentiated osteoblasts and osteocytes.

(C) uberon-4000119.description: (C): Avascular GAG-rich matrix that is not mineralized.

(C) uberon-4000120.description: (C): Avascular GAG-rich matrix that is mineralized.

(C) uberon-4000122.description: (C): Mineralized bone tissue that has terminally differentiated osteoblasts but lacks osteocytes.

(C) uberon-4000123.description: (C): Skeletal tissue that is avascular tubular mineralized matrix, primarily made of dentine that is deposited by odontoblasts that are excluded from the matrix; develops from pre-dentine tissue.

(C) uberon-4000136.description: (C): Ossification that does not require the replacement of pre-existing tissues, most often a cartilaginous model.

(C) uberon-4000138.description: (C): Replacement element that forms as a replacement of a ligament.

(C) uberon-4000140.description: (C): Ossification that requires the replacement of a pre-existing tissue prior to bone tissue formation.

(C) uberon-4000141.description: (C): Direct ossification that occurs within mesenchyme with the formation of an osteogenic condensation not associated with a perichondrium.

(C) uberon-4000142.description: (C): Direct ossification in which transformation of the pre-existing tissue occurs without dedifferentiation of cells or reinitiation of cell division; direct transformation of a non-bone tissue into a bone tissue.

(C) uberon-4000143.description: (C): Replacement ossification wherein bone tissue replaces cartilage.

(C) uberon-4000144.description: (C): Intramembranous ossification on the surface of a cartilage element as the perichondrium becomes a periosteum, without replacement of cartilage.

(C) uberon-4000146.description: (C): Chondrogenic element that is composed of cartilage during development and has the potential to become replaced by another tissue.

(C) uberon-4000159.description: (C): Sesamoid that develops within a ligament, distal to an articulation or joint.

(C) uberon-4000160.description: (C): Dermal bone of pectoral girdle that is dorsal to and articulates with the cleithrum.

(C) uberon-4000171.description: (C): Skeletal subdivision of dermal bones that may include the anterolateral plate (AL), the spinal process (Sp), and anteroventral plate (AV) and other dermal bones that are part of the pectoral girdle.

(C) uberon-4000182.description: (C): Paired fin that is a bilaterally paired anterior outgrowth located high on the side of the animal, not far behind the orbit, with the posterior extremity corresponding with the expected posterior end of the branchial region.

(C) uberon-4100001.description: (C): Anatomical cluster that is an osteological unit consisting of the astragalus and calcaneum.

(C) uberon-4100002.description: (C): Flange on the dorsal part of the humerus, associated with extensor musculature of the forelimb (manus. carpus).

(C) uberon-4100003.description: (C): Anatomical surface that is part of a skeletal element and articulates with another skeletal element.

(C) uberon-4100004.description: (C): Bony projection (peduncle) that is located on the posterior portion of the ilium, posterior to the acetabulum.

(C) uberon-4100005.description: (C): Second most proximal phalanx in manual or pedal digits.

(C) uberon-4100006.description: (C): Posterior projection of the interclavicle that extends betwen and sometimes beyond the clavicles.

(C) uberon-4100007.description: (C): Facet of scapulocoracoid with which the pectoral fin radial(s) articulates. Facet of scapulocoracoid with which the pectoral fin radial(s) articulates. Based on Goujet and Young (1995).

(C) uberon-4100010.description: (C): Distinct notch ventral to the glenoid.

(C) uberon-4100011.description: (C): A bony process at the distal margin of the acetabulum formed by the ischium and/or the ischial peduncle of the ilium.

(C) uberon-4100012.description: (C): Region of the ilium posterior and dorsal to the acetabulum.

(C) uberon-4100013.description: (C): The posterior of the two coracoid elements found in basal tetrapods. Corresponds directly to the 'coracoid' of synapsids.

(C) uberon-4100014.description: (C): Dorsal fin located posterior to the anterior dorsal fin.

(C) uberon-4100015.description: (C): Posterior most of the two 'double heads' of the blade of the ilium in some take. Distinct and separate for the dorsal iliac process.

(C) uberon-4100016.description: (C): A posteriorly directed bony projection from the ilium that is the attachment site of the iliofibularis muscle (see Sumida, 1997).

(C) uberon-4100112.description: (C): Facet to accommodate the radius on the distal end of the humerus.

(C) uberon-4100113.description: (C): Hinge in the skull skeleton to allow for kinetic movement of different parts.

(C) uberon-4100114.description: (C): Anatomical projection in the distal region of the femur.

(C) uberon-4100115.description: (C): Soft tissue notch/opening lying on a spiracle.

(C) uberon-4100116.description: (C): Anatomical projection in the posterior/distal region of the femur.

(C) uberon-4100117.description: (C): Rib located anterior to the sacral region.

(C) uberon-4100118.description: (C): Rib located in the trunk (ribcage) area (i.e. excluding cervical and caudal axial series.

(C) uberon-4100119.description: (C): Extratemporal bone: Skull bone in the posterior half of the cranium, bordering the squamosal and opercular.

(C) uberon-4100120.description: (C): Anteriorly projecting processes allowing de facto contact between consecutive vertebrae (some soft tissues are also present) via articular facets.

(C) uberon-4100121.description: (C): The distinctive arrangement of four to ten spikes on the tails of stegosaurid dinosaurs. These spikes are believed to have been a defensive measure against predators.

(C) uberon-4200000.description: (C): The medial surface of the iliac blade. Origin site of the iliofemoralis internus muscle and its homologues.

(C) uberon-4200001.description: (C): The region of the pubis posterior to the acetabulum.

(C) uberon-4200002.description: (C): Broad, convex expansion of the coracoid bone below the level of the glenoid. Based on Romer 1956.

(C) uberon-4200003.description: (C): A type of pectoral fin in which the endoskeletal elements have a main axis that runs through the center of the fin. This creates a bilaterally symmetrical fin. (Modified from Kardong 2012).

(C) uberon-4200004.description: (C): Depression on the ventreal side of the femoral head. Associated with the pubioischiofemoralis externus muscle.

(C) uberon-4200005.description: (C): Medial facing projection or surface on the anterior ( cranial) region of the cleithrum that is often textured or denticled. This process has two primary functions: 1) its shape enhances the vertical strength of the cleithrum and 2) it forms the edge of the gill chamber and helps to direct water after it has passed over the gills (modified from Clack 2012).

(C) uberon-4200006.description: (C): An anatomical projection ventral to the glenoid fossa on the scapulocoracoid that abuts on the cliethrum (if present).

(C) uberon-4200007.description: (C): The transverse pelvic ridge is a short crest directly anterior to, and not extending posterior to, the prominent supra-acetabular buttress  from Pawley and Warren 2006.

(C) uberon-4200008.description: (C): Joint that articulates left and right clavicles.

(C) uberon-4200009.description: (C): Caudal fin lepidotrichium located ventral to the notochord.

(C) uberon-4200010.description: (C): A distinct bony ridge on ventralsurface of the humeral shaft that corresponds to the attachment site of the pectoralis muscle.

(C) uberon-4200011.description: (C): A centrale found in the pes.

(C) uberon-4200012.description: (C): Flange present of the distal region of the humerus, associated with extensor musculature of forelimb.

(C) uberon-4200013.description: (C): Surface of a long bone that possess the flexor muscle attachment sites.

(C) uberon-4200014.description: (C): Projection on the lateral side of proximal part of the ulna.

(C) uberon-4200015.description: (C): The medial most digits of the pes.

(C) uberon-4200016.description: (C): Medial facing projection or surface on the anterior ( cranial) region of the cleithrum that is often textured or denticled. This process has two primary functions: 1) its shape enhances the vertical strength of the cleithrum and 2) it forms the edge of the gill chamber and helps to direct water after it has passed over the gills (modified from Clack 2012).

(C) uberon-4200017.description: (C): An anatomical projection venteral to the glenoid fossa on the scapulocoracoid that abuts on the cliethrum.

(C) uberon-4200018.description: (C): An enlargement of the distal region of the calcaneum that corresponds to the attachment site for the foot extensor muscles.

(C) uberon-4200019.description: (C): Process on ilium located anteriorly to acetabulum.

(C) uberon-4200020.description: (C): Fossa on the medial surface on the scapula above the glenoid.

(C) uberon-4200021.description: (C): Osteological unit consisting of the astragalus and calcaneum.

(C) uberon-4200022.description: (C): Narrow bone that lies ventral to the level of insertion of the pectoral fin and is sutured to the posterior edges of both the clavicle and cleithrum. Based on Forey 1998.

(C) uberon-4200023.description: (C): A dorsal fin located anterior to posterior dorsal fin.

(C) uberon-4200024.description: (C): Fossa located on the medial surface of the scapula above the glenoid.

(C) uberon-4200025.description: (C): Flattened process of the dorsl surface of the astragalus which contacts the tibia anteriorly.

(C) uberon-4200027.description: (C): A bony projection dorsal to the glenoid articulation on the scapulocoracoid.

(C) uberon-4200028.description: (C): A prominent ridge in basal tetrapods on the ventral side of the femur that includes the fourth trochater, internal trochanter and the adductor crest (based on Coates, 1996).

(C) uberon-4200029.description: (C): A bony crest on venteral side of femur that is the attachment site for the adductor muscles.

(C) uberon-4200030.description: (C): Raised surface at the posterior portion of the acetabulum (see Nesbitt, 2011).

(C) uberon-4200031.description: (C): Muscle that is associated with tail flexion. Orginates on one of the first post sacral vertebrae posteriorly and inserts on the posterior edge of the m.puboischiotibialis. (modified from Duellman and Trueb 1994).

(C) uberon-4200032.description: (C): Expanded and flattened ventral region of clavicle bone.

(C) uberon-4200033.description: (C): Expanded dorsal region of the cleithrum.

(C) uberon-4200034.description: (C): Longitudnal bony ridge on tibia, attachment site of the major extensor muscle of the hind limb.

(C) uberon-4200036.description: (C): A boney projection on the internal diaphysis of the femur anterior or medial to the intertrochanteric fossa, below the femoral head. Muscle attachment site for ventral muscle mass notably the puboischiofemoralis externus. Modified from Romer 1956.

(C) uberon-4200037.description: (C): A bony process that corresponds to the attachment site for the forelimb supinator muscles in tetrapods, distal to the deltopectoral crest and anterior to the radial condyle.

(C) uberon-4200038.description: (C): A marked depression on the medial side of the scapula blade, often opposite the glenoid region.

(C) uberon-4200039.description: (C): A bony protuberance dorsal to the acetabulum on the ilium, confluent with the supraacetabular crest (when present). Acts as a bone brace to prevent excessive femoral abduction and the origin site for part of the M. iliofemoralis.

(C) uberon-4200040.description: (C): Anatomical process located in the proximal region of the coracoid in avian theropods, that is hook-shaped.

(C) uberon-4200042.description: (C): Anatomical projection on the ilium, anchoring caudal muscles.

(C) uberon-4200043.description: (C): Fossa located on the brevis shelf.

body: [articular surface for the calcaneum on the astragalus](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_4200044)
(C) uberon-4200044.description: (C): Contact surface between the calcaneum and the astragalus located on the astragalus.
(C) uberon-4200044.label_original: articular surface for the calcaneum on the astragalus

body: [articular surface for the astragalus on the calcaneum](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_4200045)
(C) uberon-4200045.description: (C): Contact surface between the calcaneum and the astragalus located on the calcaneum.
(C) uberon-4200045.label_original: articular surface for the astragalus on the calcaneum

(C) uberon-4200046.description: (C): The astragalo-calcaneal canal forms a foramen between the articulated astragalus and calcaneum when the canal is ossified (Nesbitt, 2011).

(C) uberon-4200048.description: (C): Anatomical projection that is an expansion on the proximal region of the humerus.

(C) uberon-4200049.description: (C): A sesamoid found in the found in the ligamentum calcanei of a wide variety of frogs. (based on Nussbaum, R. A. 1982.

(C) uberon-4200051.description: (C): A notch or opening in the ventral part of the acetabular rim.

(C) uberon-4200052.description: (C): Tuberosity on the posterior surface of the lateral femoral condyle.

(C) uberon-4200053.description: (C): An internally and externally symmetrical tail (caudal) fin.

(C) uberon-4200054.description: (C): Type of tail (caudal) fin in which the vertebral column turns upwards into the upper lobe which is longer than the lower. Asymmetrical externally as well as internally.

(C) uberon-4200055.description: (C): Type of tail fin in which the vertebrae generally turn upward at the hind end of the column, but which is externally symmetrical. The fin rays of the caudal are supported by hypaxial elements.

(C) uberon-4200056.description: (C): Type of tail fin where the lower lobe is the longer and is supported by the vertebral column. Asymmetrical externally as well as internally.

(C) uberon-4200060.description: (C): Formen present on the ectepicondyle of the humerus.

(C) uberon-4200061.description: (C): Tail fin in which the the caudal part of the notochord tapers posterodorsally. Based on Pradel et al. 2007.

(C) uberon-4200062.description: (C): Caudal fin lepidotrichium located upon or above the notochord.

(C) uberon-4200063.description: (C): Posteriorly projecting bony tubercle that is located proximal to the lateral condyle of the femur.

(C) uberon-4200068.description: (C): A small plate of cartilage synchondrotically united with the pubis. Modified from Baez and Harrison 2005.

(C) uberon-4200069.description: (C): The vertical plate of bone or cartilage attached to the median line of the sternum. Modified from Baumel et al. 1993.

(C) uberon-4200075.description: (C): A spine that is part of some fin.

(C) uberon-4200076.description: (C): An opening in the dermal armour of basal gnathostomes that encloses the pectoral fins. (modified from Young 2010).

(C) uberon-4200077.description: (C): Distinct posterior most of the two 'double heads' of the blade of the ilium.

(C) uberon-4200078.description: (C): A notch for the articulation of the clavicle on other girdle elements.

(C) uberon-4200080.description: (C): A bony projection on the lateral side of the tibia, allowing contact between the later and the fibula.

(C) uberon-4200081.description: (C): Zone of bone organ located on the flat ventral side of the distal region of the furcula, serving as attachment region for pectoral muscles.

(C) uberon-4200083.description: (C): Centrale in the postaxial region of the mesopodium.

(C) uberon-4200084.description: (C): Centrale in the preaxial side of the mesopodium.

(C) uberon-4200085.description: (C): The scapula's contribution to the glenoid fossa.

(C) uberon-4200086.description: (C): A constricted region of the ilium which is dorsal to the acetabulular region. Prior to the expansion of the iliac blade.

(C) uberon-4200087.description: (C): Bony projection that is part of the dorsal surface of the ischim, where it articulates with the ilium.

(C) uberon-4200088.description: (C): Bony projection that is part of the dorsal surface of the pubis where it meets the ilium.

(C) uberon-4200089.description: (C): Articular surface on calcaneum for the fibula.

(C) uberon-4200125.description: (C): Anatomical projection (crest) located dorsaly to the acetabulum.

(C) uberon-4200139.description: (C): Endochondral element that is part of the suspensorium sometimes ossifying distally as the quadrate bone and linking the basal section of the braincase to the lower jaw.

(C) uberon-4200140.description: (C): Is a endochondral element that is part of the mesopodial skeleton and is contained within the prepollex which in some taxa appears as a pre-axial digit-like projection anterior to the first digit of the hand.

(C) uberon-4200141.description: (C): Is a endochondral element that is part of the mesopodial skeleton and is contained within the prehallux which in some taxa appears as a pre-axial digit-like projection anterior to the first digit of the foot.

(C) uberon-4300037.description: (C): Fin ray that is composed of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-4440011.description: (C): Lepidotrichium that is part of a paired fin.

(C) uberon-4500008.description: (C): Lepidotrichium that is part of a median fin.

(C) uberon-4200214.description: (C): Facets for the articulation of the epipodial (zeugopodial) elements.

(C) uberon-4200090.description: (C): Articular surface on the astragalus for the fibula.

(C) uberon-4200091.description: (C): Region consisitng of the ethmoid and sphenoid bones.

(C) uberon-4200092.description: (C): Eminence on the proximo-dorsal surface of the ungual, for attachment of flexor muscles.

(C) uberon-4200094.description: (C): The medial most digit of the manus skeleton.

(C) uberon-4200095.description: (C): Process on infraspinous (region below the spine) of scapula.

(C) uberon-4200096.description: (C): The deep fossa between the femoral condyles in which the cruciate ligaments are attached. From Medilexicon.com.

(C) uberon-4200097.description: (C): Spine ventrally located on the body and not part of the pectoral, pelvic or anal fins.

(C) uberon-4200098.description: (C): Expansion of the distal region of the ischium.

(C) uberon-4200099.description: (C): The most lateral of the paired series of extrascapular bones and is the bone where the intersection of the otic, postotic and extrascapular or supratemporal canals occur.

(C) uberon-4200100.description: (C): A bony process on the dorsal side of the proximal region of the humerus which corresponds to the insertion site of the Latissimus dorsi muscle.

(C) uberon-4200101.description: (C): Muscle that represents one branch of the larger triceps brachii, origination site near the glenoid fossa on the scapula.

(C) uberon-4200102.description: (C): Dermal armour plate that is situated behind the head and constitute the dorsal most portion of the dermal shoulder girdle. Modified from Brazeau 2009, Young 2010.

(C) uberon-4200103.description: (C): The medial of the the paired series of extrascapular bones which carries the extrascapular or supratemporal canal.

(C) uberon-4200104.description: (C): Pits located on the proximodorsal part of metacarpals denoting the attachemnt sites for ligaments.

(C) uberon-4200106.description: (C): A distinct region on a skeletal element that demarcates the attachment area of a muscle or tendon. Often associated with rugosity or tubercles.

(C) uberon-4200107.description: (C): Process located on the ventral shaft of the ischium that denotes the attachment site of the pubio-ischio-femoralis externus.

(C) uberon-4200108.description: (C): The flanking digit of the manus.

(C) uberon-4200109.description: (C): The flanking digit of the pes.

(C) uberon-4200110.description: (C): Spine located anterior to the pectoral fin.

(C) uberon-4200111.description: (C): Spine located anterior to the pelvic fin and posterior to the pectoral fin.

(C) uberon-4200112.description: (C): A triangular, anteroventrally facing area developed between the preaxial margin of the humerus and the proximal limb of the ventral humeral ridge. Based on Callier et al. 2009 .

(C) uberon-4200114.description: (C): Elongate process forming the anteriormost part of the pubis.

(C) uberon-4200115.description: (C): An skeletal element of the upper pectoral girdle overlapped by the opercular and posttemporal bones.

(C) uberon-4200116.description: (C): Slender bone connected to the carpus in pterosaurs. The bone, which may have pointed forward, supports the propatagium, a membrane located between the carpus and pectoral region.

(C) uberon-4200117.description: (C): Anteroposterior expansion of the distal region of the pubis.

(C) uberon-4200118.description: (C): Bony projection on the anterior portion of the ilium, anterior to the acetabulum that articulates with the pubis.

(C) uberon-4200119.description: (C): Contact zone between the pubis and the ischium.

(C) uberon-4200120.description: (C): A broad expnase of bone incorperating both the pubis and the ischium. Origin site for ventral limb muscle including the pubioishciofemoralis externus. Modified from Romer 1956 .

(C) uberon-4200122.description: (C): Originates in on the pubic cartillage and inserts on the tibia, acts to adduct the hindlimb. Modified from De luliis and Pulera.

(C) uberon-4200123.description: (C): The dorsal extension of the scapulocoracoid above the level of the glenoid region in basal gnathostomes. Modified from Brazeau 2009.

(C) uberon-4200124.description: (C): Anatomical projections that are  elongate processes in the mid and posterior regions of the sternum.

(C) uberon-4200126.description: (C): Bony rim that is part of the supraacetabular region.

(C) uberon-4200127.description: (C): The route through which structures pass between the base of the neck and the posterior scapular region. It is formed by the suprascapular notch of the scapula and the superior transverse scapular ligament. From http://medical-dictionary.thefreedictionary.com/suprascapular+foramen.

(C) uberon-4200128.description: (C): Series of fused cervical vertebrae or vertebral elements. Based on Jeffrey C. Carrier. Biology of Sharks and Their Relatives, 2012. CRC Press.

(C) uberon-4200129.description: (C): Axial subdivision that includes a series of fused cervical vertebrae or vertebral elements. Based on Jeffrey C. Carrier. Biology of Sharks and Their Relatives, 2012. CRC Press.

(C) uberon-4200130.description: (C): Facet for the articulation of the tibia on the astragalus (talus).

(C) uberon-4200131.description: (C): Anatomical projection on the anterolateral region of the proximal end of the femur.

(C) uberon-4200132.description: (C): OBSOLETE Eminence or swelling on anatomical surface.

(C) uberon-4200133.description: (C): A ridge or similar projection rising above the surface of an anatomical structure.

(C) uberon-4200134.description: (C): A part in the body of an organism that corresponds to an opposite symmetrical part.

(C) uberon-4200135.description: (C): A transverse flattened or cylindrical plate in the posterior body wall opposite the anterior ends of the pelvic fins, in front of the vent and at the posterior end of the body cavity, that supports a few anterior pelvic radials and a basal cartilage, the basipterygium.  from  Leonard J. V. Compagno. 2001. Sharks of the World: An Annotated and Illustrated Catalogue of Shark Species Known to Date. Volume 2.

(C) uberon-4200136.description: (C): A caudal fin with three lobes.

(C) uberon-4200150.description: (C): Foramen found on the humerus of tetrapodomorphs beyond the entepicondyle and ectepicondyle foramen. Often denoted as foramen 'c' and 'd' after Jarvik 1996.

(C) uberon-4200152.description: (C): Sesamoid bone in the tarsal region.

(C) uberon-4200159.description: (C): A collection of attached ridges on the ventrl surface of the femur consisting of the internal and fourth trochanters plus the adductor blade and crest. Most notible in early amniotes (based on Romer 1956).

(C) uberon-4200160.description: (C): The median series of bones supporting the pectoral fin of sarcopterygian fish. See Dipnomorpha. In the pectoral fin, the first mesomere is the humerus, the second the ulna, and the third probably the intermedium. The radius is the first preaxial radial. All other homologies are suspect. from http://palaeos.com/vertebrates/glossary.

(C) uberon-4200165.description: (C): A scute parte of the basal surface of the fin in Sarcopterygian fish.

(C) uberon-4200166.description: (C): The space between the bones of the tibia and the fibula.

(C) uberon-4200169.description: (C): Process on the humerus of basal tetrapods, anterior to the entepicondyle and associated with subscapularis muscle (based on Coates 1996).

(C) uberon-4200170.description: (C): Process on the humerus of basal tetrapods, anterior to the entepicondyle and adjacent to process 4 of entepicondyle (see Coates 1996).

(C) uberon-4200171.description: (C): Process on the humerus of basal tetrapods, anterior to the entepicondyle and adjacent to process 3 of entepicondyle (see Coates 1996).

(C) uberon-4200174.description: (C): The area encompassing the radial and ulnar condyles of the humerus.

(C) uberon-4200176.description: (C): A bony dorsal extension of the clavicle.

(C) uberon-4200180.description: (C): The moon shaped fusion of distal carpals 1 and 2 found in some theropod dinosaurs, permitting greater wrist mobility.

(C) uberon-4200181.description: (C): The region of the astragalus/ talus that carries the articular surface for the navicular or central metatarsal.

(C) uberon-4200183.description: (C): The rough eminence which is on the anterior inner aspect of the neck of the radius and into which the tendon of the biceps is inserted. From http://www.merriam-webster.com/medical.

(C) uberon-4200184.description: (C): His roughened area of bone sits distomedially at the base of the coronoid process. It is the attachment site for the brachialis muscle. From http://www.anatomyexpert.com/.

(C) uberon-4200185.description: (C): A fossa on the distal humerus proximal to the entepicondyle.

(C) uberon-4200187.description: (C): Increase the number of phalanges per digit beyond their ancestral digital  formulas. Modified from Cooper and Dawson 2009.

(C) uberon-4200190.description: (C): An articular process on anterior surface of neural arch of vertebrae which fits into zygantrum. Modified from Henderson's dictionary of Biological terms 12th Edition.

(C) uberon-4200191.label_original: obsolete humeral facet of the ulna

(C) uberon-4200193.description: (C): Anatomical project part of the blade of the ilium that projects posteriorly.

(C) uberon-4200194.description: (C): The anteriormost of the two possible elements found in the tetrapod centrum (when the centrum is not a single element).

(C) uberon-4200195.description: (C): The posteriormost of the two possible elements found in the tetrapod centrum (when the centrum is not a single element).

(C) uberon-4200196.description: (C): The intercentrum unit of the atlas vertebra.

(C) uberon-4200197.description: (C): Ridge or keel at the proximal end of the humerus. (see Laurin 1998).

(C) uberon-4200198.description: (C): Process that is part of the mandible that is in close proximity to the incisor teeth.

(C) uberon-4200199.description: (C): Ciliary restraint system in the inner ear that uses sallets instead of the tectorial membrane.

(C) uberon-4200203.description: (C): Facet on the ulna for articulation with the ulnar condyle of the humerus.

(C) uberon-4200204.description: (C): Facet on the radius for articulation with the radial condyle of the humerus.

(C) uberon-4200206.description: (C): The internal part of the rim denoting the coracoid foramen.

(C) uberon-4200207.description: (C): The external wall of the rim denoting the coracoid foramen.
(C) uberon-4200207.label_original: external rim of the coracoid foramen

(C) uberon-4200208.description: (C): Radial bone found in between the proximal and distal radial bones.

(C) uberon-4200209.description: (C): A projection on the postaxial region of the ulnare.

(C) uberon-4200210.description: (C): A projection on the postaxial region of the femur.

(C) uberon-4200211.description: (C): A projection on the postaxial region of the fibula.

(C) uberon-4200216.description: (C): Facet on the femur for the fibula.

(C) uberon-4200217.description: (C): Facet on the femur for the tibia.

(C) uberon-4200218.description: (C): A collection of muscle and tendinous tissue.

(C) uberon-4200221.description: (C): Distinct layer that indicate the growth of an organism.

(C) uberon-4200222.description: (C): Groove along the distal margin of the humerus, ventral to the radial and ulnar condyle.

(C) uberon-4200223.description: (C): Foramen located on the scapulocoracoid, located just behind the cleithral anteroventral process(the articulation with the cleithrum). Modified from Coates 1996.

(C) uberon-4200224.description: (C): Modified from Garvey et al. 2005. ' Between the dorsal ridge and the caput humeri is a futher recessed area......that clearly separates the two structures and is slightly separted from the dorsal surface of the entepicondyle, and more specifically from the unfinished bone of the entepicondyle, by a narrow ridge.'.

(C) uberon-4200225.description: (C): Muscle found primarily in basal sarcopterygians that runs between teh scapulocoracoid and the humerus. Its exact homologies with more derived shoulder muscles in Tetrapoda is unclear.

(C) uberon-4200226.description: (C): A ramus of the celithrum that descend along the girdle. Its rounded outer surface forms the articulation surface for the clavicle while its anterior surface overlaps with the anterior process of the scapulocoracoid.

(C) uberon-4200231.description: (C): A bone surface that is not smooth and periosteal.  The usual implication is that the bone was still growing, was covered in cartilage, or both. From Paleos.com.

(C) uberon-4200233.description: (C): A process, extending dorsally from the clavicular plate, that attaches to the cleithrum. Modified from Clack 2012 and Coates 1996.

(C) uberon-4200243.description: (C): ...a v-shaped pair of ridges, each carrying three or four smallpores Modified from Ahlberg et al. 2005.

(C) uberon-4200245.description: (C): Bone, often with tooth attachments, on the lingual side of the anterior of the lower jaw.

(C) uberon-4200250.description: (C): The ossification of the Meckel's cartilage.

(C) uberon-4300001.description: (C): A fossa that is a depression in the proximal end of the maxilla involved in articulation with the palatine [Baldwin, CC and Johnson GD. 1996. Interrelationships of Aulopiformes. Pages 355-404 in MLJ Stiassny, LR Parenti, and DG Johnson, (eds.), Interrelationships of fishes. Academic Press, San Diego, CA.].

(C) uberon-4300002.description: (C): A process on the palatine that projects outward and upward and articulates with a depression (maxillary saddle) in the proximal end of the maxilla [Gosline WA et al, 1966; Baldwin, CC and Johnson GD. 1996. Interrelationships of Aulopiformes. Pages 355-404 in MLJ Stiassny, LR Parenti, and DG Johnson, (eds.), Interrelationships of fishes. Academic Press, San Diego, CA.].

(C) uberon-4300003.description: (C): Paired, thin dermal bones at the rear of the caudal fin skeleton, derived from scales.

(C) uberon-4300004.description: (C): A continuous flap of skin with scales implanted in pockets or invaginations [Baldwin, CC and Johnson GD. 1996. Interrelationships of Aulopiformes. Pages 355-404 in MLJ Stiassny, LR Parenti, and DG Johnson, (eds.), Interrelationships of fishes. Academic Press, San Diego, CA.].

(C) uberon-4300005.description: (C): The space in the pupil, which is not occupied by the lens. A rostral aphakic space may enhance the forward binocular field of vision.

(C) uberon-4300007.description: (C): Process that is posteriorly oriented and medially located on the basipterygium. It is a paired projection. [PHENOSCAPE:bf].

(C) uberon-4300008.description: (C): Anatomical cluster that consists of the epipleurals.

(C) uberon-4300012.description: (C): A rudder-like lobe formed from extensions of dorsal and anal fin rays.

(C) uberon-4300016.description: (C): Cartilage element associated with the pelvic fin in aulopiform fishes.

(C) uberon-4300017.description: (C): Dermal bone formed by the fusion of dermethmoids and rostral bones [Fink, W L Weitzman, S H. 1982. Relationships of the stomiiform fishes (Teleostei), with a description of Diplophos Bulletin of The Museum of Comparative Zoology 150:31-93. http://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/part/28697].

(C) uberon-4300018.description: (C): In the clasper skeleton, a flat semicylindrical cartilage that is partially fused to the lateral edge of the axial cartilage, and forms the lateral wall of the clasper groove [Compagno, L. 2001. Sharks of the World: An Annotated and Illustrated Catalogue of Shark Species Known to Date. Volume 2].

(C) uberon-4300019.description: (C): The large cartilage of the dorsal fin, on which the radials articulate distally [Compagno 2001. Sharks of the World: An Annotated and Illustrated Catalogue of Shark Species Known to Date. Volume 2].

(C) uberon-4300020.description: (C): The large cartilage of the anal fin, on which the radials articulate distally [Compagno 2001. Sharks of the World: An Annotated and Illustrated Catalogue of Shark Species Known to Date. Volume 2].

(C) uberon-4300021.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderm fishes.

(C) uberon-4300022.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, located in the ventral armour adjacent to the interolateral (IL) and anterior ventrolateral (AVL) plates.

(C) uberon-4300023.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, and located anterior to the anterior ventrolateral (AVL) plate.

(C) uberon-4300024.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, and located lateral to the anterior ventrolateral (AVL) plate.

(C) uberon-4300025.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, located posterior to the main components of the complex.

(C) uberon-4300026.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the ventral region of scapular complex in placoderms (see also posterior ventrolateral plate). In most placoderms with a long ventral armour, the ventral wall is typically composed of two large paired lateral plates (anterior and posterior ventrolaterals).

(C) uberon-4300028.description: (C): Dermal bone that is part of the ventral region of scapular complex in placoderms (see also anterior ventrolateral plate). In most placoderms with a long ventral armour, the ventral wall is typically composed of two large paired lateral plates (anterior and posterior ventrolaterals).

(C) uberon-4300029.description: (C): Dermal articulation between skull and shoulder girdle localized to paired dermal neck-joint between anterior dorsolateral plate (ADL) and paranuchal (PNu) plates in placoderms.

(C) uberon-4300031.description: (C): Membrane that connects the lepidotrichia or ceratotrichia of a fin.

(C) uberon-4300032.description: (C): The large cartilage of the posterior dorsal fin, on which the radials articulate distally.

(C) uberon-4300033.description: (C): The large cartilage of the anterior dorsal fin, on which the radials articulate distally.

(C) uberon-4300034.description: (C): Cartilage element on the neurocranium of sawsharks and batoids, separate cartilages attached to the sides of the nasal capsules that support the sides or front of the head. [Compagno, L.J.V. Sharks of the world. An annotated and illustrated catalogue of shark species known to date. Volume 2. Bullhead, mackerel and carpet sharks (Heterodontiformes, Lamniformes and Orectolobiformes). FAO Species Catalogue for Fishery Purposes. No. 1, Vol. 2. Rome, FAO. 2001. 269p. ISBN 92-5-104543-7].

(C) uberon-4400005.description: (C): A rod-like entity that functions in support of fin folds and fins.

(C) uberon-4400000.description: (C): The posterior and innermost of the three principal basal cartilages in the fins of fishes.

(C) uberon-4300090.description: (C): The x bone is a detached neural spine anterior to the neural spine of preural centrum 2.

(C) uberon-4300091.description: (C): The y bone is a detached neural spine anterior to the haemal spines of preural centrum 2.

(C) uberon-4300096.description: (C): Anal fin pterygiophore that is the anteriormost of the series.

(C) uberon-4300097.description: (C): Anal fin spine that is the anteriormost element of the series.

(C) uberon-4300098.description: (C): Anal fin spine that is located posteriorly adjacent to the first anal fin spine.

(C) uberon-4300101.description: (C): A small to large enameloid-covered, dentine-cored spine located on the anterior margins of one or both of the dorsal fins, found on bullhead sharks (Heterodontiformes), many dogfish sharks, fossil (but not living) batoids, chimaeroids, but lost entirely or buried in the fin bases of other shark-like fishes [Compagno, Sharks of the World].

(C) uberon-4400001.description: (C): Elastoidin fin ray that is thickened, generally unbranched and found in the fins of Chondrichthyes.

(C) uberon-4300102.description: (C): Scale that is posteriorly adjacent to the pectoral girdle [Cloutier and Arratia 2004, character 183].

(C) uberon-4300103.description: (C): Pectoral fin lepidtrichium that is small, unbranched and unsegmented.

(C) uberon-4300104.description: (C): A paired dermal bone in Gasterosteiformes connected with the coracoid and extending posteriorly. Has also been applied to the element below the scapula and applied to the coracoid in Dipnoi. Dictionary of Ichthyology.

(C) uberon-4300105.description: (C): Caudal vertebra that is the anteriormost element of the series.

(C) uberon-4300106.description: (C): Zone of bone organ that is the ventral extension of the posttemporal.

(C) uberon-4300108.description: (C): Zone of bone organ that is part of a lepidotrich and connected to other segments by collagen fibers. These segments lend flexibility to the lepidtrich.

(C) uberon-4300109.description: (C): Lepidotrichial segment that is part of the proximal region of a caudal fin ray.

(C) uberon-4300112.description: (C): Lepidotrichial segment that is part of the distal region of a caudal fin ray.

(C) uberon-4300114.description: (C): An adhesive disk modified from the pelvic fins in, for example, clingfishes (Gobiesocidae), gobies (Gobiidae) and snailfishes (Liparidae).

(C) uberon-4300115.description: (C): Distinctive first dorsal fin taking the form of a modified oval sucker-like organ with slat-like structures that open and close to create suction and take a firm hold against the skin of larger marine animals.

(C) uberon-4300119.description: (C): Region surrounding the glenoid fossa on the scapulocoracoid.

(C) uberon-4300120.description: (C): Region of dorsal fin that is composed of spinous rays (vs soft rays).

(C) uberon-4300121.description: (C): A fossa on the posterior median part of the neural arch of a vertebra (as of a snake) that accommodates the zygosphene of the next vertebra.

(C) uberon-4300122.description: (C): Posteriorly projecting processes allowing de facto contact between consecutive vertebrae (some soft tissues are also present) via articular facets.

(C) uberon-4300123.description: (C): Anatomical region lying to the anterior or dorsal side of the metapterygial axis.

(C) uberon-4300124.description: (C): The intercentrum unit of the axis vertebra. .

(C) uberon-4300125.description: (C): Ridge that is part of the ilium.

(C) uberon-4300126.description: (C): Tectorial restraint system is a type of ciliary restraint system for hair cells in the inner ear.  In tectorial restraint systems, the tectorial membrane restrains the cilia of the hair cells by attaching either directly to ciliary tufts or indirectly through various kinds of fibrous structure (simple fibers, fibrous strands, finger-like processes, tectorial plates) [Phylogenetic Relationships of the Lizard Families: Essays Commemorating Charles L. Camp. 1988. Eds. R Estes, GK Pregill. Stanford University Press].

(C) uberon-4300127.description: (C): Bony protuberance on the external surface of the occipital bone.[PHENOSCAPE:AD].

(C) uberon-4300128.description: (C): Elements of the sacrum joining true sacral vertebrae to pelvis [12th edition of Henderson's Dictionary of Biological terms].

(C) uberon-4300129.description: (C): Cloacal glands that secrete into the dorsal roof of the cloacal tube and or the anterior cloacal chamber. Found in male salamanders.

(C) uberon-4300132.description: (C): Foramen for the passage of the glossopharyngeal nerve IX.

(C) uberon-4300133.description: (C): The region of the upper jaw on or near the midline.

(C) uberon-4300134.description: (C): Region of the braincase which bears the facets for the hyomandibula in fishes. This region disappears in the origin of tetrapods and the space it occipied comes to contribute to the fenestra vestibulii. Clack, JA, 2001. Ch. 23, The otoccipital region. In Major Events in Early Vertebrate Evolution. Per Ahlberg editor.

(C) uberon-4300135.description: (C): Tooth of the upper jaw that is adjacent to the upper jaw symphysis.

(C) uberon-4300137.description: (C): The region of an anatomical structure (such as a tooth or jaw bone) facing the tongue.

(C) uberon-4300138.description: (C): The region of an anatomical structure, such as a tooth or jaw bone, facing the lips.[PHENOSCAPE:WD].

(C) uberon-4300139.description: (C): The region of an anatomical structure, such as a tooth or jaw bone, oriented posteriorly and facing the lips.

(C) uberon-4300140.description: (C): The region of an anatomical structure, such as a tooth or jaw bone, facing the midline of the jaw.

(C) uberon-4300142.description: (C): Foramen for the passage of the internal carotid artery.

(C) uberon-4300144.description: (C): Foramen for the profundus or ophthalmic nerve.

(C) uberon-4300147.description: (C): Subdivision of organism that is the basal region of the pectoral fin.

(C) uberon-4300151.description: (C): Cartilage element that lies between processes of the cleithrum and pelvic girdle in gobioid fishes. Posterodorsal to the ventral end of each cleithrum is a posteriorly projecting process. The pelvic intercleithral cartilage (an unpaired, median structure) forms a bridge between the processes (From Springer, 1983).

(C) uberon-4300152.description: (C): Accessory nasal sacs are found in a variety of teleosts (Webb, 1993) and likely assist in ventilating the olfactory epithelium by transmitting pressure fluctuations associated with gill irrigation from theoral cavity to the nasal (or sensory) sac (Jakubowski,1975; Webb, 1993; Belanger et al., 2003). [def from Eastman, J. T. and Lannoo, M. J. (2004)].

(C) uberon-4300153.description: (C): Sharpey's fibres (bone fibres, or perforating fibres) are a matrix of connective tissue consisting of bundles of strong collagenous fibres connecting periosteum to bone. They are part of the outer fibrous layer of periosteum, entering into the outer circumferential and interstitial lamellae of bone tissue.

(C) uberon-4300154.description: (C): A ventrally projecting spur on the posteriormost ventral procurrent caudal ray overlapping ventrally the preceding ray in various percomorphs (Johnson, 1975).

(C) uberon-4300155.description: (C): Unpaired bone that covers the base of the first pectoral ray. [Filleul and Lavoué 2001].

(C) uberon-4300157.description: (C): Region in the middle of the shaft of a long bone (e.g. humerus, femur etc).

(C) uberon-4300172.description: (C): A paired fin bud that develops into a pectoral fin.

(C) uberon-4300173.description: (C): A paired fin bud that develops into a pelvic fin.

(C) uberon-4300174.description: (C): A finger-like out-pocketing of the intestine where it meets the end of the stomach (pylorus). Also spelled cecum (ceca). Serves to aid digestion.

(C) uberon-4300175.description: (C): Fin spine that precedes the dorsal fin, oriented anteriorly towards the head of the fish.

(C) uberon-4300176.description: (C): Branch of supraorbital sensory canal that extends to the parietal.
(C) uberon-4300176.label_original: parietal branch of the supraorbital canal

(C) uberon-4300177.description: (C): Tooth row consisting of replacement teeth.

(C) uberon-4300178.description: (C): Dentary tooth row that is lingual in position relative to other tooth rows.

(C) uberon-4300179.description: (C): Tooth row on the premaxilla that is lingually located relative to other tooth rows.

(C) uberon-4300180.description: (C): The fleshy throat region of a fish which extends forward from the ventral part of the chest and narrows anteriorly, and externally separating the two gill chambers; that narrowed portion of the breast which lies between the gill chambers and separates them.

(C) uberon-4300181.description: (C): Sclerotic cartilage that is located posterior to the eye.

(C) uberon-4300182.description: (C): Sclerotic cartilage that is located anterior to the eye.

(C) uberon-4300184.description: (C): Neural spine that is associated with the fifth vertebra.

(C) uberon-4300185.description: (C): Neural spine that is associated with the sixth vertebra.

(C) uberon-4300186.description: (C): Neural spine that is associated with the seventh vertebra.

(C) uberon-4300188.description: (C): The posteriormost scale in a scale series.

(C) uberon-4300189.description: (C): Parapophysis that is the lateral projection from the third centrum. Parapophysis 3 is bilaterally paired.

(C) uberon-4300192.description: (C): Pelvic fin lepidotrichium that is distally branched and segmented.

(C) uberon-4300193.description: (C): Anal fin lepidotrichium that is not distally branched.

(C) uberon-4300194.description: (C): A light-emitting organ which appears as luminous spots on various marine animals, including fish and cephalopods.

(C) uberon-4300195.description: (C): Consists of a set of tubuli occupying the space between the external dermal bones above the dorsal and anterior wal of the nasal capsule below. Thomson and Campbell (1971).

(C) uberon-4300197.description: (C): More or less concentric lines of discontinuity in the cosmine of Dipnoi, probably due to cyclic resorption and redeposition during growth occurring on the bases of individual scales and also as large structures between headshield plates.[Fishbase].

(C) uberon-4300198.description: (C): Radial found above the vertebral column.

(C) uberon-4300199.description: (C): Dermal bone of the lower jaw.

(C) uberon-4300200.description: (C): Dermal bones (postparietals, supratemporals, intertemporals, extrascapulars) posterior to the intracranial joint. Forey 1997.

(C) uberon-4300201.description: (C): Fossa for epaxial musculature inserting on the braincase. Forey et al. 1996.

(C) uberon-4300202.description: (C): The braincase of most plesiomorphic sarcopterygians is divided by the intracranial point into ethmosphenoid and otic-occipital portions each covered by dermal bones. The function of the joint is presumably to increase the gape of the mouth rapidly during opening phases. (Forey 1997).

(C) uberon-4300203.description: (C): The dorsal portion of the endocranium that covers the orbital region. Hanken and Hall (1993).

(C) uberon-4300204.description: (C): Structures that communicate with the main olfactory chamber and may be located posterior, ventral, or dorsal to it [De Pinna, 1996].

(C) uberon-4300205.description: (C): Ligament between the palatine and maxilla [Stiassny 1986].

(C) uberon-4300206.description: (C): Ligament that connects the ventromedial end of the lacrimal to the anguloarticular (or 'mandible'). Parenti (2008).

(C) uberon-4300208.description: (C): A series of plate like bones found ventrally to the jaw.

(C) uberon-4300210.description: (C): Dorsal gill-arch muscle connecting right and left epibranchial 2s. Springer and Johnson (2015).

(C) uberon-4300211.description: (C): Body plates on the lateral sides of the body that occur as single bilateral rows and their number is highly heritable. Bell and Richkind (1981).

(C) uberon-4300212.description: (C): Odontoid tissue forming a cap on teeth found in teeth of actinopterygian fishes.

(C) uberon-4300222.description: (C): Scale that is adjacent to the pelvic fin and aligned with the origin of the pelvic fin. It is typically an elongate scale.[Mattox and Toledo-Piza 2012].

(C) uberon-4300224.description: (C): Vertebral elements lacking hemal spines (Weitzman, 1962), refers generally to the anterior vertebral region bounding the abdominal cavity. Alternate but not quite synonymous terms are abdominal or trunk vertebrae, which bear parapophyses and ribs. In many actinopterygians dorsal to the posterior abdominal cavity there are transitional vertebrae lacking ribs but also without hemal spines or sometimes even enclosed hemal arches. The primary definition would identify these vertebrae as precaudal.(Bird and Mabee, 2003).

(C) uberon-4300225.description: (C): Vertebral cartilage elements lacking hemal spines (Weitzman, 1962), refers generally to the anterior vertebral region bounding the abdominal cavity. Alternate but not quite synonymous terms are abdominal or trunk vertebrae, which bear parapophyses and ribs. In many actinopterygians dorsal to the posterior abdominal cavity there are transitional vertebrae lacking ribs but also without hemal spines or sometimes even enclosed hemal arches. The primary definition would identify these vertebrae as precaudal.(Bird and Mabee, 2003).

(C) uberon-4300226.description: (C): Mesenchyme that is part of a forelimb bud.

(C) uberon-4300227.description: (C): Mesenchyme that is part of a hindlimb bud.

(C) uberon-4300228.description: (C): Mesechyme that is part of a pectoral fin bud.

(C) uberon-4300229.description: (C): Mesechyme that is part of a pelvic fin bud.

(C) uberon-4300230.description: (C): A wing bud that develops into a wing.

(C) uberon-4300231.description: (C): Mesenchyme that is part of a forelimb wing bud.

(C) uberon-4300233.description: (C): Calcareous tooth with a hyptertrophied base.

(C) uberon-4300234.description: (C): Series of scales in which each scale envelopes or overlaps an adjacent scale.

(C) uberon-4300235.description: (C): A cycloid scale bearing a serrated margin; superficially similar to ctenoid scales but having spines as outgrowths of the scale as oppose to true ctenii.

(C) uberon-4300236.description: (C): Rib that articulates with the parapophysis of the seventh centrum.

(C) uberon-4300237.description: (C): Rib that articulates with the parapophysis of the eighth centrum.

(C) uberon-4300239.description: (C): Hindlimb that is used to propel an animal through water.

(C) uberon-4300240.description: (C): Ossicle that surrounds the sensory canals of the snout when passing from the ethmoidal commissure to the infraorbital series and have first been noticed by Nybelin [14] in Elops. From: Filleul and Lavoué. (2001). Basal teleosts and the question of elopomorph monophyly. Morphological and molecular approaches. Comptes rendus de l'Académie des sciences. Série III, Sciences de la vie. 324. 393-9. 10.1016/S0764-4469(00)01302-0.

(C) uberon-4300241.description: (C): Sensory canal that traverses the rostral bone.

(C) uberon-4300242.description: (C): The sixth scale in the lateral line series.

(C) uberon-4300243.description: (C): Premaxillary tooth that is the second tooth in a premaxillary tooth series, and positioned adjacent to the symphyseal tooth.

(C) uberon-4300244.description: (C): Premaxillary tooth that is the third tooth in a premaxillary tooth series, and positioned adjacent to the second tooth.

(C) uberon-6000128.description: (C): The mesoderm of segments T1-A9. It first becomes morphologically distinct during ventral furrow formation. Following invagination during stages 6 and 7, it remains a coherent structure with no morphologically apparent subdivisions, apart from transient metamery during stage 9, until stage 11. It undergoes a number of morphological changes during this period: as its cells divide following invagination, it loses its epithelial integrity and by stage 9 has rearranged into a monolayer of cuboidal cells. A further division happens during stage 10 leading to two distinct layers by stage 11.

(C) uberon-6001668.description: (C): Hematopoietic organ of the larva, located along the dorsal vessel, behind the brain. It produces the plasmatocytes, crystal cells and lamellocytes which are released at the end of the larval instar and onset of metamorphosis. It is composed of 3 pairs of bilateral lobes: an anterior primary lobe, a posterior secondary lobe and the most posterior lobe (or multiple lobes), the tertiary lobe. Each lobe is separated by pericardial cells. In the late embryo, the lymph gland consists of a single pair of lobes (primary lobes) containing around 20 cells each that flank the dorsal vessel. By the second larval instar, the lymph gland is composed of two or three new pairs of posterior lobes, and the primary lobes have increased in size to contain around 200 cells. During the first and early second larval instars, the lymph gland comprises only the hematopoietic progenitor population. The lymph gland increases in size ten-fold by the late third instar, and at this stage the progenitor cells (prohemocytes) become restricted to the medial region (medullary zone) of the primary lobe and become quiescent. The differentiated hemocytes are found in the periphery (cortical zone) of the primary lobe and these cells proliferate extensively. The posterior signalling center is a group of about 30 cells at the posterior tip of the primary lobe that secretes several signalling molecules and functions as a stem-cell niche. The secondary and tertiary lobes contain prohemocytes, and rarely a differentiated cell. Lymph glands are eliminated at metamorphosis.

(C) uberon-6005467.description: (C): Primordium of the insect embryo that gives rise to the embryonic/larval lymph gland.

(C) uberon-6001722.description: (C): A closely associated cluster of three neuroendocrine glands located anterior to the aorta and dorsal to the esophagus. At embryonic stage 17 and in larva it is found anterior to the brain and is formed by the corpus cardiacum ventrally, the prothoracic gland laterally and the corpus allatum dorsally. The adult ring gland is located anterior to the proventriculus and is formed by the corpus cardiacum ventrally, the corpus allatum dorsally and the hypocerebral ganglion posterior to the corpus cardiacum. It is innervated by neurons of the nervus corporis cardiaci (NccI-III).

(C) uberon-6005036.description: (C): Deep and narrow pit formed by the invagination of a tracheal placode in a late extended germ band embryo. Invagination of the placode begins during stage 11. Branches begin to bud from the pit during stage 11, with a dorsal and ventral stem being apparent by mid-stage 12. The pit closes over during stage 13. There are 10 pairs of tracheal pits - one pair in each tracheal metamere (each segment from T2 to A8). Pits are located in the central one third of each parasegment, with the most anterior in parasegment 4 and the most posterior in parasegment 14.

(C) uberon-6005037.description: (C): Primordium of a single tracheal metamere of the embryonic/larval tracheal system from its appearance as a placode during stage 11 to the completion of fusion with adjacent tracheal metameres in stage 15/16. There are 10 pairs of tracheal primordia - one pair in each segment from T2 to A8. Each tracheal primordium originates as a slight depression in the lateral ectoderm during stage 10 known as a tracheal placode. During stage 11, these placodes invaginate to form tracheal pits that elongate and branch. These pits close over during stage 13. Fusion of tracheal primordia begins at stage 14 with fusion of the dorsal trunk primordia and is complete by early stage 16.

(C) uberon-6007046.description: (C): An insect embryonic structure that develops from the dorsal ectoderm.

(C) uberon-6005569.description: (C): The sum of all the structures in the embryo that will develop into the embryonic/larval tracheal system. This corresponds to the tracheal primordia and their component tracheal branch primordia along with primordia of the spiracles.

(C) uberon-6005054.description: (C): Opening of the tracheal system on the surface of the body.

(C) uberon-6005070.description: (C): The visceral musculature comprises circular and longitudinal fibers which surround the entire intestinal tract, with the exception of the recurrent layer of the proventriculus. The circular fibers derive from a bilaterally symmetrical band of mesodermal cells extending continuously throughout most of the germ band. The longitudinal fibers derive from clusters of mesodermal cells which appear during stage 12 at the posterior end of the embryo and migrate anteriorly.

(C) uberon-8400001.description: (C): The region of the hepatic acinus that is closest to the arterial blood supply and has the highest oxygen concentration. Zone 1 is located in the periportal region of the liver lobule, closest to the portal triad. Hepatocytes in this region are primarily involved in oxidative energy metabolism.

(C) uberon-8400005.description: (C): Any of the metabolic zones found in the liver. Liver tissue is heterogenous at the level of morphometry and histochemistry. This heterogeneity is linked to the position of a cell within the functional unit of the tissue, which, in turn, is related to the blood supply: cells located in the upstream zone differ from those in the downstream zone with respect to subcellular structures, key enzymes, translocators, and receptors and, therefore, have different metabolic capacities. This is the basis for 'metabolic zonation', a concept first proposed in mammals for carbohydrate metabolism and later expanded to include amino acid and ammonia metabolism, xenobiotic metabolism, protective metabolism, and formation of plasma proteins.

(C) uberon-8400006.description: (C): The region of the liver lobule that is closest to the portal triad. The functionally-defined hepatic acinus zone 1 is generally found in this region.

(C) uberon-8400002.description: (C): The region of the hepatic acinus immediately surrounding the central veins. This region has the lowest oxygen concentration in the acinus. Zone 3 is located in the centrilobular region of the liver lobule, closest to the central vein. Hepatocytes in this region are the primary location for the biotransformation of drugs.

(C) uberon-8400007.description: (C): The region of the liver lobule that is closest to the central vein. The functionally-defined hepatic acinus zone 3 is generally found in this region.

(C) uberon-8400003.description: (C): The region of the hepatic acinus in between zones 1 and 3. Blood in this region has an intermediate oxygen concentration relative to the other two zones of the hepatic acinus. Zone 2 is located in the midzonal region of the liver lobule. Hepatocytes in this region have mixed functionality in comparison with those in zones 1 and 3.

(C) uberon-8400008.description: (C): The region of the liver lobule that is between the periportal and centrilobular regions. The functionally-defined hepatic acinus zone 2 is generally found in this region.

(C) uberon-8400024.description: (C): Region of liver parenchyma immediately below the capsule. This region is frequently specified in pathology diagnoses.

(C) uberon-8410003.description: (C): In human, ductal plate is a double-layered cylindrical structure of bile duct epithelium that surrounds the portal ramifications by the eighth gestational week. After approximately the 12th gestational week, remodelling of ductal plate begins, and maturity is attained by the end of gestation or early postnatal period.

(C) uberon-8410005.description: (C): Glandular epithelium of the anal transition zone. The anal transition zone is defined loosely as the tissue interposed between the uninterrupted squamous epithelium of the anoderm and the uninterrupted mucosal epithelium of the anal canal in the anorectum.
