(C) uberon-8410017.description: (C): A portal vein that drains the descending colon. It is a tributary of the inferior mesenteric vein, and follows the path of its corresponding artery, the left colic artery.

(C) uberon-8410018.description: (C): A portal vein that drains the ascending colon. It is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein, and travels with its corresponding artery, the right colic artery.

(C) uberon-8410019.description: (C): The area where the jejunum ends and the ileum part of the intestine begins. Although there is no clear distinct section, the ileum is narrower and has smaller villi than the jejunum.

(C) uberon-8410020.description: (C): A venule located in the vermiform appendix.

(C) uberon-8410021.description: (C): The skin covering the inguinal region between the abdomen and the thigh on either side of the pubic bone.

(C) uberon-8410022.description: (C): The first branch of the inferior mesenteric artery (IMA) is the left colic artery. The left colic artery supplies blood flow to the distal third of the transverse colon and the entirety of the descending colon. Once diverging from the IMA, the left colic artery runs anterior to the left ureter, left internal spermatic vessels (males), and psoas major before branching into its ascending and descending segments.

(C) uberon-8410023.description: (C): The right colic artery may arise directly from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) but often arises from a common trunk with the ileocolic artery or middle colic artery. It supplies the ascending colon.

(C) uberon-8410025.description: (C): The region of the prostate gland anterior to the central and peripheral zones, surrounding the proximal urethra. It is the zone of the human prostate gland that grows the most throughout life, and is responsible for benign prostatic hypertrophy.

(C) uberon-8410026.description: (C): The region of the prostate that is located posterior to the central and transition zones, surrounding the distal urethra. It is the zone of origin for the vast majority of human prostatic cancers.

(C) uberon-8410027.description: (C): The region of the prostate gland that is located between the peripheral and transition zones, surrounding the ejaculatory ducts. It gives rise to a very small percentage of human prostate cancers, often aggressive and invading the seminal vesicles.

(C) uberon-8410028.description: (C): An arteriole located in the vermiform appendix.

(C) uberon-8410029.description: (C): A lymphatic capillary that is located in the vermiform appendix.

(C) uberon-8410030.description: (C): A lymphatic vessel located in the vermiform appendix.

(C) uberon-8410031.description: (C): A muscularis mucosa that is part of a vermiform appendix.

(C) uberon-8410032.description: (C): The trabecular sinus is the lymph-filled space outside the trabeculae between lobules of the lymph node. This is a continuation of the subcapsular sinus which receives the afferent vessels and is present beneath the capsule. This space is traversed by both reticular fibers and cells in the lymph.

(C) uberon-8410033.description: (C): A vein where lymph node venules condense and which exits at the lymph node hilum. It is also called hilar vein.

(C) uberon-8410034.description: (C): An artery that enters the lymph node at the hilum and branches into smaller arterioles.

(C) uberon-8410035.description: (C): An arteriole that arises from the hilar artery of a lymph node and radiates centrifugally, branching in the medulla.

(C) uberon-8410042.description: (C): An arteriole that is part of a lymph node.

(C) uberon-8410036.description: (C): Medullary venules are a continuation of high endothelial venules which condense repeatedly in the interfollicular cortex and peripheral deep cortical unit and then transition to medullary venules at the corticomedullary junction. The medullary venules condense and return centripetally to the hilar vein.

(C) uberon-8410041.description: (C): A venule that is part of a lymph node.

(C) uberon-8410037.description: (C): High endothelial venules are specialized blood vessels adapted for lymphocyte trafficking. They form a spatially organized network, which controls both the type of lymphocyte and the site of entry into lymphoid tissues. Uniquely, high endothelial venules express vascular addressins that regulate lymphocyte entry into lymphoid organs. They perform this function in all lymphoid organs except the spleen.

(C) uberon-8410038.description: (C): A high endothelial venule that is part of a of lymph node.
(C) uberon-8410038.label_original: high endothelial venule of lymph node

(C) uberon-8410039.description: (C): A high endothelial venule that is located in the vermiform appendix.

body: [high endothelial venule of small intestine Peyer's patch](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8410040)
(C) uberon-8410040.description: (C): A high endothelial venule that is located in a Peyer's patch in the small intestine.
(C) uberon-8410040.label_original: high endothelial venule of small intestine Peyer's patch

(C) uberon-8410044.description: (C): A vein that is part of a vermiform appendix.

(C) uberon-8410045.description: (C): An artery that is part of a vermiform appendix.

(C) uberon-8410046.description: (C): A circular muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a vermiform appendix smooth muscle.

(C) uberon-8410047.description: (C): A longitudinal muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a vermiform appendix smooth muscle.

(C) uberon-8410049.description: (C): A nerve fiber that is located in the serosa of vermiform appendix.

(C) uberon-8410051.description: (C): A lymphatic vessel located in the colon.

(C) uberon-8410052.description: (C): Lymph node germinal centers contain two microenvironments: the light zone and the dark zone. The light zone is sparsely populated with B cells and includes additional cell types such as follicular dendritic cells, lymph node tingible macrophages and T follicular helper cells.
(C) uberon-8410052.label_original: lymph node germinal center light zone

(C) uberon-8410053.description: (C): Lymph node germinal centers contain two microenvironments: the light zone and the dark zone. The dark zone is densely populated with B cell blasts and reticular cells.
(C) uberon-8410053.label_original: lymph node germinal center dark zone

(C) uberon-8410054.description: (C): A lymphatic capillary located in the colon.

(C) uberon-8410055.description: (C): A lymphatic capillary located in the anorectum.

(C) uberon-8410058.description: (C): Myenteric nerve plexus that is located in the colon.

(C) uberon-8410059.description: (C): Submucous nerve plexus that is located in the colon.

(C) uberon-8410060.description: (C): A circular muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a colon smooth muscle.

(C) uberon-8410061.description: (C): A longitudinal muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a colon smooth muscle.

(C) uberon-8410062.description: (C): A parasympathetic nerve that releases acetylcholine.

(C) uberon-8410063.description: (C): Myenteric nerve plexus that is part of the small intestine.
(C) uberon-8410063.label_original: myenteric nerve plexus of small intestine

(C) uberon-8410064.description: (C): Submucous nerve plexus that is located in the small intestine.
(C) uberon-8410064.label_original: submucous nerve plexus of small intestine

(C) uberon-8410065.description: (C): Histologically, the marginal zone pattern of the lymph node is characterized by lymphoid follicles with three distinct layers. The inner layer is composed of follicular center zones, the middle layer of darkly stained mantle zones, and the outer layer of marginal zones. However, the marginal zone pattern is rarely seen in reactive lymph nodes except for mesenteric lymph nodes. Lymph node marginal zones are populated by marginal zone B cells which express CD19 and CD20 and have the phenotypic features of memory B cells.

(C) uberon-8410066.description: (C): The lymph node paracortex is the middle layer of the lymph node and is mostly populated by T cells and dendritic cells. The paracortex also contains specialised blood vessels called high endothelial venules which allow lymphocytes to enter the node.

(C) uberon-8410067.description: (C): Follicules in the lymph node are surrounded and separated by the interfollicular cortex. Together with the lymph node follicle, the interfollicular cortex of the lymph node lobule make up the superficial cortex of the lymph node. Capillaries empty into the high endothelial venules located in the interfollicular cortex. The interfollicular cortex also serves as transit corriders for lymphocytes migrating between the B and T cell areas.

(C) uberon-8410069.description: (C): Lymphoid tissue found in some birds and similar, but not identical, to mammalian lymph nodes.

(C) uberon-8410070.description: (C): A chest muscle with a role in forceful inspiration. In human, there are twelve levatores costarum on either side of the chest; they are small tendinous and fleshy bundles arising from the ends of the transverse processes of the seventh cervical and upper eleven thoracic vertebrae. They pass obliquely downward and laterally, like the fibers of the intercostales externi, and each is inserted into the outer surface of the rib immediately below the vertebra from which it takes origin, between the tubercle and the angle (levatores costarum breves). Each of the four lower muscles divides into two fasciculi, one of which is inserted as above described; the other passes down to the second rib below its origin (levatores costarum longi).

(C) uberon-8410071.description: (C): The section of the lymph node capsule that faces the subcapsular sinus. In human, it's characterized by specific protein markers.

(C) uberon-8410072.description: (C): The section of the lymph node cortex that faces the subcapsular sinus. In human, it's characterized by specific protein markers.

(C) uberon-8410074.description: (C): A lymph node sinus intimately associated with paracortical cords that originate in the interfollicular cortex and extend into the medullary cords.

(C) uberon-8410075.description: (C): Lymph node paracortical parenchyma containing dense networks of T cells, B cells, fibroblastic reticular cells, and dendritic cells.

(C) uberon-8410076.description: (C): A glomus-like dermal microanatomical structure found in human and placed in front of, or immediately below, the tip of the coccyx. Each glomus consists of one or more arterial segments that branch into a number of glomic arterioles surrounded by rows of round, uniform, epithelioid contractile cells, that drain into a collecting venous plexus.

(C) uberon-8410078.description: (C): A great lymphatic vessel that empties lymph into one of the subclavian veins. In humans, there are two lymph ducts in the body: the right lymphatic duct and the thoracic duct. The right lymphatic duct drains lymph from the right upper limb, right side of thorax and right halves of head and neck. The thoracic duct drains lymph into the circulatory system at the left brachiocephalic vein between the left subclavian and left internal jugular veins.

(C) uberon-8410079.description: (C): Red bone marrow located in an iliac crest.
(C) uberon-8410079.label_original: red bone marrow of iliac crest

(C) uberon-8410080.description: (C): Red bone marrow located in the sternum.

(C) uberon-8420000.description: (C): Hair that grows on the scalp.

(C) uberon-8420001.description: (C): A vein that accompanies an ethmoidal artery and drains the ethmoidal cells.

(C) uberon-8420002.description: (C): An ethmoidal vein that accompanies an anterior ethmoidal artery. The anterior ethmoidal vein normally drains into the inferior root of the superior ophthalmic vein.

(C) uberon-8420003.description: (C): An ethmoidal vein that accompanies a posterior ethmoidal artery. The posterior ethmoidal vein often drains into a venous network under the orbital roof.

(C) uberon-8440000.description: (C): A laminar subdivision of the neocortex that is comprised of a part of layer II and a part of layer III.

(C) uberon-8440001.description: (C): A laminar subdivision of the neocortex that is comprised of a part of layer IV and a part of layer V.

(C) uberon-8440002.description: (C): A laminar subdivision of the neocortex that is comprised of a part of layer V and a part of layer VI.

(C) uberon-8440003.description: (C): The deepest layer of the neocortex. While layer 6b is considered part of layer 6, it is distinct morphologically, genetically, and developmentally from the rest of layer 6. Neurons in L6b project to cortical targets and higher-order thalamus and develop from a precursor population that arises from the subplate.

(C) uberon-8440007.description: (C): The anterior part of the periventricular hypothalamic nucleus.

(C) uberon-8440008.description: (C): The intermediate part of the periventricular hypothalamic nucleus.

(C) uberon-8440010.description: (C): A subdivision of the cytoarchitecturally defined occipital region of cerebral cortex in the human. Defined by the band of Gennari, which gives it the name striate (furrowed) area, it occupies the banks of the calcarine sulcus which are located in the cuneus and the lingual gyrus of the occipital lobe. Cytoarchitecturally it is bounded by the area 18 of Brodmann (human) which surrounds it ( Brodmann-1909 ). In the mouse ( Paxinos-2001 ) and the rat ( Swanson-1998 ) it is located on the dorsolateral surface of the cerebral hemisphere[BrainInfo].

(C) uberon-8440012.description: (C): One of three components of the cerebrum that is a composite structure of the endbrain defined on the basis of origin from the ventricular ridge of the embryonic Encephalon. It consists of the extended striatum and the extended pallidum.

(C) uberon-8440013.description: (C): A small paired band that passes around the splenium of the corpus callosum from the lateral longitudinal stria to the dentate gyrus. The FC exhibits clear anatomical borders with the distalmost region of the CA1.

(C) uberon-8440014.description: (C): A small cluster of neurons situated in the anterior hypothalamus, sitting just above and to the side of the optic chiasm in the brain of humans and other animals.

(C) uberon-8440016.description: (C): A group of cells in the vicinity of the lateral reticular nucleus of the medullary reticular formation that label for norepinephrine in primates.

(C) uberon-8440017.description: (C): A group of cells in the vicinity of the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus nerve in the medulla that label for norepinephrine in primates and rodents.

(C) uberon-8440018.description: (C): A group of cells exhibiting noradrenergic fluorescence that, in the rat, are located in the Tegmen ventriculi quarti (roof of the fourth ventricle) ventral to the cerebellar nuclei, and in the macaque, are found at the edge of the lateral recess of the fourth ventricle caudally, extending to beneath the floor of the ventricle where they merge with the noradrenergic group A6, the locus ceruleus.

(C) uberon-8440019.description: (C): A group of cells in the vicinity of the superior olivary complex in the pontine tegmentum that label for norepinephine in primates, rodents, and other mammals.

(C) uberon-8440021.description: (C): A group of cells fluorescent for norepinephrine that is located in the pontine reticular formation ventral to the superior cerebellar peduncle of the pons in rodents and in primates.

(C) uberon-8440022.description: (C): A group of cells fluorescent for norepinephrine that are scattered in the nucleus subceruleus of the macaque.

(C) uberon-8440023.description: (C): A group of cells fluorescent for norepinephrine that are located in the central gray of the midbrain at the level of the trochlear nucleus in the squirrel monkey (Saimiri) and to a lesser degree in the macaque.

(C) uberon-8440024.description: (C): A cortical area between the agranular insular cortex and the supplemental somatosensory area in rats and mice. The VISC is the architectonically equivalent structure granular insula in humans.

(C) uberon-8440025.description: (C): A small group of cells located lateral to the pyramid of the medulla in the rat and the mouse that functionally it belongs to the reticular formation of the subcortical motor system.

(C) uberon-8440026.description: (C): The part of the parapyramidal nucleus that is closely adjacent to the inner surface of the pyramidal tract.

(C) uberon-8440027.description: (C): The part of the parapyramidal nucleus that is located on the ventral surface of the medulla lateral to the pyramidal tract.

(C) uberon-8440028.description: (C): A group of neurons in the floor of the fourth ventricle, in close proximity to the nucleus of the hypoglossal nerve in the gray substance of the medulla oblongata, all of which contain cells with characteristics suggestive of reticular connections.

(C) uberon-8440029.description: (C): Nerve fibers that originate in the magnocellular red nucleus, cross to the other side of the midbrain, and descend in the lateral part of the brainstem tegmentum in the midbrain, and travel through the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord, coursing adjacent to the lateral corticospinal tract.

(C) uberon-8440030.description: (C): A part of the striatum which is primarilly composed of amygdalar areas. The sAMY is composed of the anterior amygdalar area, central amygdalar nucleus, intercalated amygdalar nucleus, medial amygdalar nucleus, and the bed nucleus of the accessory olfactory tract.

(C) uberon-8440031.description: (C): The main route taken by fibers from the ventral subiculum to the hypothalamus, where they innervate the medial preoptic area, “shell” of the ventromedial nucleus, dorsomedial nucleus, ventral premammillary  nucleus, and cell-poor zone around the medial mammillary nucleus.

(C) uberon-8440032.description: (C): A region in the medial prefrontal cortex that is dorsal to the infralimbic area important in expression of conditioned reward and fear behaviour.

(C) uberon-8440033.description: (C): A region in the medial prefrontal cortex that is ventral to the prelimbic area important in supression of conditioned reward and fear behaviour.

(C) uberon-8440034.description: (C): A subdivision of inferior cerebellar peduncle that connects the medulla to the cerebellum.

(C) uberon-8440035.description: (C): A region in the dorsal pons that plays a central role in inducing motor suppression during REM sleep.

(C) uberon-8440036.description: (C): A premotoneuron pool in the trigeminal reflex arc that is a key structure of jaw movement control.

(C) uberon-8440037.description: (C): A small cluster of neurons dorsal to the facial motor nucleus in the pontine tegmentum.

(C) uberon-8440038.description: (C): A small region of neurons in the brainstem, dorsolateral to the genu of facial nerve, that have efferents to the vestibular periphery.

(C) uberon-8440039.description: (C): The cortical region between the cortical amygdalar area and the piriform area.

(C) uberon-8440040.description: (C): A cytoarchitectonic area on the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere rostral to the septum, ventral to the infralimbic area and dorsal to the tenia tecta in the mouse and rat.

(C) uberon-8440041.description: (C): A hypothalamic region in rodents that is homologous to the lateral tuberal nucleus in humans and higher primates and is involved in energy homeostasis.

(C) uberon-8440042.description: (C): A prominent nucleus located in the ventral tuberal area of Teleostei that is anatomically homologous to the hypothalamic arcuate (infundibular)-median eminence (ME) system of tetrpods.

(C) uberon-8440043.description: (C): A structure embedded in the superior olivary complex that is driven by input pathways from the octopus cells in the cochlear nucleus and the neurons of the medial nucleus of the trapezoid body.

(C) uberon-8440044.description: (C): A laminar subdivision of the neocortex that is comprised of the more surface layers, commonly layers two through four.

(C) uberon-8440045.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that is rostral to area 17, caudal to area 19 and also abuts PPc and area 20a.
(C) uberon-8440045.label_original: second visual cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440046.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret located rostral to area 18 and caudal to area 21.
(C) uberon-8440046.label_original: third visual cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440047.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that is caudal to the suprasylvian visual areas and rostral to area 19.
(C) uberon-8440047.label_original: fourth visual cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440048.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that is posterior to area 20b and lies lateral to areas 17, 18, and 19.
(C) uberon-8440048.label_original: temporal visual area a (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440049.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that is posterior to area PS and anterior to 20a.
(C) uberon-8440049.label_original: temporal visual area b (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [posterior parietal rostral cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440050)
(C) uberon-8440050.description: (C): A multimodal area of the ferret involved in vision and somatosensation that lies between the medial wall of the hemisphere and the medial lip of the suprasylvian sulcus and is posterior to caudal somatosensory cortex (SIII) and anterior to PPc.
(C) uberon-8440050.label_original: posterior parietal rostral cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440051.description: (C): A laminar subdivision of the neocortex that is comprised of the deeper layers, commonly layers five and six, however, could also consist part of layer four.

body: [posterior parietal caudal cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440052)
(C) uberon-8440052.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that  lies between the medial wall of the hemisphere and the medial lip of the suprasylvian sulcus and is posterior to PPr and anterior to area 18 (on the lateral gyrus) and area 21 (on the suprasylvian gyrus).
(C) uberon-8440052.label_original: posterior parietal caudal cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [anteromedial lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440054)
(C) uberon-8440054.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that lies medial to the fundus in the suprasylvian sulcus, posterior to the MRSS and anterior to the PMLS.
(C) uberon-8440054.label_original: anteromedial lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [anterolateral lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440055)
(C) uberon-8440055.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that lies on the lateral bank of the suprasylvian sulcus, posterior to SIII, anterior to area PLLS and medial to A1.
(C) uberon-8440055.label_original: anterolateral lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [posteromedial lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440056)
(C) uberon-8440056.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that is located in the posterior bank of the suprasylvian sulcus.
(C) uberon-8440056.label_original: posteromedial lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [posterolateral lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440059)
(C) uberon-8440059.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret located in the lateral bank of the suprasylvian sulcus posterior to ALLS, anteriomedial to DLS and lateral to PMLS.
(C) uberon-8440059.label_original: posterolateral lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [dorsal lateral suprasylvian visual cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440060)
(C) uberon-8440060.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret located in the lateral bank of the suprasylvian sulcus anterior to VLS and posterior to PLLS.
(C) uberon-8440060.label_original: dorsal lateral suprasylvian visual cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [ventral lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440061)
(C) uberon-8440061.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret located in the medial bank of the suprasylvian sulvus lateral to area PMLS.
(C) uberon-8440061.label_original: ventral lateral suprasylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [posterior suprasylvian visual cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440062)
(C) uberon-8440062.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret that is lateral to the occipital visual areas (area 17, 18, 19 and 21), medial to perirhinal cortex and anterior to area 20b.
(C) uberon-8440062.label_original: posterior suprasylvian visual cortical area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440063.description: (C): A multimodal area in the ferret responsive to visual, somatic, and auditory stimuli. The anterior border of AEV is coincident with the anterior portion of the ectosylvian gyrus containing higher order somatosensory cortical areas and the posterior border abuts higher order auditory cortical areas.
(C) uberon-8440063.label_original: anterior ectosylvian visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440064.description: (C): A visual area in the ferret located on the dorsal bank of the splenial sulcus between the medial border of area 17 and the lateral borter of CVA.
(C) uberon-8440064.label_original: spenial visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440066.description: (C): A visual area of the ferret located in the fundus of the splenial sulcus medial to SVA.
(C) uberon-8440066.label_original: cingulate visual area (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [A lamina of the lateral geniculate nucleus (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440067)
(C) uberon-8440067.description: (C): A major laminae of the lateral geniculate nucleus of the ferret receiving crossed retinal inputs, located medial to the C laminae and lateral to the A1 and P laminae.
(C) uberon-8440067.label_original: A lamina of the lateral geniculate nucleus (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [A1 lamina of the lateral geniculate nucleus (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440068)
(C) uberon-8440068.description: (C): A major laminae of the lateral geniculate nucleus of the ferret receiving uncrossed retinal inputs, located medial to the C and A laminae (Linden, Guillery & Cucchiaro, 1981)
(C) uberon-8440068.label_original: A1 lamina of the lateral geniculate nucleus (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [C lamina of the lateral geniculate nucleus (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440069)
(C) uberon-8440069.description: (C): The most lateral laminae of the LGN of the ferret. The C laminae includes the C lamina, which is the innermost layer, followed by C1, C2, and C3 being the outermost lamina.
(C) uberon-8440069.label_original: C lamina of the lateral geniculate nucleus (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

body: [Perigeniculate lamina of the lateral geniculate nucleus (sensu Mustela putorius furo)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8440070)
(C) uberon-8440070.description: (C): A lamina of the LGN in the ferret located medial to the A lamina in the rostral regions of the visual thalamus ((Linden, Guillery & Cucchiaro, 1981; Dell, Innocenti, Hilgetag, & Manger, 2019).
(C) uberon-8440070.label_original: Perigeniculate lamina of the lateral geniculate nucleus (sensu Mustela putorius furo)

(C) uberon-8440072.description: (C): A nucleus of the brain that is embedded in the pontine tegmentum, it is defined on the basis of inputs from the lateral hypothalamic area and central amygdalar nucleus, it is located ventral to the locus ceruleus, dorsal to Barrington's nucleus, lateral to the laterodorsal tegmental nucleus, and medial to the midbrain trigeminal nucleus.

(C) uberon-8440073.description: (C): A nucleus of the brain that is the most ventral portion of the gigantocellular nucleus in the medullary reticular formation, between the lateral paragigantocellular nucleus and the midline or nucleus raphe magnus. Functionally it belongs to the reticular formation (functional) of the subcortical motor system.

(C) uberon-8440074.description: (C): A cluster of large nerve cells distributed in the vestibular component of vestibulocochlear nerve fibers that functionally belong to the vestibulomotor regions of the behavioral control column.
(C) uberon-8440074.label_original: interstitial nucleus of the vestibular nerve

(C) uberon-8440075.description: (C): The part of the cerebral cortex that is responsible for the perception of taste.

(C) uberon-8440076.description: (C): A part of the cerebral cortex that comprises of the primary motor cortex and the premotor cortex.

(C) uberon-8480016.description: (C): A retroperitoneal space that lies between the anterior and posterior renal fascia; it is a paired inverted cone shaped of tissue containing the kidney, the proximal portion of the collecting system, renal and perirenal vasculature, perirenal lymphatics, adrenal glands and variable amount of fat.

(C) uberon-8480017.description: (C): A space that is bounded anteriorly by the posterior parietal peritoneum, laterally by the lateroconal fascia and posteriorly by the anterior renal fascia; it contains the pancreatic gland, retroperitoneal segments of the duodenum, ascending and descending colon and the mesenteric root, as well as adipose tissue.

(C) uberon-8480018.description: (C): A space that is bound anteriorly by the posterior renal fascia and posteriorly by the transversalis fascia, and it only contains adipose tissue, lymphatics and blood vessels.

(C) uberon-8480019.description: (C): An extraperitoneal space bounded laterally by the perirectal fascia, posteriorly by the posterior pelvic fascia, and anteriorly by the rectovesical fascia in the male and the rectovaginal fascia in the female.

(C) uberon-8480020.description: (C): An extraperitoneal space circumscribed by the umbilicovesical fascia anterior and laterally, and rectovaginal (in females) or rectovesical (in males) septum posteriorly, it encounters the urachus, obliterated umbilical vessels, urinary bladder and the lower uterine segment or seminal vesicles.

(C) uberon-8480021.description: (C): An extraperitoneal space anterior and lateral to the umbilicovesical fascia, and posterior to the trasversalis fascia. (C) uberon-8480022.description: (C): A recess on either side of the laryngeal orifice, which is bounded medially by the aryepiglottic fold, laterally by the thyroid cartilage and thyrohyoid membrane. The pyriform sinus is involved in speech.

(C) uberon-8600019.description: (C): A maternal facing structure of the placental disc, adjacent to the intervillous space. Major components of the placental basal plate include decidua basalis, fibrinoid, connective tissue, extravillous trophoblasts, and residues of degenerating villi and maternal vessels.

(C) uberon-8600020.description: (C): An extension of the basal plate that protrudes into the intervillous space, creating a system of grooves which delimit elevated areas, also known as cotyledons or maternal lobes.

(C) uberon-8600022.description: (C): A septum that surrounds and gives shape to the secondary pulmonary lobules, it is composed of connective tissue within which run the pulmonary veins and lymphatic vessels.

(C) uberon-8600025.description: (C): An anatomical space that separates the basal plate and the chorionic plate. The intervillous space is filled with endometrial gland secretions during early stages of the pregnancy and later perfused with maternal blood, bathing the chorionic villous tree.

(C) uberon-8600026.description: (C): A tree-like structure formed by chorionic villi that sprouts from the chorionic plate in the placental disc. The arborous shape of the chorionic villous tree provides maximal contact area with maternal blood in the intervillous space.

(C) uberon-8600027.description: (C): A chorionic villus that provides structural support to the villous tree. A chorionic stem villus is characterized by a condensed fibrous stroma in which fetal arteries, veins, arterioles, and venules are embedded. It represents a distributing framework for fetal chorionic circulation, supplying the floating villi. It can exhibit a diameter ranging from approximately 3000 μm (trunci near the chorionic plate) to 80 μm (smallest ramuli chorii).

(C) uberon-8600029.description: (C): A bulbous, immature chorionic villus that is formed of loose connective tissue with few fetal vessels. A chorionic immature intermediate villus develops from a chorionic mesenchymal villus, and is the forerunner of a chorionic stem villus.

(C) uberon-8600028.description: (C): The first generation of a tertiary villus that is derived from a syncytial sprout by the invasion of the mesenchyme, in which blood vessels differentiate through vasculogenesis, and gradually transforms into a new immature intermediate villus. A chorionic mesenchymal villus has a thick trophoblastic covering, and cytotrophoblast cells are interposed between syncytium and the trophoblastic basal lamina over 50–100% of the surface. The stroma is characterized by loosely arranged collagen fibers that enmesh mesenchymal and some villous macrophages. The fetal capillaries are poorly developed.

(C) uberon-8600030.description: (C): The most distal part of a chorionic villus. A chorionic terminal villus is a grape-like structure characterized by a high degree of capillarization and highly dilated sinusoids. A terminal villus has less stroma and a discontinuous cytotrophoblast layer, and contains 4–6 fetal capillaries per cross section. It exhibits a diameter ranging from 40 to about 80 μm.

(C) uberon-8600032.description: (C): A chorionic villus that is not attached to the placental basal plate and it is immersed in maternal blood.

(C) uberon-8600031.description: (C): A slender branch of a chorionic stem villus. A chorionic mature intermediate villus lacks fetal arterioles and venules in the stroma, which is composed of slender fetal capillaries embedded into a loose connective tissue that is rich in cells but poor in fibers. It exhibits a diameter ranging from 60 to about 100 μm.

(C) uberon-8600033.description: (C): A distal smaller chorionic stem villus that is connected to the maternal side of the placenta (in early gestational stages to the decidua, and later to the developing basal plate) via a cytotrophoblast cell column. A chorionic anchoring villus stabilizes the position of the villous tree in the maternal intervillous bloodstream.

(C) uberon-8600034.description: (C): A lamina propria that is part of a jejunum.

(C) uberon-8600035.description: (C): A lamina propria that is part of an ileum.

(C) uberon-8600041.description: (C): A capillary that is part of a chorionic terminal villus. This capillary is generally narrow, but displays sinusoidal dilations along its length, often at the points of acute bends. These dilations bring the capillary endothelium into close contact with the overlying syncytiotrophoblast to form a vasculosyncytial membrane.

(C) uberon-8600045.description: (C): A lateral wall of the urinary bladder that is located on the right side.
(C) uberon-8600045.label_original: right lateral wall of urinary bladder

(C) uberon-8600046.description: (C): The most anterior wall of the urinary bladder.

(C) uberon-8600047.description: (C): The most posterior wall of the urinary bladder.

(C) uberon-8600049.description: (C): The anterosuperior surface of the urinary bladder, with boundaries at the apex and fundus of the urinary bladder.

(C) uberon-8600050.description: (C): An accumulation of extravillous trophoblast cells at the tip of a floating villus or occasionally attached to the chorionic plate embedded in fibrin.

(C) uberon-8600051.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the main pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a segment of the lung.

(C) uberon-8600052.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the segmental pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a subsegment of the lung.

(C) uberon-8600053.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the azygos vein and drains blood from the esophagus.

(C) uberon-8600054.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the superior intercostal vein and drains the first intercostal space.

(C) uberon-8600055.description: (C): An artery that branches from the right coronary artery and supplies the atrioventricular node.

(C) uberon-8600056.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein and drains the anterior surface of the sacrum.

(C) uberon-8600057.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein.

(C) uberon-8600058.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein and drains the uterus.

(C) uberon-8600059.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of a vertebral vein and drains the suboccipital region, adjacent vertebral column, and deep muscles of the neck.

(C) uberon-8600060.description: (C): An artery that is a branch of the segmental pulmonary artery and supplies deoxyge blood to a smaller subsegment of the lung.

(C) uberon-8600061.description: (C): A venule that receives drainage from the capillary beds after blood has perfused the pulmonary alveoli, and is tributary of the pulmonary venules.

(C) uberon-8600062.description: (C): An artery that branches from the subclavian artery and supplies the thyroid gland, neck, and upper back regions.

(C) uberon-8600063.description: (C): An artery that branches from the left anterior descending artery and supplies the interventricular septum of the heart.

(C) uberon-8600102.description: (C): An artery that branches from the left coronary artery and supplies the anterior wall of the left ventricle, the interventricular septum, and the apex of the heart.

(C) uberon-8600064.description: (C): An artery that branches from the right coronary artery or the circumflex artery and supplies the posterior and lateral walls of the left ventricle.

(C) uberon-8600103.description: (C): A venous plexus that is tributary of the basivertebral veins and internal vertebral veins, draining blood from the vertebrae and spinal cord. The anterior internal vertebral venous plexus is located within the vertebral canal.

(C) uberon-8600065.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the femoral vein and drains blood from the front and middle areas of the thigh.

(C) uberon-8600066.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the anterior internal vertebral venous plexus and drains blood from the vertebral bodies.

(C) uberon-8600067.description: (C): A venule that is tributary of the bronchial veins and drains blood from the bronchi and bronchioles of the lungs.

(C) uberon-8600068.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the facial vein and drains blood from the chin and lower lip.

(C) uberon-8600069.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the lingual vein and drains blood from the tongue.

(C) uberon-8600070.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the lingual vein and drains blood from the dorsum of the tongue, and the sides of the tongue.

(C) uberon-8600071.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the lingual vein and drains blood from the ventral (inferior) surface of the tongue and the sublingual glands.

(C) uberon-8600072.description: (C): A venous plexus tha connects the middle and superior thyroid veins.

(C) uberon-8600073.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the axillary vein and drains blood from the region around the neck of the humerus.

(C) uberon-8600074.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the axillary vein and drains blood from the thoracoacromial region, including the pectoral, shoulder, and clavicular regions.

(C) uberon-8600075.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the external jugular vein and drains blood from the superficial muscles of the back, mainly the trapezius muscle.

(C) uberon-8600076.description: (C): A venous plexus that is tributary of the deep cervical veins and drains blood from the suboccipital region.

(C) uberon-8600077.description: (C): An arteriole that branches from the pulmonary arteries and supplies deoxygenated blood to the pulmonary capillaries and alveolar capillaries of the lungs.

(C) uberon-8600078.description: (C): An artery of the neck that branches from the external carotid artery and supplies the pharynx.

(C) uberon-8600079.description: (C): An artery that branches from the internal carotid artery and supplies the anterior clinoid process of the dura mater.

(C) uberon-8600080.description: (C): An artery that branches from the descending thoracic aorta and supplies the dorsal portion of the pericardium.

(C) uberon-8600081.description: (C): An artery that branches from the internal thoracic artery and supplies the pericardium and the diaphragm.

(C) uberon-8600082.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the great saphenous vein and drains blood from the inguinal region and the anterior abdominal wall.

(C) uberon-8600083.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the posterior tibial vein and drains blood from the lateral compartment of the leg.

(C) uberon-8600084.description: (C): A venule that is tributary of the prostatic venous plexus and drains blood from the prostate gland.

(C) uberon-8600085.description: (C): A venule that branches from the hepatic portal vein to transport nutrient-rich blood from the gastrointestinal tract and spleen to supply the liver. The hepatic portal venule is tributary of the hepatic sinusoids.

(C) uberon-8600086.description: (C): An artery that branches from the inferior alveolar artery and supplies the roots and pulp of the teeth of the lower jaw. It forms anastomoses with its contralateral partner.

(C) uberon-8600087.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the angular vein and drains blood from the superficial tissues and skin of the dorsum (bridge) and ala (wings) of the nose.

(C) uberon-8600088.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the angular vein and drains blood from the muscles and skin of the forehead.

(C) uberon-8600089.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the angular veins and drains blood from the bridge of the nose.

(C) uberon-8600090.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the cavernous sinus and drains blood from the pituitary gland.

(C) uberon-8600091.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the transverse sinus and drains blood from the adjacent cortical regions of the temporal lobe. The inferior anastomotic vein forms an anastomosis (connection) between the superficial middle cerebral vein anteriorly and the transverse sinus posteriorly.

(C) uberon-8600092.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the brachial vein and drains blood from the lateral structures of the forearm, carpal and metacarpal bones, joints of the hand, and lateral forearm muscles.

(C) uberon-8600093.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the brachial vein and drains blood from the hand and medial and posterior aspect of forearm.

(C) uberon-8600094.description: (C): An arteriole that branches from the pulmonary arteriole and supplies deoxygenated blood to the pulmonary capillaries in the alveoli of the lungs.

(C) uberon-8600095.description: (C): An artery that branches from the facial artery, and branches to supply the soft palate and the palatine tonsil.

(C) uberon-8600096.description: (C): An artery that branches from the facial artery that runs forward under the mouth, then turns upward upon reaching the chin.

(C) uberon-8600097.description: (C): An artery that branches from the lingual artery and supplies blood to the tongue itself, particularly the body and tip of the tongue. The deep lingual artery travels superiorly in a tortuous course along the under (ventral) surface of the tongue, below the longitudinalis inferior, and above the mucous membrane.

(C) uberon-8600098.description: (C): An artery that branches from the lingual artery and supplies the soft palate, tonsils, epiglottis, palatoglossal arch, and adjacent mucous membrane. The dorsal lingual artery runs along the upper border of the hyoid bone and anastomises with its fellow of the opposite side.

(C) uberon-8600099.description: (C): An artery that branches from the maxillary artery and supplies the meninges. The accessory meningeal artery ascends through the foramen ovale to enter the cranial cavity and supply the dura mater of the floor of the middle cranial fossa and of the trigeminal cave, and to the trigeminal ganglion.

(C) uberon-8600100.description: (C): An artery that branches from the maxillary artery and supplies blood to structures in the auditory tube, tympanic cavity, and upper pharynx. The artery of the pterygoid canal courses through the pterygoid canal, a small bony canal located in the sphenoid bone of the skull.

(C) uberon-8600101.description: (C): An artery that branches from the maxillary artery and supplies the hard and soft palate.

(C) uberon-8600104.description: (C): A vein that drains blood from the vertebral column and intervertebral discs. In the neck, it is tributary of into the vertebral veins. In the thorax, it is tributary of the posterior intercostal veins. In the lumbar and sacral regions, it is tributary of the lumbar and lateral sacral veins

(C) uberon-8600105.description: (C): A vein that is tributary of the inferior vena cava and drains blood from the posterior abdominal wall and lumbar region.

(C) uberon-8600106.description: (C): An artery that branches from the axilliary artery and supplies the deltoid, biceps brachii, and coracobrachialis muscles, the glenohumeral joint, the proximal humeral head, and the skin overlying the anterior aspect of the proximal humerus. This artery courses laterally across the anterior surface of the humerus and anastomoses with the posterior humeral circumflex artery.

(C) uberon-8600107.description: (C): An artery that branches from the axilliary artery and supplies the deltoid, teres major, teres minor, and long and lateral heads of the triceps brachii muscles, glenohumeral joint, and the cutaneous supply to the area posterolateral to the proximal humerus. This artery courses posteriorly with the axillary nerve, through the quadrangular space, to the posterior aspect of the humerus and anastomoses with the anterior humeral circumflex artery.

(C) uberon-8600108.description: (C): A segment of the ureter that extends from the renal pelvis to the common iliac artery bifurcation (to form the internal and external iliac arteries).

(C) uberon-8600109.description: (C): A segment of the ureter that extends from the common iliac artery bifurcation to the bladder. From there, the ureter curves back and follows the lateral pelvic wall inferiorly to connect with the posterolateral bladder wall.

(C) uberon-8600110.description: (C): The terminal segment of the ureter that is continuous with the distal ureter, lies where the ureter enters the bladder and extends within the bladder wall. The intramural ureter is aperistaltic, serving as a reflux-preventing mechanism, preventing the backflow of urine from the bladder into the ureters.

(C) uberon-8600111.description: (C): A distal ureter that is part of the right ureter.

(C) uberon-8600113.description: (C): A proximal ureter that is part of the right ureter.

(C) uberon-8600115.description: (C): An intramural ureter that is part of the right ureter.

(C) uberon-8600112.description: (C): A distal ureter that is part of the left ureter.

(C) uberon-8600114.description: (C): A proximal ureter that is part of the left ureter.

(C) uberon-8600116.description: (C): An intramural ureter that is part of the left ureter.

(C) uberon-8600117.description: (C): A posterior free border of a mesosalpinx.

(C) uberon-8600118.description: (C): A ganglion that is part of a myenteric plexus. The myoenteric ganglion serves as a control center for local gut functions, such as motility.

(C) uberon-8600119.description: (C): A myenteric ganglion located in the myenteric plexus of the small intestine.

(C) uberon-8600120.description: (C): A ganglion that is part of the atrial region of the heart. The activation of efferent neurons in this ganglion results in the modulation of heart rate, atrio-ventricular node conduction, and inotropism of atria and ventricles.

(C) uberon-8600121.description: (C): A ganglion that is part of the lumbar portion of the sympathetic trunk. The neurons in a lumbar ganglion are postganglionic sympathetic neurons that synapse with axons from preganglionic sympathetic neurons.

(C) uberon-8600122.description: (C): A ganglion that is part of the sacral portion of the sympathetic trunk. A sacral ganglion consists of postganglionic sympathetic neurons that receive presynaptic input from preganglionic sympathetic axons descending through the sympathetic trunk from thoracolumbar levels.

(C) uberon-8600124.description: (C): A simple columnar epithelium that is part of the fallopian tube.

(C) uberon-8600125.description: (C): The superior region of the fallopian tube epithelium.

(C) uberon-8600126.description: (C): The inferior region of the fallopian tube epithelium.

(C) uberon-8600127.description: (C): The most proximal region to the mesosalpinx of the fallopian tube epithelium.

(C) uberon-8600128.description: (C): The most proximal region to the antimesosalpinx of the fallopian tube epithelium.

(C) uberon-8600129.description: (C): A transient, mesoderm-derived structure in the ovary that forms immediately after the rupture of a mature ovarian follicle during ovulation. It is formed by bleeding of small blood vessels in the follicle wall as the follicle collapses, resulting in a blood-filled center that rapidly clots. This structure develops into the corpus luteum.

(C) uberon-8600130.description: (C): The most superior region of the muscularis layer of the fallopian tube.
(C) uberon-8600130.label_original: superior muscular layer of fallopian tube

(C) uberon-8600131.description: (C): The most inferior region of the muscularis layer of the fallopian tube.
(C) uberon-8600131.label_original: inferior muscular layer of fallopian tube

(C) uberon-8600132.description: (C): The most proximal region to the mesosalpinx of the muscularis layer of the fallopian tube.
(C) uberon-8600132.label_original: mesosalpinx-proximal muscular layer of fallopian tube

(C) uberon-8600133.description: (C): The most proximal region to the antimesosalpinx of the muscularis layer of the fallopian tube.
(C) uberon-8600133.label_original: antimesosalpinx-proximal muscular layer of fallopian tube

(C) uberon-8600134.description: (C): The lamina propria that underlies the epithelial lining of the ascending colon.

(C) uberon-8600135.description: (C): The lamina propria that underlies the epithelial lining of the descending colon.

(C) uberon-8600136.description: (C): The lamina propria that underlies the epithelial lining of the sigmoid colon.

(C) uberon-8600137.description: (C): The lamina propria that underlies the epithelial lining of the transverse colon.

(C) uberon-8600139.description: (C): The lamina propria that underlies the epithelial lining of the caecum.

(C) uberon-8600140.description: (C): The lamina propria that underlies the epithelial lining of the rectum.

(C) uberon-8600141.description: (C): A tooth surface structure that is oriented away from the median plane of the dental arch or oral cavity.

(C) uberon-8600148.description: (C): A surface structure that is part of a calcareous tooth.

(C) uberon-8600142.description: (C): A tooth surface structure that forms the cutting edge of an incisor or canine tooth. It functions to shear or incise food during biting.

(C) uberon-8600143.description: (C): A tooth surface structure that faces the lips.

(C) uberon-8600147.description: (C): A tooth surface structure that is oriented toward the lips or cheeks.

(C) uberon-8600144.description: (C): A tooth surface structure that faces the tongue or its anatomical equivalent.

(C) uberon-8600145.description: (C): A tooth surface structure that is oriented toward the median plane of the dental arch.

(C) uberon-8600146.description: (C): A tooth surface structure that is oriented toward the buccal mucosa (i.e., the inner lining of the cheek).

(C) uberon-8600149.description: (C): A tooth surface structure that forms the chewing edge of premolar or molar tooth. It functions to chew or grind food during biting.

(C) uberon-8700000.description: (C): A transient organ in the developing embryo composed of the dorsal aorta, developing gonads, and embryonic kidney. This structure is located in the embryonic mesoderm and serves as the primary site for the generation of definitive hematopoietic stem cells.

(C) uberon-8700001.description: (C): A specialized epithelial layer overlying the luminal surface of lymphoid follicles in gut-associated lymphoid tissue. It is found in Peyer's patches of the small intestine and appendix in humans and in the intestine and caecal patches in mice. This layer contains specialised M cells and has fewer goblet cells compared to surrounding tissue. This layer plays a crucial role in mucosal immune surveillance.

(C) uberon-8700002.description: (C): The second deepest layer of the stratified squamous epithelium lining the esophagus, positioned directly above the stratum basale. It consists of multiple layers of keratinocytes connected by strong intercellular junctions called desmosomes, giving the cells a characteristic 'spiny' appearance. This layer provides structural support, contributes to the epithelial barrier function, and serves as a transitional zone for keratinocytes migrating towards the luminal surface, playing a crucial role in maintaining the integrity and protective properties of the esophageal lining.

(C) uberon-8850000.description: (C): An anatomical cavity that is part of the alveolus of the lung

(C) uberon-8910001.description: (C): The stomatogastric ganglion (STG) consists of about 30 neurons that form two central pattern generator circuits in crustaceans. STG neurons have large soma (~50-100 um) and have complex branches. The STG contains the motor neurons that innervate the striated muscles that move the gastric mill and pyloric regions of the stomach.

(C) uberon-8910010.description: (C): The stomatogastric nerve (SGN) is made up of four separate nerves that emerge from the paired commissural ganglia, the superior and inferior esophageal nerves (SONs and IONs).

(C) uberon-8910011.description: (C): Nerve carrying dorsal gastric (DG) neurons which control the medial tooth movements in crustaceans.

(C) uberon-8910012.description: (C): Consists of gastropyloric receptor (GPR) neurons, which are stretch receptors that innervate stomach muscles in crustaceans.

(C) uberon-8910013.description: (C): Consists of lateral gastric (LG) neurons. The alternation between the lateral gastric neurons/medial gastric neurons and the lateral posterior gastric neurons control the movements of the lateral teeth in crustaceans.

(C) uberon-8910014.description: (C): The motor axons that project into the dorsal ventricular nerve bifurcate and then project into both lateral ventricular nerves.

(C) uberon-8910015.description: (C): Innervates pyloric region of the stomach.

(C) uberon-8910016.description: (C): Innervates muscles that dilate valves of the pylorus motor neurons involved in filtering in crustaceans. Anterior burster neurons are intrinsic oscillators that are electrically coupled with pyloric dilator neurons, causing them to fire bursts of action potentials. Together these neurons inhibit lateral pyloric and pyloric neurons, forcing them to fire in alternation with the pyloric dilator neurons.

(C) uberon-8910017.description: (C): The inferior esophageal nerve (ION) is one of the four nerves that make up the stomatogastric nerve (SGN).

(C) uberon-8910018.description: (C): The superior esophageal nerve (SON) is one of the four nerves that make up the stomatogastric nerve (SGN).

(C) uberon-8910020.description: (C): Neurons with cell bodies in the esophageal ganglion turn on the gastric mill rhythm and strongly affects the pyloric rhythm.

(C) uberon-8910021.description: (C): Contains motor fibers that innervate the esophagus. Stimulating the pyloric suppressor neuron alters both pyloric and gastric rhythms but also elicits activity in a third oscillatory circuit located in the commissural ganglia called the esophageal rhythm.

body: [junction of superior esophageal nerve and stomatogastric nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_8910022)
(C) uberon-8910022.description: (C): The junction between the stomatogastric nerve (STN) and the superior esophageal nerve (SON) shows synaptic structures. Octopamine may be released at this site by projection neurons; its application at this junction induces action potentials in the axons of the modulatory commissural neuron 5 (MCN5) that project from the commissural ganglia to the stomatogastric ganglion (STG).
(C) uberon-8910022.label_original: junction of superior esophageal nerve and stomatogastric nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)

(C) uberon-8910023.description: (C): Most of the efferent fibers leaving the stomatogastric ganglion and leading to the gastric mill or pyloric stomach muscles run posteriorly in the dorsal median ventricular nerve. This nerve branches bilaterally into the right and left lateral ventricular nerves (LVN) which go to their respective sides of the stomach.

(C) uberon-8910024.description: (C): A region of squamous epithelium found in the tracheobronchial tree - continuous with the tracheobronchial epithelium.

(C) uberon-8920000.description: (C): An artery that branches from the ophthalmic artery and supplies the anterior segment of the eyeball and ciliary body.

(C) uberon-8920001.description: (C): An artery that branches from the ophthalmic artery and supplies the choroid and ciliary processes.

(C) uberon-8920002.description: (C): An artery that branches from the ophthalmic artery and supplies the choroid, ciliary body and iris.

(C) uberon-8920003.description: (C): An artery that is a branch of the right coronary artery. It follows the acute margin of the heart supplying blood to the right ventricle.

(C) uberon-8920004.description: (C): An artery that branches from the renal artery. The anterior division of the renal artery typically divides into four segmental arteries, whereas the posterior division of the renal artery supplies one segmental artery.

(C) uberon-8920005.description: (C): A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, superiorly and laterally. It supplies the superior (apical) lobe of the kidney.

(C) uberon-8920006.description: (C): A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, superiorly and laterally towards the superior pole of the kidney. It does not ascend as steeply as the superior segmental artery and does not extend into the superior pole. It supplies the anterosuperior lobe of the kidney, which includes the central anterosuperior region, extending to the lateral aspect and slightly onto the posterior surface of the kidney.

(C) uberon-8920007.description: (C): A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, laterally and angled slightly inferiorly. It supplies the anteroinferior lobe of the kidney, which includes the central anteroinferior region, extending to the lateral aspect and slightly onto the posterior surface of the kidney.

(C) uberon-8920008.description: (C): A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, inferiorly and laterally towards the inferior pole of the kidney. It supplies the inferior lobe of the kidney, which encompasses the whole of the inferior pole of the kidney, including the anterior and posterior surfaces.

(C) uberon-8920009.description: (C): A segmental renal artery that passes posterior to the renal pelvis and travels laterally, more or less horizontally. It supplies the posterior lobe of the kidney, which includes all of the central-posterior surface of the kidney. This excludes the superior and inferior poles and a small posterolateral portion.

(C) uberon-8920010.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the great cardiac vein (left coronary vein) and drains blood from the left ventricle of the heart. It courses with the left marginal artery as it travels superiorly along the left cardiac border.

(C) uberon-8920011.description: (C): A vein that drains blood from the most superficial zones of the renal cortex. Groups of stellate veins are arranged in a star-like pattern, converging centrally to drain into an interlobular vein.

(C) uberon-8920012.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the renal vein and drains blood from a segment of the kidney.

(C) uberon-8920013.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the superior ophthalmic vein and drains blood from the ciliary body of the eye.

(C) uberon-8920014.description: (C): A bronchial vein that drains blood from the bronchi into the accessory hemiazygos vein or the left superior intercostal vein.

(C) uberon-8920015.description: (C): A bronchial vein that drains blood from the bronchi into the azygos vein.

(C) uberon-8920016.description: (C): A pulmonary vein that drains blood from the inferior lobe of the right lung.

(C) uberon-8920017.description: (C): A pulmonary vein that drains blood from the inferior lobe of the left lung.

(C) uberon-8920018.description: (C): A pulmonary vein that drains blood from the superior and middle lobes of the right lung.

(C) uberon-8920019.description: (C): A pulmonary vein that drains blood from the superior lobe and lingula of the left lung.

(C) uberon-8920020.description: (C): An artery that branches from the splenic artery and supplies the head, uncinate process, neck, body and tail of the pancreas. It anastamoses with the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

(C) uberon-8920021.description: (C): An artery that branches from the splenic artery and supplies the left half of the body and tail of the pancreas.

(C) uberon-8920022.description: (C): An artery that branches from the splenic artery and supplies the tail of the pancreas.

(C) uberon-8920023.description: (C): An artery that branches from the dorsal pancreatic artery and supplies the body and tail of the pancreas. It is also known as the inferior pancreatic artery.

(C) uberon-8920024.description: (C): An artery that branches from the gastroduodenal artery and supplies the first and second parts (superior and descending parts) of the duodenum and the head of the pancreas.

(C) uberon-8920025.description: (C): An artery that branches from the gastroduodenal artery and supplies the first and second parts of the duodenum, distal common bile duct and head of the pancreas.

(C) uberon-8920026.description: (C): An artery that branches from the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery. It courses on the anterior surface of the uncinate process continuing on to the head of the pancreas. It supplies the uncinate process, head of the pancreas, and the second and third parts of the duodenum.

(C) uberon-8920027.description: (C): An artery that branches from the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery. It courses posterior to the uncinate process and head of the pancreas. It supplies uncinate process and head of the pancreas, second and third parts of the duodenum.

(C) uberon-8920028.description: (C): A vein that joins the gastrocolic trunk, draining into the superior mesenteric vein. It drains the ventral surface of the distal first and second portion of the duodenum and the ventral surface of the pancreatic head.

(C) uberon-8920029.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the hepatic portal vein. It drains the dorsal surface of the distal first and second portion of the duodenum and the dorsal surface of the pancreatic head.

(C) uberon-8920030.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein. It drains the ventral surface of the second and third portion of the duodenum and the ventral surface of the head and uncinate process of the pancreas.

(C) uberon-8920031.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein. It drains the dorsal surface of the second and third portion of the duodenum and the dorsal surface of the head and uncinate process of the pancreas.

(C) uberon-8920032.description: (C): An artery that branches from the ileocolic artery and supplies the anterior portion of the cecum.

(C) uberon-8920033.description: (C): An artery that branches from the ileocolic artery and supplies the posterior portion of the cecum.

(C) uberon-8920034.description: (C): An artery that branches from the ileocolic artery and supplies the cecum and inferior portion of the ascending colon.

(C) uberon-8920035.description: (C): An arterial arcade that connects the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries and supplies the colon.

(C) uberon-8920036.description: (C): An artery that branches from the left colic artery and supplies the superior portion of the descending colon, the left colic flexure, and the right one half to one third of the transverse colon.
(C) uberon-8920036.label_original: ascending branch of left colic artery

(C) uberon-8920037.description: (C): An artery that branches from the left colic artery and supplies the inferior portion of the descending colon.
(C) uberon-8920037.label_original: descending branch of left colic artery

(C) uberon-8920038.description: (C): An artery that is a collateral pathway linking the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries and supplies the colon.

(C) uberon-8920039.description: (C): An artery that branches from the left hepatic artery and supplies the medial portion of the caudate lobe of the liver.

(C) uberon-8920040.description: (C): An artery that branches from the right hepatic artery and supplies the lateral portion of the caudate lobe of the liver.

(C) uberon-8920041.description: (C): An artery that branches from the ulnar artery and supplies the medial aspect of the forearm, medial aspect of the wrist, and to the region surrounding the hypothenar eminence.

(C) uberon-8920042.description: (C): An artery that branches from the ileocolic artery and supplies the distal most ileum, ileocecal junction, cecum and appendix.

(C) uberon-8920043.description: (C): An artery that branches from the gastroduodenal artery and supplies the posterior surface of the proximal duodenum.

(C) uberon-8920044.description: (C): An artery that branches from the gastroduodenal artery and supplies the superior, right, and anterior surfaces of the first part of the duodenum, extending into the second part.

(C) uberon-8920045.description: (C): An artery that branches from the proper hepatic artery and supplies the right side of the lesser curvature of the stomach and adjacent anterior and posterior surfaces.

(C) uberon-8920046.description: (C): An artery that branches from the splenic artery and supplies the fundus of the stomach on the side of the greater curvature of the stomach.

(C) uberon-8920047.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the splenic vein and drains the anterior and posterior body of the stomach and greater omentum.

(C) uberon-8920048.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein and drains the greater omentum and distal body and antrum of the stomach.

(C) uberon-8920049.description: (C): An artery that branches from the splenic artery at the splenic hilum at which it divides into one or two terminal branches supplying a lobe of the spleen.

(C) uberon-8920050.description: (C): An artery that branches from the left gastric artery and supplies the abdominal esophagus.
(C) uberon-8920050.label_original: esophageal branches of left gastric artery

(C) uberon-8920051.description: (C): An artery that branches from the internal pudendal artery and supplies the scrotum.

(C) uberon-8920052.description: (C): An artery that branches from the internal iliac artery and supplies the lower vagina and fundus of the bladder.

(C) uberon-8920053.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the inferior mesenteric vein and drains the upper two thirds of the rectum and upper anal canal.

(C) uberon-8920054.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the internal pudendal vein and drains the lower third of the rectum and anal canal.

(C) uberon-8920055.description: (C): A vein that is a tributary of the internal pudendal vein and drains the skin and fascial layers of the posterior scrotum.
